name: Citrus Sunrise Highball
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice. Add 2 oz (60 ml) zero-proof tequila and 3 oz (90 ml) orange juice, then stir gently.
Pour 1 oz (30 ml) lemonade over the top.
Add 1/2 oz (15 ml) grenadine; it sinks to the bottom and makes the layered sunrise effect.
Garnish with an orange slice and a maraschino cherry, add a straw and serve.
verified_note: Closest published match to a citrus sunrise highball (no recipe by this exact name found). Lemonade mapped to lemon_lime_soda as the closest id. Zero-proof tequila (60 ml) has no id and is listed as unmapped; it can be dropped or replaced with extra juice. Not included: zero-proof tequila alternative (e.g. Ritual or Seedlip Grove 42), 60 ml

name: Electric Blue Lagoon Sparkler
steps: Fill a large glass with ice.
Pour in 1 oz (30 ml) non-alcoholic blue curacao syrup and 1 oz (30 ml) alcohol-free vodka (or lemon juice or orange juice instead).
Slowly top with 1 cup (240 ml) lemonade.
Stir gently, garnish with fruit or flowers, and serve.
verified_note: No recipe by the exact name; Blue Lagoon Mocktail is the same drink. Lemon juice used as the page's allowed substitute for alcohol-free vodka. Lemonade (240 ml) mapped to lemon_lime_soda as the closest id. Page says hurricane or tulip glass, highball also works.

name: Sparkling Berry Sangria Punch
steps: In a pitcher, whisk together 60 ml cranberry juice, 30 ml orange juice, 60 ml pineapple juice and the juice of about 1/8 of a lemon and 1/8 of a lime (about 7 ml each). For a party, the page makes 8 servings in one large pitcher.
Slice a little of the remaining lemon and lime, cut a small piece of orange and Granny Smith apple into bite-sized chunks, and slice 1 strawberry.
Add the sliced fruit, 2 tbsp blueberries and 2 mint leaves to the pitcher, stir, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, add 120 ml sparkling water (or lemon-lime soda).
Scoop some of the fruit into a punch cup and pour the liquid over it, leaving room for more fizz.
verified_note: Page makes 8 (2 cups cranberry juice, 1 cup orange juice, 2 cups pineapple juice, 2 limes, 2 lemons, 1 orange, 1 Granny Smith apple, 1/2 pint strawberries, 1 cup blueberries, 1/2 cup mint, 4 cups sparkling water); divided by 8. Blueberries mapped to berries. Page does not say to serve over ice.

name: Passionfruit Mint Sparkler
steps: Make the syrup: add 50 ml water, 27 g sugar and a few mint leaves (about half of the mint for one drink) to a pan. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 3 minutes, stirring now and then. Remove from the heat.
Halve 1 passion fruit and scrape the pulp, seeds and juice into the pan. Let it cool completely.
Strain through a sieve, pressing out as much liquid as possible, and discard the cooked mint. Stir half of the passion fruit seeds and a little lime zest into the syrup, then chill.
To serve, put the syrup and the remaining fresh mint leaves in a tumbler, top with ice and sparkling water, and serve immediately.
verified_note: Page makes 6 (160 g sugar, 300 ml water, 25 g mint, 6 passion fruit, 1 lime zest); divided by 6. Syrup (about 50 ml water plus 27 g sugar) mapped to simple_syrup:50; the passion fruit pulp is cooked into it. Mint and sparkling water amounts per drink are not given: 5 leaves and 100 ml are estimates. Page has no lime juice or agave.

name: Pomegranate Rose Spritz
steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Add 120 ml (1/2 cup) pomegranate juice and 1/4 tsp rosewater.
Add a squeeze of lime and top with club soda to taste.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and lime if desired.
verified_note: Page gives no amount for the lime squeeze (5 ml estimated) or the club soda (to taste; 100 ml estimated). Page does not name a glass.

name: Tart Cherry Limeade Fizz
steps: Fill a lowball or rocks glass with ice.
Add 30 ml (1 oz) cherry simple syrup and 30 ml (1 oz) fresh-squeezed lime juice to the glass.
Top with 120 to 180 ml (4 to 6 oz) lime sparkling water and stir to combine.
If you like, garnish with a lime slice and a cherry.
verified_note: Page uses cherry simple syrup (not tart cherry juice); mapped to cherry_juice. Lime sparkling water mapped to soda_water; used 150 ml, midpoint of 4-6 oz.

name: Grapefruit Rosemary Spritz
steps: Make the rosemary syrup (enough for about 4 drinks): put 1 cup fresh rosemary, 1 cup water and 1 cup sweetener in a small saucepan and stir to dissolve the sweetener.
Keep it at a very light boil, barely bubbling, for 5 minutes. Remove from heat, cover and steep for 30 minutes, then set aside to cool.
For one drink, add 1/4 cup (60 ml) freshly squeezed grapefruit juice and 1/8 cup (30 ml) rosemary syrup to an ice-filled glass.
Top with about 1/2 cup (120 ml) sparkling water and finish with a pinch of sea salt (optional).
Garnish and serve.
verified_note: Rosemary syrup mapped to simple_syrup. Page lists 2 cups sparkling water for the batch, divided by 4 drinks gives 120 ml (assumed split). Page ingredient list says 120 ml grapefruit juice but the method uses 1/4 cup (60 ml) per drink; method used. Salt mapped to black_salt (sea salt). Glass type not specified.

name: Zero-Proof Paloma
steps: Notch a grapefruit wedge, run it around the rim of the glass, and dip the rim in a plate of flaky sea salt and tajin.
Add 30 ml (1 oz) lime juice, 60 ml (2 oz) fresh grapefruit juice, 1/4 tsp honey (or simple syrup) and 1/4 tsp pickle brine to the glass. Stir until the honey dissolves.
Fill the glass with ice, top with 90 ml (3 oz) tonic water (or grapefruit soda) and serve immediately.
garnish: grapefruit wedge, flaky sea salt and tajin rim
verified_note: Page uses tonic water (or grapefruit soda), not plain soda; mapped to tonic. Honey used as listed (simple syrup is the alternative). Salt/tajin rim kept as garnish only. Not included: pickle brine 0.25tsp

name: Shirley Temple
steps: Pour lemon juice, grenadine and ginger ale into a chilled glass
Fill the glass with ice
Garnish with a lemon wheel and a maraschino cherry

name: Roy Rogers
steps: Fill a glass with ice and pour in the cola
Add a splash of grenadine and stir gently
Garnish with a maraschino cherry

name: Sparkling Cranberry Mocktail
steps: Rinse 1 tbsp fresh cranberries and 1 sprig of rosemary.
Pour 80 ml (1/3 cup) cranberry juice and 355 ml (1 1/2 cups) cranberry Sprite into a 15.5 oz highball or Collins glass, then stir gently.
Garnish with 1 tbsp crushed ice, the fresh cranberries and the rosemary sprig. Serve immediately.
verified_note: Cranberry Sprite mapped to lemon_lime_soda (closest id). Fresh cranberries (garnish) mapped to berries.

name: Sparkling Pomegranate Mocktail
steps: Fill a highball glass about halfway with ice.
In a cocktail shaker or jug, gently stir together 60 ml (1/4 cup) 100% pomegranate juice, 1 to 1 1/2 tbsp fresh orange juice and the juice of 1/2 lime.
Pour into the glass and slowly top with 120 ml (1/2 cup) sparkling water.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds, a lime wheel and a rosemary sprig. Serve immediately.
garnish: pomegranate seeds, lime wheel, rosemary sprig
verified_note: Page makes 2 (1/2 cup pomegranate juice, 2-3 tbsp orange juice, juice of 1 lime, 1 cup sparkling water, lemon-lime soda or ginger ale); divided by 2. Lime juice of 1/2 lime estimated at 15 ml. Sparkling water used.

name: Mimosa Mocktail
steps: Tilt a champagne flute and pour in 120 ml (4 oz) ginger ale.
Top it off with 60 ml (2 oz) chilled fresh orange juice.

name: Rose Mocktail
steps: Make the cardamom rose syrup ahead (batch, makes about 1 1/2 cups): lightly crush 20 cardamom pods (about 1 1/2 tsp) and toast them in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add 240 ml (1 cup) water, 1/4 cup edible rose petals and, if using, 1 tsp dried hibiscus. Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Stir in 1/2 cup (170 g) honey and 1 tbsp (15 ml) lemon juice, cover and steep for at least 1 hour. Strain through a fine mesh sieve and store in the fridge for up to 1 month.
Add crushed ice to a glass, then add 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the rose syrup and 1 tbsp (15 ml) lemon or lime juice.
Top with 240 ml (1 cup) soda water.
Garnish with fruit or lemon slices if you like.
verified_note: Page's homemade cardamom rose honey syrup mapped to rose_syrup:30. Page does not name a glass. Its ingredient list says 2 tbsp simple syrup but the method says rose syrup; the method was followed.

name: Rose & Rhubarb Soda
steps: Make the rhubarb syrup ahead (batch, enough for many drinks): combine 3/4 lb chopped rhubarb, 1 cup water, 1 cup cane sugar and 1 split vanilla bean in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, then lower the heat, cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in 1/2 tsp orange blossom water, cover and let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate overnight, then strain through a nut milk bag or a cheesecloth-lined sieve.
Fill a shaker with ice and add 22 ml (0.75 oz) fresh strained lemon juice, 22 ml (0.75 oz) rhubarb syrup and 3 drops rose water. Shake.
Strain into a chilled small glass (coupe or bistro glass).
Top with about 60 ml (2 oz) tonic water.
verified_note: Rhubarb syrup has no id; mapped to simple_syrup:22. 3 drops rose water is about 1 dash. Optional egg white skipped. No garnish listed on page. Not included: rhubarb syrup (homemade, 22 ml)

name: Beet-Sumac Soda
steps: Stir beet juice, syrup and lemon
Add ice and top with soda water

name: Homemade Tarragon Soda
steps: Make the tarragon syrup (enough for 5 glasses): heat 3/4 cup sugar and 1/2 cup water in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves.
Add 1 bunch fresh tarragon, 1 teaspoon aniseed or fennel seeds, 1 tablespoon lemon zest, 1/8 teaspoon baking soda and 1 pinch kosher salt. Boil for 1 minute, then let cool for 5 minutes.
Blend the mixture with 1/2 cup ice until smooth, refrigerate for at least 1 hour, then strain.
Stir in 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice and keep refrigerated until serving.
To serve, fill a glass with ice, add 2 oz (60 ml) of the tarragon syrup and top with seltzer water.
verified_note: Page is the Georgian tarkhun tarragon soda; 101cookbooks' Homemade Tarragon Soda gives no per-glass amounts so this page was used. Syrup (sugar, water, tarragon, lemon juice) is mapped to simple_syrup:60 per glass. Seltzer amount is not given; 120 ml is an assumed top-up. Garnish not stated on page (tarragon sprig is an assumption). Not included: fresh tarragon (1 bunch per 5 glasses, inside the syrup)

name: Cider, Thyme & Tonic
steps: Lightly bruise thyme in the glass
Add ice and apple cider
Top with tonic

name: Ranch Water (Zero-Proof)
steps: Pour 45 ml (1 1/2 oz) non-alcoholic agave spirit alternative into a glass.
Squeeze in 15 ml (1/2 oz) fresh lime juice.
Fill the rest of the glass with about 180 ml (6 oz) soda water, ideally Topo Chico.
Garnish with a lime wedge and squeeze in more lime if you like.
verified_note: Page does not name a glass or say to use ice; temp set to cold. Not included: Ritual Agave Spirit Alternative 45 ml

name: Italian Greyhound Spritz
steps: Add 45 ml (1 1/2 oz) non-alcoholic gin alternative, 30 ml (1 oz) non-alcoholic aperitif alternative and 60 ml (2 oz) fresh grapefruit juice to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake until well chilled.
Pour into a fresh glass filled with ice and top with sparkling water.
verified_note: Page gives no amount for the sparkling water; 60 ml is an estimate to top the glass. Page does not name a glass or garnish. Not included: Ritual Gin Alternative 45 ml, Ritual Aperitif Alternative 30 ml

name: Sparkling Citrus Hibiscus Cooler
steps: Heat 3 cups (24 oz) water to a low simmer, add 3 hibiscus tea bags (or 1 tablespoon loose hibiscus tea), steep 3 minutes, then remove the bags or strain out the tea. Let it cool to room temperature, about 20 minutes. This makes enough for 4 glasses.
Make honey syrup: warm 2 tablespoons honey with 2 tablespoons water until the honey fully stirs in, then set aside.
Fill a medium (12 oz) glass with ice and pour in about 3/4 cup (180 ml) of the cooled hibiscus tea, so the glass is about half full.
Add 1 tablespoon (15 ml) lime juice and 1 teaspoon of the honey syrup, then stir.
Top the glass with sparkling water (Topo Chico or club soda) and stir gently.
Taste and adjust the lime juice or syrup, garnish with a lime round and serve right away.
verified_note: Closest published page found (no published recipe uses hibiscus + orange juice with exactly this name). Quantities divided by 4. 1 tsp honey syrup = about 1/2 tsp honey + 1/2 tsp water. Sparkling water amount is not stated ('top'); 120 ml assumed to fill a 12 oz glass.

name: Cucumber Mint Hydration Refresher
steps: Put about 1/3 cup thinly sliced cucumber in the bottom of a glass and muddle it gently until lightly crushed.
Add 4 fresh mint leaves (or small sprigs) and muddle them with the cucumber. Add about 20 ml (4 tsp) fresh lime juice and about 1 1/4 tsp simple syrup.
Fill the glass with ice.
Top with 1/2 cup (120 ml) cold sparkling water or club soda and stir gently.
Garnish with cucumber slices and mint and serve right away.
verified_note: Page gives only mint (4 leaves) and 1/2 cup sparkling water for a single glass; cucumber, lime juice (1/2 cup) and simple syrup (2 to 3 tbsp) come from the 6-serving pitcher divided by 6. Recipe is titled Cucumber Lime Cooler, closest match to this refresher.

name: Lavender Honey Lemonade
steps: Put 1/2 tsp dried edible lavender buds into a tea bag or small cheesecloth pouch and seal it.
Bring 1 cup (240 ml) water to a boil, add the lavender pouch and steep for 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove the pouch and let the lavender water cool completely.
Mix in the juice of 1/2 large lemon (about 1 1/2 tbsp) and 1 1/4 tbsp honey (adjust to taste). Stir or shake to mix.
Serve over ice cubes.
verified_note: Page: 2 tsp lavender, 4 cups water, juice of 2 large lemons (about 6 tbsp), 5 to 6 tbsp honey; divided by 4.

name: Thyme Blackberry Breeze
steps: Puree 1 cup thawed frozen blackberries in a food processor until smooth.
Combine the puree, 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey syrup and 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium heat about 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Let the mixture cool completely, strain it into an airtight glass container and refrigerate (keeps up to 2 months). This makes about 10 servings.
To serve, mix 1 to 2 tablespoons of the syrup with 8 ounces (240 ml) seltzer water over ice.
verified_note: No published recipe under the exact name 'Thyme Blackberry Breeze'; closest blackberry-thyme soda used. Ings are about 1/10 of the syrup batch (one serving). The honey syrup recipe is not on the page ('see recipe'), counted as honey. Page does not mention a garnish.

name: Basil Watermelon Smash
glass: glass filled with ice (page names no glass type)
steps: Make the basil syrup: put 1/4 cup packed fresh basil leaves, 1/4 cup sugar and 1/4 cup water in a small pan. Heat over medium heat, stirring now and then, until it reaches a gentle simmer without boiling, and keep heating for 5 to 7 minutes until the sugar has dissolved.
Take the pan off the heat, strain out the basil and let the syrup cool to room temperature. You only need 15 ml (1/2 oz) for one drink; keep the rest.
Blend 1 cup seedless watermelon chunks until smooth, then strain out the pulp so you have about 1/2 cup (120 ml) of watermelon juice.
Add the watermelon juice, 30 ml (1 oz) fresh lime juice and 15 ml (1/2 oz) basil syrup to a shaker filled with ice. Shake for 15 seconds.
Strain into a glass filled with ice, top with 60 ml (2 oz) sparkling water and serve right away.
verified_note: Basil syrup mapped to simple_syrup (the basil and sugar go into the syrup batch, so no separate basil line). Watermelon is 1 cup chunks blended and strained to about 120 ml juice.

name: Elderflower Apple Sparkler
glass: cup (page does not name a glass)
steps: In a jug or mixing glass, add 30 ml (2 tbsp) elderflower cordial, 3/4 of a mint sprig and 7.5 ml (1/2 tbsp) lemon juice and muddle with a wooden spoon.
Add 125 ml (1/2 cup) good-quality chilled apple cider and about 1/4 of a small apple, thinly sliced into rounds, and stir to combine.
Just before serving, add about 190 ml (3/4 cup) chilled sparkling water.
Pour into a cup or glass filled with ice, making sure the apple slices go in too.
verified_note: Page makes 4 (1/2 cup cordial, 3 mint sprigs, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 cups apple cider, 1 small apple, 750 ml sparkling water); divided by 4. Apple cider mapped to apple_juice. Optional bourbon omitted.

name: Chamomile Peach Mule
steps: Fill a mug with ice
Add chamomile, peach and lemon and stir
Top with ginger beer

name: Minted Green Tea Sparkler
steps: Bring 1 cup (240 ml) water to a boil, take it off the heat, add 1 green tea bag and steep for 4 minutes with the bag submerged.
Discard the bag, cool the tea for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for 2 hours or until chilled.
At serving time put 8 to 10 mint leaves in a glass and mash them several times with a muddler or wooden spoon to release the juices without crushing them to pulp. Add about 1/2 cup ice cubes.
Stir 1/4 cup (60 ml) 100 percent white grape juice and 2 tbsp fresh lime juice into the chilled tea and pour it into the glass.
Garnish with a lime wedge and a mint leaf.
verified_note: Closest published match (no page named Minted Green Tea Sparkler had single-serving amounts). Page: 4 cups water, 4 tea bags, 32 to 40 mint leaves plus 4 sprigs, 1 cup white grape juice, 1/2 cup lime juice; divided by 4. The tea is mapped as green_tea 240 ml (brewed). White grape juice mapped to grape_juice.

name: Sage Grapefruit Tonic
steps: In the bottom of a cocktail shaker crush 1 to 2 fresh sage leaves into 1/2 to 1 tbsp agave nectar (use less if the grapefruit is sweet) with a muddler or wooden spoon.
Add 1 cup (240 ml) fresh grapefruit juice (about 1 large grapefruit), the juice of 1/2 lime (about 1 tbsp), the juice of 1/2 large lemon (about 2 tbsp) and a pinch of sea salt.
Shake vigorously, then strain over ice cubes.
verified_note: Sage has no id, so it is listed in unmapped. Page: 3 sage leaves, 1 to 2 tbsp agave, 2 large grapefruits (about 2 cups) juice, 1 lime, 1 large lemon, sea salt to taste, serves 2 to 3; divided by 2. Salt mapped to black_salt (sea salt). Not included: fresh sage leaves, 1 to 2 leaves

name: Hibiscus Lemongrass Basil Iced Tea
steps: Bring 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) water to a boil in a small pot.
Take it off the heat and add 1/4 of a lemongrass stalk (thinly sliced), 1 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp dried hibiscus flowers and 3 tbsp loosely packed fresh basil leaves.
Cover and steep for 20 minutes.
Strain into a jug or glass and discard the solids.
Stir in 1 tbsp fresh lime juice. Taste and add more honey if needed.
Chill until cold, then serve over ice with a lemongrass stalk, basil and lime slices.
verified_note: Page yields 1 quart from 5 cups water, 1/4 cup honey, 1/2 cup dried hibiscus flowers, 3/4 cup basil, 1/4 cup lime juice, 1 stalk lemongrass; divided by 4 (about 250 ml per glass, my assumption). hibiscus_tea here means dried hibiscus flowers, not brewed tea; basil given in tbsp.

name: Tangerine Rosemary Mocktail
steps: Make rosemary simple syrup: combine 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup granulated sugar and 4 sprigs rosemary in a small saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Remove from the heat, let steep about 10 minutes, strain out the rosemary and cool completely. Keep refrigerated in a lidded jar (makes enough for many drinks).
Fill a glass with ice.
Add 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh tangerine juice, 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice, 1 tablespoon rosemary simple syrup and 2 tablespoons lemon-lime soda.
Top with club soda and stir before drinking. For a less sweet drink, leave out the lemon-lime soda.
Garnish with a tangerine slice and a rosemary sprig.
verified_note: Tangerine juice mapped to orange_juice. Rosemary simple syrup mapped to simple_syrup (rosemary-infused). Club soda amount not stated; 90 ml assumed to top the glass. Rosemary sprig is garnish only.

name: Cranberry Rosemary Refresher
steps: Make the rosemary syrup: in a small pan over medium-low heat whisk 2 tbsp sugar with 2 tbsp water, add 3/4 of a fresh rosemary sprig and bring to a simmer, whisking often (about 5 minutes).
As soon as it simmers, take the pan off the heat, cover it and let it cool for 10 minutes. Strain the syrup and chill it.
Fill a highball glass with ice and add the 2 tbsp rosemary syrup.
Pour in 1/4 cup (60 ml) chilled unsweetened cranberry juice.
Top with 1 cup (240 ml) chilled sparkling water or club soda. Add about 1 tbsp cranberries and stir until combined. Garnish with a lime wedge and serve.
garnish: 1 tbsp cranberries, lime wedge or rosemary sprig
verified_note: Page makes 4 and gives 1 cup cranberry juice, 4 cups sparkling water, 2 tbsp rosemary syrup per glass (made from 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup water, 3 rosemary sprigs); divided by 4 here. Syrup mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Watermelon Mint Cider-Vinegar Tonic
steps: Make the concentrate (batch): bring 3 cups (710 ml) water and 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt to a boil in a saucepan. Add 1 cup (340 g) good-quality honey, stir until dissolved and remove from the heat.
Put 6 cups (910 g) coarsely chopped watermelon and 1 cup (25 g) tightly packed fresh spearmint in a large bowl. Pour in the honey water and let it cool to room temperature.
Stir in 1 cup (240 ml) cider vinegar, then refrigerate for several hours or overnight to steep.
Strain the mixture (the pickled watermelon can be eaten). Store the concentrate in a clean glass jar in the fridge for up to 1 week.
To serve one drink: pour 1/4 cup (60 ml) concentrate into a glass over ice, dilute with 3/4 cup (180 ml) water, and garnish with watermelon, sliced cucumber and mint.
verified_note: Ings are 1/20 of the batch (one 240 ml serving: 60 ml concentrate + 180 ml water, so water = 35 ml from concentrate + 180 ml). Salt (1/4 tsp per batch) skipped. Mint 1.25 g approximated as 3 leaves.

name: Pineapple Coconut Water
steps: Put 90 ml (3/8 cup) fresh pineapple juice, 60 ml (1/4 cup) pure coconut water and 1/4 tsp pure ginger juice into a cocktail shaker or mason jar filled with ice.
Shake well, then taste. Add 1/2 tsp runny honey only if it needs it.
Fill a small chilled glass with ice and a few thin lime slices, pour in the mixture and add an extra squeeze of lime if you like.
verified_note: Ginger is pressed ginger juice (1/2 tsp for 2, so 1/4 tsp). Lime is used for slices and a squeeze (1 lime for 2). Honey optional, left out of ings.

name: Strawberry Basil Fields
steps: Cut the tops off 4 strawberries, halve them and put them in a cocktail shaker.
Add 8 to 9 large fresh basil leaves and 1/2 teaspoon granulated sugar.
Muddle until the strawberries are very soft.
Add 1 cup lemonade and a little ice, put the lid on and shake until combined.
Fill a glass with ice and strain the mixture over it through a fine mesh or Hawthorne strainer.
Top with a small splash of club soda or seltzer water and garnish with a basil sprig.
verified_note: No published recipe under the exact name 'Strawberry Basil Fields'; this is the closest single-serving strawberry-basil mocktail found. Sugar 0.5 tsp mapped to simple_syrup. Club soda is 'a small splash' (30 ml assumed). Lemonade is the main liquid and has no id. Not included: Lemonade, 1 cup (240 ml)

name: Classic Lemonade
steps: Stir the lemon juice and simple syrup together
Add cold water and stir well
Pour over ice

name: Pink Strawberry Lemonade
steps: Make the syrup: heat 2 tbsp of the water with 1.5 tbsp honey (or sugar) in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring until it reaches a low simmer and the sweetener dissolves, about a minute.
Blend 57 g hulled strawberries with 45 ml lemon juice until smooth (the page says about 30 seconds, longer if needed).
In a glass or jar, mix the strawberry-lemon puree, the syrup, 0.75 tsp rose water (optional) and 120 ml cold water. Stir well.
Serve over ice.
verified_note: Honey or sugar both allowed on page; used honey. Total water 150 ml = 30 ml in syrup + 120 ml cold. Rose water is optional on the page.

name: Fresh Ginger Lemonade
steps: Cut about 17 g unpeeled fresh ginger into thin slices and remove the zest of half a lemon in strips with a vegetable peeler.
In a small saucepan bring 3/4 cup (190 ml) water, 2 tbsp (25 g) sugar, the ginger slices and the lemon zest to a boil.
Remove from heat, cover and steep for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Strain out the ginger and zest, then mix the ginger syrup with 1/4 cup (62 ml) fresh lemon juice and chill thoroughly.
Serve over plenty of ice.
verified_note: Page: 55-85 g ginger (used 70 g), zest of 2 lemons, 750 ml water, 100 g sugar, 250 ml lemon juice for 4 servings, divided by 4. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Ginger Spiced Lemonade
steps: Put 1/4 cup chopped jaggery and 1 cup (240 ml) water in a bowl and mix.
Let the jaggery dissolve fully, about 30 to 40 minutes, then strain through a fine strainer if there is any dirt.
Add 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Add 1/8 tsp dry ginger powder, about 1/16 tsp black pepper powder, about 1/5 tsp green cardamom powder and a pinch of salt, and mix well.
Add a few ice cubes or refrigerate, and serve chilled.
verified_note: Page recipe is Panakam (jaggery-ginger-pepper-lemon drink), halved from 1/2 cup jaggery, 2 cups water, 1/4 tsp dry ginger, 1/8 tsp pepper, 1/3-1/2 tsp cardamom, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 pinch salt; servings not stated. Dry ginger powder mapped to ginger; salt to black_salt.

name: Saffron Cardamom Lemonade
steps: Make the syrup: combine 0.25 cup sugar, a pinch (about 1/16 tsp) of saffron strands, a tiny pinch (about 1/32 tsp) of crushed cardamom seeds and 60 ml (0.25 cup) water in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Heat until the sugar dissolves, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Let the syrup cool, then stir in 0.75 tsp rose water and a tiny pinch of salt. Refrigerate until fully chilled.
Fill a glass with 240 ml (1 cup) cold water and plenty of crushed ice. Add 60 ml lemon juice and the chilled syrup, then stir well.
Serve cold.
verified_note: Page uses sugar for the syrup; mapped to simple_syrup:0.25cup (sugar). Water 300 ml = 60 ml in syrup + 240 ml for the drink. 1/4 tsp saffron per 4 servings is about 1 pinch each. Salt (tiny pinch) omitted from ings. Page names no serving glass.

name: Arnold Palmer
steps: Stir lemon juice, syrup and cold water into a lemonade
Fill the glass one-third with lemonade and add ice
Top with cold-brewed black tea and stir

name: Lemon Squeeze
steps: Shake lemon and honey with ice
Strain and top with soda

name: Cherry Limeade
steps: Stir the syrup, lime juice and cherry juice together
Pour over a glass of crushed ice
Top with club soda just before serving and stir gently

name: Watermelon Mocktail
steps: Optional rim: mix 0.5 tbsp sugar, 1/16 tsp salt and 0.75 tsp lime zest on a small plate, rub a lime slice round the rim of the glass and dip the rim in the mix.
Blend 0.25 cup peeled, chopped watermelon until smooth (the page blends 1 cup for 4 glasses; a larger batch is easier in a blender).
Put 2 slices of lime (about 0.5 lime) in the glass, add about 1 tbsp torn mint leaves and 1 tbsp sugar (optional).
Muddle everything with a rolling pin or muddler, and add ice if using.
Pour the watermelon juice over the mixture, top with 240 ml chilled sparkling water or soda and mix well.
Garnish with mint and lime slices and serve immediately.
verified_note: Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:1tbsp. Lime is 2 slices (about 0.5 lime) muddled, not juice. Page names no glass; highball suggested by size.

name: Virgin Mojito
steps: Muddle 6 mint leaves in a cocktail shaker.
Add 1 oz (2 tbsp, 30 ml) lime juice and 1/2 oz (1 tbsp, 15 ml) simple syrup (or 1 oz orgeat syrup).
Fill the shaker with ice and shake until cold.
Fill a glass with ice and strain the drink into it.
Top with 4 oz (1/2 cup, 120 ml) soda water (or tonic water), add more ice and garnish with extra mint leaves.
verified_note: Orgeat option not mapped; simple syrup used. Shaking time not given.

name: Cardamom Mojito Mocktail
steps: Crush 1 to 2 green cardamom pods (skin on; recipe uses 3 for two drinks, so about 1 1/2 per drink).
Boil the crushed pods with 3 tbsp sugar and 45 ml water until the sugar dissolves.
Take off the heat and let the flavour develop, then strain and cool the syrup completely.
In a tall glass, lightly muddle about 2 tbsp mint leaves with half a lime cut in wedges.
Pour in the cardamom syrup.
Top with 150 ml soda water, add ice cubes and extra mint leaves, and serve.
verified_note: Divided the 2-serving recipe by 2. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:3tbsp (it is dissolved in the 45 ml water). Page gives no times for resting/cooling, no lime wedge or mint-per-glass quantities, and no syrup amount per glass; the whole single-serving batch of syrup goes in. Ice amount not stated.

name: Pomegranate Mojito Mocktail
steps: Put the wedges of half a lime and 1/4 cup (60 ml) pomegranate juice into a tall glass (add sweetener if you like) and muddle gently until the lime juice is pressed out.
Clap 6 to 8 mint leaves between your hands to release their scent, add them to the glass and press gently with the muddler a couple of times.
Add plenty of ice and top with 1 cup (240 ml) soda water (ginger ale also works). Stir well.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds, mint and lime.
verified_note: Mint 6-8 leaves mapped to 7. Sweetener optional, 'to taste' (not mapped). Optional NA rum ignored. Glass 'tall glass' mapped to collins.

name: Virgin Piña Colada
steps: Add 3/4 cup ice to a blender.
Pour in 1/2 cup (120 ml) whisked cream of coconut, 1/4 cup (60 ml) pineapple juice and 1/4 cup (60 ml) heavy whipping cream.
Blend until completely smooth (add frozen pineapple or more ice for a thicker drink if you like).
Pour into a glass and, if you like, garnish with pineapple leaves, edible flowers or citrus.
garnish: pineapple leaves, edible flowers or citrus (optional)

name: Virgin Mary
steps: Stir the tomato juice with lime juice, pepper, chilli and black salt
Pour over ice
Top with a celery stalk

name: Zero-Proof Margarita
steps: Rim the glass with salt using a lime wedge
Shake the lime juice, orange juice and agave with ice for 15 seconds
Strain over fresh ice
Top with sparkling water and garnish with lime

name: Spicy Mango Margarita (Zero-Proof)
steps: Mix 1 tbsp kosher salt, 1/8 tsp ground sumac and 1 tsp sea salt on a plate.
Rub the outside rim of a lowball glass with a lime half and roll it in the salt mixture.
For the spicy version, put 2 to 3 jalapeno slices in the bottom of the glass.

Fill the glass with ice, add 1/4 cup (60 ml) mango juice, 1 tbsp lime juice and 1 oz (30 ml) coconut water (or a non-alcoholic tequila alternative), and stir, smashing the jalapeno a little (more smashing and seeds make it hotter). A shaker can be used instead.
Fill to the top with sparkling water and stir again.

name: Zero-Proof Moscow Mule
steps: Muddle the lime quarters in the mug until the juice is released
Clap the mint and press it gently into the lime
Add plenty of ice, top with ginger beer and stir gently

name: Pom Mexican Mule
steps: Add 2 oz (60 ml) non-alcoholic agave spirit, 1/2 oz (15 ml) simple syrup, 1/2 oz (15 ml) lime juice, 1 oz (30 ml) pomegranate juice and ice to a copper mug.
Top with 3 oz (90 ml) ginger beer.
Stir.
Garnish with a lime wheel and pomegranate arils.

name: Faux Cosmopolitan
steps: Shake the cranberry and lime juice with ice
Strain into a martini glass

name: Virgin Daiquiri (Strawberry)

name: Non-Alcoholic Appletini

Add apple juice, lemon juice and simple syrup to a shaker full of ice and shake hard for 10 to 20 seconds until frosty
Strain into the chilled martini glass (no ice in the glass) and top with the sparkling water, or stir it in gently after straining
Garnish with a slice of green apple and serve right away

name: Watermelon Punch (Zero-Proof)
steps: Blend and strain watermelon

name: Pineapple Punch

Stir 1/4 cup (60 ml) pineapple juice with 1 tbsp (15 ml) frozen limeade concentrate (undiluted) until combined.
Stir in a few pieces of fresh fruit such as pineapple chunks, orange slices or lime rounds (frozen fruit also works and can replace ice).
Just before serving, pour in about 1/3 cup (83 ml) chilled ginger ale or lemon-lime soda, stir gently and serve immediately.
garnish: pineapple pieces, orange slices, lime rounds

name: 5-Minute Mango Mocktail
steps: Put half a lime (cut in slices or wedges), about 1 tbsp of mint leaves and 1 tbsp sugar (optional) into a serving glass.
Muddle for about a minute.
Half-fill the glass with ice (about 1/4 cup).
Pour 1/4 cup (60 ml) mango pulp or juice over the ice.
Top up with 1/2 cup (120 ml) sparkling water or Sprite.
Garnish with a sprig of mint and a slice of lime and serve immediately, well chilled.

name: Penicillin Mocktail
steps: Make the ginger-honey syrup ahead: simmer 6 oz honey, 3 oz water and a finely chopped 3 to 4 oz piece of ginger on low for 10 minutes, let cool, strain out the ginger and bottle it (the page also gives juicer and blender methods).
Add 2 oz (60 ml) non-alcoholic spirit, 0.75 oz (22 ml) lemon juice and 0.75 oz (22 ml) ginger-honey syrup to a shaker.

Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with a lemon peel or a piece of candied ginger.

name: Coconut Strawberry Cream Bliss
steps: Purée strawberries into the glass base with crushed ice
Shake coconut milk and vanilla until frothy
Pour gently over the red layer

name: Creamy Banana Chai Frappe
steps: Place 1 cup (240 ml) almond milk (or any milk), 2 cups ice, 0.5 banana, the contents of 1 chai tea bag (cut open, tea removed) and honey to sweeten in a blender.
Blend until smooth.

name: Avocado Lime Frost
steps: Blend avocado, lime, sweetener and coconut water with ice until velvety

name: Frozen Peach Velvet Slush
steps: Blend about 70 g (one sixth of a 15.25 oz can) drained sliced peaches, 30 ml (2 tbsp) frozen orange juice concentrate and 60 ml (0.25 cup) apricot nectar until smooth. The page makes 6 servings, so a full batch is easier in a blender.

name: Guava Cream Dream
steps: Shake guava, coconut cream, lime and syrup hard with ice

name: Watermelon Lime Mint Chiller
steps: Blend 1 cup diced watermelon, 5 mint leaves and about 12 ml (2 1/2 tsp) lime juice until combined.
Pour over ice and garnish. For a fizzy version, top up with about 120 ml sparkling water (page: 2 cups sparkling water or kombucha stretches the recipe to 4 servings) and stir gently.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Coffee Smoothie
steps: The day before, pour 3/4 cup (180 ml) of brewed, cooled coffee into an ice cube tray and freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Add the coffee ice cubes, 1 tablespoon peanut butter, 1/4 cup (60 ml) whole milk, 1 tablespoon chocolate syrup and half a ripe banana to a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour into a glass and top with whipped cream and a little more chocolate syrup.
verified_note: Page serves 2 and every amount was halved. Brewed cooled coffee mapped to cold_brew. Whipped cream amount for topping is not given; 1 tbsp is a placeholder. Glass type is not stated on the page.

name: Energizing Green Smoothie
steps: Pour 150 ml chilled coconut water into a blender.
Add 0.25 cup frozen mango chunks, 0.25 cup frozen pineapple chunks, 0.5 sliced medium banana and 2 handfuls of baby spinach.
Cover and blend until smooth.
Serve right away.

name: Tropical Fruit Smoothie
steps: Add 3/8 cup (90 ml) pineapple juice, 1/4 cup (60 ml) canned coconut milk (light is fine), half a sliced large banana, 1/2 cup frozen mango and 1/2 cup frozen pineapple to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Pour into a glass, add garnishes if you like, and serve immediately.
garnish: maraschino cherry, lime slice, mint sprig or pineapple wedge (optional)

name: Blueberry Cashew Buckwheat Smoothie
steps: Put 2 tbsp cooked buckwheat, 0.25 cup fresh or frozen blueberries, 1.5 tbsp cashews, 0.5 tbsp chia seeds, 0.25 banana, 2 tbsp plain yogurt, 0.25 cup skimmed milk and 0.5 tbsp linseed or hemp seeds in a blender.

name: Berry Banana Protein Shake
steps: Put 0.25 cup frozen blueberries and raspberries, 0.5 small banana, 0.5 cup (120 ml) unsweetened vanilla almond milk, 0.5 scoop vanilla protein powder and a handful of ice into a blender.
Blend it up until smooth.

name: Strawberry Milkshake
steps: Blend the strawberries, ice cream and milk until smooth and creamy
Pour into a glass, top with whipped cream and a strawberry

name: Citrus Espresso Tonic
steps: Fill a rocks glass nearly to the top with ice.
Slowly pour in 4 to 5 oz (118 to 148 ml) tonic water, depending on your ice and glass, leaving room for the espresso. Add 3 dashes orange bitters.
Gently pour 1.5 oz (44 ml) espresso (a bright, light roast) so it floats on top of the tonic. A small pitcher helps if pouring from the espresso cup is tricky.
Squeeze one lime wedge over the drink. Cut a small slit in the second wedge and set it on the rim as garnish.
Gently stir with a straw right before serving.

name: Iced Vanilla Oat Latte
steps: Finely grind the whole coffee beans, put the grounds in the espresso machine and press them firmly into the basket, then pull a double espresso shot (1.5 oz / 45 ml).
Fill a glass with ice, mounding it slightly above the rim.
Pour in 8 oz (240 ml) cold oat milk.
Add 1/2 fl oz (15 ml) vanilla simple syrup, and add the espresso shot (the page does not say when; it goes in with the syrup).
Serve immediately.

name: Ginger Cold Brew Fizz
steps: Add cubed ice to a serving glass.
Pour in 4 3/4 oz (about 140 ml) ginger beer.
Layer 2 oz (about 60 ml) cold brew on top of the ginger beer.
Top the drink with 3/4 oz (about 22 ml) orange juice.

name: Hibiscus Cold Brew Tonic
steps: Combine hibiscus and tonic over ice
Float cold brew on top

name: Salted Caramel Iced Coffee
steps: Make the caramel first (makes enough for several drinks): put 1 cup granulated sugar and 1/4 cup water in a heavy-bottomed pot and stir constantly over medium-high heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture boils.
Lower the heat to medium-low and let it boil without stirring until deep amber, about 7 to 10 minutes. Remove from the heat immediately, as it burns quickly.
Whisk in 3/4 cup heavy cream until smooth (if it seizes, return to low heat and whisk until dissolved, then remove from heat).
Whisk in 3 tbsp butter, 1/2 tsp fine sea salt and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract. Let the caramel cool; it thickens as it cools.
For one drink, add 2 tbsp caramel to a mug or heatproof container, pour in 8 oz (240 ml) strong coffee, and stir until the caramel dissolves.
Optionally drizzle more caramel inside a serving glass, fill it with ice (larger chunks are best) and pour the coffee mixture over.
Optionally top with a splash of milk and a small pinch of salt.
garnish: drizzle of caramel, pinch of salt

name: Spiced Mocha Chiller
steps: Blend coffee, milk, cocoa, maple and a pinch of cayenne with ice
Top with whipped cream and cocoa

name: Cold Brew
steps: Make the concentrate (page batch scaled to one glass): put about 17 g (page: 3 oz / 85 g for the whole batch) coarsely ground coffee and about 140 ml (page: 3 cups for the whole batch) filtered water in a jar and stir. Rest 5 minutes, then stir again.
Cover the jar and refrigerate for 12 to 18 hours.

Set a thin paper coffee filter or thin cotton cloth in a small fine-mesh sieve over a measuring cup. Pour the concentrate through it and let it drain for a few minutes. The concentrate keeps in the fridge up to 2 weeks (best in the first week).
To serve, fill a glass with ice, add water until the glass is half full, top with the concentrate (about 120 ml) and stir. Adjust the water-to-concentrate ratio to taste.

name: Vietnamese Iced Coffee
steps: Place a Vietnamese coffee filter (phin) on top of a mug or heat-proof glass. If you do not have one, use a French press.
Unscrew the press from inside the filter, add 2 tbsp dark roast ground coffee, and screw it back on so the grounds are snug but still have a little give.
Pour in just enough hot water to soak the grounds and wait 30 seconds.
Fill the filter with hot boiling water (3/4 cup total), cover it, and let it brew for about 5 minutes.
Add 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk to a tall glass, stir in the brewed coffee, add 2/3 cup crushed ice, and serve.

name: Thai Iced Coffee
steps: Steep 3 tbsp (45 ml) Thai coffee powder in 3/4 cup (180 ml) off-the-boil water for 5 minutes (cloth filter bag, French press, or a jug you will filter later).
In a mixing glass, combine 2 tbsp (30 ml) sweetened condensed milk, 2 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt.
Strain or filter the steeped coffee into the mixing glass.
Stir until the condensed milk and sugar dissolve. Taste and adjust sweetness; it should taste slightly strong and sweet because the ice will dilute it.
Fill a 16 oz glass completely with ice and pour the coffee over it.
Drizzle 2-3 tbsp (30-45 ml) evaporated milk on top, then stir it in before drinking. Add more for extra creaminess.

Sugar 2 tsp mapped to simple_syrup:2tsp. Evaporated milk 2-3 tbsp, used 2 tbsp = 30 ml. Salt pinch mapped to black_salt. Not included: Thai coffee powder (3 tbsp)

name: Kori-Kohi (Coffee Ice Cubes & Milk)
steps: Dissolve 1/2 tbsp instant coffee in 2 tbsp hot water.
Add 6 tbsp cold water and mix well.
Pour the mixture into an ice cube tray and freeze.
When frozen, transfer the coffee cubes to a glass.
Pour 3/4 cup (180 ml) warm or room-temperature milk over the cubes and stir until they dissolve.
Sweeten with a little sugar syrup if desired, then serve.

name: Peanut Butter Iced Coffee
steps: Add 1/2 cup (120 ml) brewed coffee at room temperature, 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk, 1/2 tbsp peanut butter and 1/2 tbsp granulated sweetener (optional) to a high-speed blender.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into a glass filled with ice and serve.

name: Iced White Chocolate Mocha
steps: Put 1 1/2 cups ice into a 16 oz glass.
Mix 2 tbsp white chocolate powder or sauce with 1 shot (about 2 oz / 60 ml) of espresso. Use a double shot for a stronger drink.
Stir thoroughly until the sugar has dissolved.
Pour the sweet espresso over the ice.
Pour 3/4 cup (180 ml) whole milk over the ice, give it a quick stir, and top with whipped cream if you like.
verified_note: White chocolate powder/sauce mapped to white_chocolate.

name: Vanilla Sweet Cream Cold Brew
steps: Make the cold brew ahead: combine 1 cup coarse ground coffee with 4 cups cold water in a French press or lidded jar and refrigerate 12 hours, then press or strain through a coffee filter. Do not use fine-grind coffee.
Make the vanilla syrup ahead: boil 1/4 cup water and 1/4 cup sugar over medium-high heat for 1 minute until the sugar dissolves, remove from heat, stir in 2 tsp vanilla extract and cool completely.
Make the sweet cream ahead: combine 1/2 cup whole milk, 1/2 cup heavy whipping cream and the cooled vanilla syrup in a small jar.
Fill a 16 oz glass with ice.
Add 4 oz cold brew concentrate, 4 oz water and 2 oz vanilla sweet cream; adjust to taste. Optionally top with whipped cream or vanilla sweet cream cold foam.
garnish: optional whipped cream or sweet cream cold foam

name: Iced Caramel Macchiato
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice, then pour in 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk.
Add 2 shots of espresso (or strong brewed coffee) and 1 tsp vanilla simple syrup (or 1 pump vanilla coffee syrup), then stir to combine.
Drizzle 1 tbsp caramel sauce over the top and serve immediately.
verified_note: Page says 2 shots espresso without a volume; taken as 60 ml (30 ml per shot).

name: Dirty Horchata
steps: In a bowl combine 30 g (about 1/6 cup) white rice, 12 g chopped almonds and 1/3 of a cinnamon stick. Cover with warm water and soak for 5 hours or overnight, until softened.
Strain and discard the soaking water. Put the rice mixture in a blender with 60 ml evaporated milk and blend on high until thick and smooth.

Push the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a pitcher. Stir in 160 ml cold water, 60 ml whole milk, about 1 3/4 tbsp granulated sugar and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract until fully combined. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
To serve, pour the horchata into an ice-filled glass and top with about 40 ml (roughly 2 to 3 tbsp) cold brew concentrate, to taste.
verified_note: Divided from 6 servings (1 cup rice, 1/2 cup chopped almonds, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 cups water, 12 oz evaporated milk, 1 1/2 cups whole milk, 2/3 cup sugar, 1 tbsp vanilla, 1 cup cold brew concentrate). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup, vanilla extract to vanilla_syrup, cold brew concentrate to cold_brew.

name: Homemade Frappuccino
steps: Put 1 cup crushed ice, 120 ml cold espresso (or very strong cold coffee), 90 ml half and half (or your preferred milk, soy or almond) and 1 tbsp granulated sugar into a blender.
Blend until well blended.
Pour into a tall glass. If you like, top with whipped cream and a drizzle of chocolate syrup.
Serve immediately.
verified_note: Half and half mapped to milk; granulated sugar mapped to simple_syrup (1 tbsp). Page halved from 2 servings (2 cups ice, 1 cup espresso, 3/4 cup half and half, 2 tbsp sugar). Whipped cream and chocolate syrup are optional toppings with no stated amount.

name: Lavender Frappuccino
steps: Make the lavender powder first (makes a batch; store airtight at room temperature): grind 1/4 cup culinary dried lavender to a fine powder, whisk in 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 2 1/2 tsp black currant powder (for color), 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp soy lecithin powder (optional), then grind again in batches until fine.
Add 3/4 cup (180 ml) whole milk, 1/4 cup (60 ml) heavy cream, 2 tbsp vanilla syrup, 1 tbsp lavender powder (or lavender syrup), 1/2 tsp xanthan gum (or 1 tsp corn starch) and 1 cup ice to a blender.
Blend until smooth and frothy.
Pour into a cup and top with whipped cream.
verified_note: Lavender powder (lavender, sugar, black currant powder) mapped to lavender at 1 tbsp. Page does not name a glass; tall assumed. Not included: xanthan gum 1/2 tsp (or 1 tsp corn starch), black currant powder (in homemade lavender powder)

name: Iced Coffee with Ice Cream
steps: Blend 1/2 cup vanilla ice cream, 3 oz (90 ml) chilled strong coffee, 3 1/2 tbsp milk and 1 tsp sugar until smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass. If you like, add one more scoop of ice cream on top.
Serve right away. Do not serve it over ice, as melting ice dilutes the drink.
garnish: extra scoop of vanilla ice cream (optional)
verified_note: Chilled strong coffee mapped to cold_brew; 3 1/2 tbsp milk = about 52 ml; sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Coconut Milk Iced Coffee
steps: Boil water and let it sit for 1 to 2 minutes (off the boil).
Put 1.5 tbsp espresso coffee powder in a cafetiere (French press) and pour in 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the off-the-boil water.
Steep for 5 minutes, then slowly press down the plunger.
Pour the coffee into a jug, let it cool, then chill for several hours (overnight is ideal).
Whisk in 125 ml (1/2 cup) coconut milk and 1 tbsp condensed milk, then serve over plenty of ice.
verified_note: Chilled cafetiere coffee mapped to cold_brew:125. Halved from 2 servings (3 tbsp coffee, 250 ml water, 250 ml coconut milk, 2 tbsp condensed milk). name: Indian Cold Coffee
steps: Add ice cubes, instant coffee, sugar and cold milk to a blender
Blend until frothy and pour into a tall glass; serve right away

name: Iced Pistachio Latte
steps: Make the pistachio syrup first (this makes a batch that keeps up to 2 weeks in the fridge): lightly crush 1 cup pistachios in a small saucepan, add 1 cup water and 1 cup granulated sugar, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Fill a tall glass with ice and pour 2 oz (60 ml) freshly brewed espresso over the ice.
Add 2 tbsp of the pistachio syrup (the page says 1 to 3 tbsp depending on taste) and stir.
Top with 6 oz (180 ml) cold milk or milk alternative and garnish with toasted pistachios.

name: Espresso Martini (Zero-Proof)
steps: Add 30 ml espresso, 1/8 cup (about 30 ml) sweetened condensed milk and 1/4 cup (about 60 ml) skim milk to a shaker filled with ice. (The page also lists 30 ml non-alcoholic vodka as optional.)
Shake well. A mason jar or any container with a tight lid also works.
Pour into a martini glass and serve, garnished with 3 coffee beans.
verified_note: Skim milk mapped to milk (whole). Page does not state servings; one martini glass assumed. Non-alcoholic vodka is optional on the page and left out. Not included: non-alcoholic vodka (optional, 30 ml)

name: Egg Coffee (Cà Phê Trứng)
steps: Brew the coffee. Traditional: set a phin filter on a cup, pack 4 tbsp Vietnamese ground coffee in the well, add a little hot water and bloom for 15 seconds, then fill with more hot water (about 1/2 cup total) and let it drain. Or brew 2-3 oz (60-90 ml) strong coffee any way you like.
In a small bowl, whisk 2 pasteurized egg yolks, 1 tsp white sugar and 1 tbsp sweetened condensed milk until light, frothy and noticeably bigger in volume.
Gently spoon or pour the egg cream over the brewed coffee. Adjust sugar and condensed milk to taste.
Optionally dust the top with cocoa powder or cinnamon.
Serve warm.
verified_note: Brewed strong coffee 2-3 oz -> espresso:75 (midpoint). Sugar 1 tsp -> simple_syrup:1tsp. Condensed milk 1 tbsp = 15 ml. Page also gives iced option (cool the coffee, pour over ice, add egg cream). Imbibe page failed to load so a second source was used.

name: Affogato
steps: Scoop 1/2 cup (1 to 2 scoops) high-quality vanilla gelato or ice cream into a small bowl or glass. Chilling the glass first helps it hold its shape longer.
Pour 1 shot (1.5 oz) hot espresso or very strong brewed coffee over the top.
Serve immediately. Optional: top with shaved chocolate, add about 1 teaspoon liqueur or serve biscotti on the side.

name: Mocha Latte
steps: Heat 1/2 cup (120 ml) coffee and 1 cup (240 ml) milk together in a pot over the stove.
Once warm, whisk in 1 to 2 tbsp hot cocoa/cacao mix until fully combined.
Keep heating until the mixture is nearly boiling and frothy (a hand frother can help).
Pour into a cup and top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cocoa powder.

name: Dirty Chai Latte
steps: In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, combine 0.5 tsp chai spices, 120 ml (1/2 cup) water and 0.5 black tea bag (or 0.5 tsp loose black tea). Bring to a boil, remove from heat and let rest 1 minute.
Meanwhile make 2 oz (60 ml) espresso or strong coffee and pour it into your mug.
Strain the tea into the mug (straining is optional, the spices settle to the bottom).
Rinse the saucepan, add 60 ml (1/4 cup) milk and 0.5 tbsp maple syrup, and heat to 150F (65C): hot with small bubbles at the edges but not simmering.
Froth the milk with a hand frother, whisk or French press, then let the foam rest about 30 seconds.
Pour the milk and foam into the mug, sprinkle with extra chai spices and serve.
verified_note: Halved to 1 small serving. Water + black tea bag brewed -> black_tea:120. Homemade chai spice blend (0.5 tsp) has no id and is not listed on the page's ingredient line; left unmapped. Maple syrup 1 tbsp halved to 0.5 tbsp. Not included: homemade chai spice blend (0.5 tsp)

name: Mexican Coffee
steps: Heat 1 cup (240 ml) water, 1 whole clove, 1/4 cinnamon stick and 2 tbsp brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add 1 tbsp regular-grind coffee and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir, cover and remove from heat.
Let the grounds settle, then pour into a mug (or strain into the mug).
verified_note: Page does not state servings; assumed 4 mugs from 4 cups water, so everything divided by 4 (2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 clove, 1/4 cinnamon stick, 1 tbsp coffee). Brown sugar -> simple_syrup:2tbsp. Ground coffee has no id (only brewed espresso/instant). Food Network version was rejected because it contains coffee liqueur. Not included: regular grind coffee (1 tbsp)

name: Café de Olla
steps: Heat water with piloncillo (or jaggery), ground coffee and a cinnamon stick, stirring until the sugar dissolves
Bring to a boil, take off the heat and steep 5 minutes
Strain into mugs and serve hot

name: Café Bombón
steps: Carefully pour 2 oz (60 ml) sweetened condensed milk into a small glass.
Hold a teaspoon over the milk and slowly pour 1 oz (30 ml) espresso over the back (convex side) of the spoon so it runs gently on top.
Serve showing the two layers, and stir before drinking.
verified_note: Recipe card uses 2:1 condensed milk to espresso (the article text mentions 1:1 as the usual ratio).

name: Café con Leche
steps: Make 4 oz (1/2 cup) strong coffee in a Moka pot, or pull an espresso shot.
Steam 4 oz (1/2 cup) whole milk with an espresso machine, stretching it to 20 to 25 percent in height. Or froth it with a frother, French press or whisk.
Pour the coffee into a cup and stir in 1 to 2 teaspoons sugar.
Add the steamed milk and serve immediately.
verified_note: Sugar (1 to 2 tsp, 1.5 used) mapped to simple_syrup. Page offers oat milk as a dairy-free option. Espresso 120 ml means 4 oz strong coffee (Moka pot or espresso).

name: Flat White
steps: Brew 36 g espresso.
Pour 120 ml cold milk into a clean pitcher, up to just below the spout.
Steam the milk adding only a small amount of air (usually a couple of seconds). It should be thin and glossy with no visible bubbles; steam to 60-65C (do not go above 70C).
Knock the pitcher gently on the counter and swirl the milk to remove large bubbles.
Starting low, pour the milk into the espresso at an angle, swirling gently to combine.
When the cup is about two-thirds full, bring the pitcher closer to the surface and keep pouring while straightening the cup.
verified_note: Espresso given as 36 g liquid, entered as 36 ml.

name: Apple Crisp Macchiato
steps: Make the apple syrup: combine 1 large diced Granny Smith apple, 1 cup apple cider, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup light brown sugar and 2 cinnamon sticks in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low and cook 10 minutes until the apples are tender and the sugar has dissolved.
Remove from the heat and let steep 15 minutes.
Strain through a fine mesh sieve, pressing on the apples to extract flavor. Refrigerate in an airtight container (makes enough for many drinks).
Pour 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk and 2 to 3 teaspoons of the apple syrup into a tall glass.
Fill the glass with ice and top with 1 shot freshly brewed espresso. Drizzle with extra syrup if you like.
For a hot drink, heat the milk and skip the ice.
verified_note: Homemade apple-cinnamon syrup mapped to simple_syrup (12 ml = 2 to 3 tsp). Page's main version is iced; hot version given as a tip. Our hot mug version is covered by the tip. Not included: Apple-cinnamon syrup (homemade)

name: Gingerbread Latte
steps: Make the gingerbread syrup (brown sugar syrup simmered 20 minutes with fresh ginger, allspice berries and cinnamon sticks; the page gives no amounts here).
Brew 2 shots (2 oz / 60 ml) espresso with an espresso machine, manual espresso maker, French press or moka pot.
Stir 1 tbsp gingerbread syrup into the espresso.
Steam or froth 4 oz (1/2 cup, 120 ml) whole or oat milk.
Pour the milk into the center of the espresso so a light foam sits on top.
Sprinkle with cinnamon if you like.
verified_note: Gingerbread syrup (linked recipe, amounts not on page) -> closest id brown_sugar_syrup, 1 tbsp. Syrup contains ginger, allspice, cinnamon. Not included: gingerbread syrup (exact recipe not on page)

name: Peppermint Mocha
steps: Heat 3/4 cup (180 ml) milk with 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder and 1/8 tsp peppermint extract in a saucepan until boiling, then remove from heat.
Froth the mixture with a milk frother or immersion blender.
Pour the peppermint chocolate mixture over 2 oz (60 ml) espresso (or 1 cup brewed coffee).
Top with whipped cream, crushed candy canes and/or chocolate shavings if you like.
garnish: whipped cream, crushed candy canes, chocolate shavings
verified_note: Sugar 3 tbsp -> simple_syrup:3tbsp. Peppermint extract 1/8 tsp has no id (mint is fresh leaves) so left unmapped. Not included: peppermint extract (1/8 tsp)

name: Pistachio Latte (Hot)
steps: Put 1 cup (240 ml) milk, 2 tbsp (30 g) pistachio butter (or pistachio cream) and 1 tbsp maple syrup (or other sweetener, if you want it sweet) in a saucepan. Stir, then heat over medium just until hot, about 150°F (65°C) on a cooking thermometer.
Turn off the heat and stir in 1/4 tsp pure vanilla extract.
Whisk or froth the milk mixture until small bubbles form.
Pour 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot espresso or strong brewed coffee into a mug. Once the milk foam settles, slowly pour the milk over the coffee, garnish and serve.
verified_note: Pistachio butter/cream mapped to nuts (30g). Vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup (closest). Page does not name a garnish; the page also has an iced variation (not used).

name: Billionaire's Latte
steps: Spoon 2 tablespoons caramel into your serving mug or glass to form a bottom layer.
Add 3 to 4 pieces of chocolate (dark, milk or white), either melted or whole; they will melt when the hot coffee is poured over them.
Prepare 1 shot of espresso and pour it into the glass.
Heat 120 ml whole milk, then froth it with a milk frother.
Pour the milk into the glass so the foam sits on top.
Sprinkle 1 crushed shortbread cookie over the top and serve immediately.
verified_note: 3-4 chocolate pieces approximated as chocolate_syrup:15 (about 15 g chocolate). Espresso shot taken as 30 ml. Shortbread has no id. Not included: Shortbread cookie, 1, crumbled

name: Eggnog Latte
steps: Pour 2 oz (60 ml) espresso into a mug.
Combine 1/2 cup (120 ml) eggnog and 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk in a milk steamer and steam them according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Pour the steamed eggnog-milk mixture into the mug and spoon the foam on top.
Optionally sprinkle with freshly grated nutmeg.
verified_note: Store-bought eggnog (1/2 cup / 120 ml) has no id and is left unmapped; closest approximation would be milk plus cream plus egg yolk but the page does not use those. Not included: eggnog (120 ml)

name: Ruby Chocolate Latte
steps: Heat water in a kettle (the page sets the kettle to 60°C). Put 1/2 tsp ground coffee (page: 1 tsp for 2 cups) in a cafetiere and pour in about 30 ml of the hot water (the author says 60 ml for the 2-cup batch; the amount is not on the recipe card).
Let the coffee brew for 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir with a wooden spoon and scoop off the grounds floating on top, then press the plunger all the way down.
Bring 175 ml whole milk to a gentle boil in a pan.
Add 35 g ruby chocolate to the milk and stir well until melted.
Pour the coffee into the chocolate milk and mix well. Serve hot in a glass.
verified_note: Ruby chocolate has no id; mapped to white_chocolate (closest, ruby is a pink cocoa-butter based chocolate). Brewed cafetiere coffee mapped to espresso:30. Water for brewing is not on the card; 60 ml for 2 cups comes from an author comment. Halved from 2 servings. Page also says it can be cooled and served over ice.

name: Coconut Milk Coffee (Hot)
steps: Pull a single shot of espresso, or brew strong coffee with a French press, moka pot or other maker.
Heat 1 cup (250 ml) unsweetened coconut milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until warm but not boiling, about 2 to 3 minutes (or microwave in 15-second intervals until warm and steaming).
Froth the milk until foamy and velvety with a steam wand, hand frother or a jar with a lid.
Pour the hot coffee into your cup and stir in 1 to 2 tsp sweetener.
Slowly pour the frothed milk over the coffee, holding back the foam with the back of a spoon, then spoon the foam on top.
Stir and drink.
verified_note: Page gives 'single shot' with no ml; 30 ml assumed as one standard shot. Sweetener 1-2 tsp -> maple_syrup 1.5tsp. Optional 1/2 tsp vanilla/coconut extract and nutmeg/cinnamon garnish skipped.

name: South Indian Filter Coffee
steps: Brew a strong decoction with ground filter coffee
Put sugar in the tumbler, add hot milk, then the decoction
Pour back and forth between tumbler and dabara 2 to 3 times to froth

name: Thai Spiced Iced Tea
steps: Bring 1 1/4 cups (about 295 ml) water to a boil in a small saucepan.

Remove from the heat and add about 1 1/8 tsp loose black or red Thai tea (or 1 1/2 tea bags), 1/2 star anise and 3/4 of a clove (about 1 clove and a piece of star anise is fine), keeping everything submerged. Steep for 10 minutes.
Strain out the tea, star anise and clove.
Stir in 1/2 tbsp sugar until fully dissolved, then let the tea cool to room temperature.
Fill a tall glass with ice and pour in the tea until it is about 3/4 full.
Add 1 tbsp sweetened condensed milk, stir and drink right away.
verified_note: Divided by 4. black_tea:295 is the brewed tea volume (water 5 cups / 4). Star anise (0.5) and cloves (0.75) both map to the clove id, so clove:0.75pcs covers the cloves and the star anise is mentioned in the steps. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page uses sweetened condensed milk, not evaporated milk.

name: Earl Grey Fog & Tonic
steps: Pour 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water over 1 tbsp loose-leaf Earl Grey tea and let it steep for 30 minutes.
Let the tea cool, then stir in 1 tsp fresh lemon juice.
Strain the tea into a tall glass filled with ice, filling it about half to three-quarters full.
Top with about 1/2 cup (120 ml) tonic water and stir. Use more tea than tonic or half and half, to taste.
verified_note: Page uses diet tonic; mapped to tonic. Page makes 2 servings (2 tbsp tea, 2 cups boiling water, 1 cup tonic, 2 tsp lemon juice), halved. Tea brewed amount counted as earl_grey:240.

name: Peach Rosemary Iced Tea
steps: Bring 1/2 cup (about 107 ml) water to a boil, remove from the heat, add about 1/4 of a tea bag (the page uses 2 bags per 9 cups) and 2/3 of a rosemary sprig, and steep 5 minutes. Remove the tea bag.
Stir in 1 tbsp sugar until dissolved and let the rosemary steep 15 more minutes. Remove the rosemary.
Pour the tea into a large glass or jar, add another 1/2 cup (about 107 ml) water and about 50 g (2 oz) sliced peaches (fresh or frozen), and cover.
Let it sit at room temperature for about 1 hour, then refrigerate so the peaches steep overnight (up to 5 days).
Serve over ice, garnished with a rosemary sprig.
verified_note: Divided by 9 (page: 8 cups water, 2 tea bags, 6 rosemary sprigs, 1 cup sugar, 1 lb peaches, makes about 9 cups). Brewed tea mapped to black_tea in ml (4 cups/9 = 107 ml); extra water 107 ml. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:1tbsp. Page gives no glass.

name: Matcha Vanilla Swirl
steps: Fill your serving glass with ice.
Blend 3 tbsp rolled oats, 1 tsp maple syrup, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, a pinch of sea salt and 3/4 cup (180 ml) filtered water on high for about 1 minute until smooth.
Pour this oat milk through a fine mesh strainer into the glass of ice, pressing the pulp with a spoon so all the liquid passes through.

Sift 1 tsp matcha into a small wide bowl. Add a little of 1/3 cup (80 ml) hot water that has been off the boil for about a minute and whisk hard until dissolved. Add the rest of the hot water and whisk again until frothy.
Pour the matcha over the iced oat milk and stir to combine.
verified_note: No page titled Matcha Vanilla Swirl was found; used this vanilla oat iced matcha latte as the closest real recipe. Homemade oat milk (oats plus water) mapped to oat_milk:180. Vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup (0.5 tsp); maple syrup 1 tsp. Oats and salt not listed as ids. Not included: rolled oats 3 tbsp (inside homemade oat milk), sea salt pinch

name: Matcha Island
steps: Add 2 oz (60 ml) Ritual Gin Alternative, 1 oz (30 ml) cream of coconut, 1/2 oz (15 ml) lemon juice and 1/2 tsp matcha powder to a shaker with ice and shake thoroughly.
Double-strain into a glass, then add ice.
verified_note: Cream of coconut (sweetened) mapped to coconut_milk. Glass type not given by page. This is a Ritual Gin Alternative recipe from a brand blog, no pineapple. Not included: Ritual Gin Alternative 60 ml (branded non-alcoholic gin)

name: Masala Chai
steps: Bring water to a gentle boil with the crushed whole spices and ginger
Add the tea leaves and simmer 1 to 2 minutes
Add milk and sugar, bring to a boil and simmer a minute, then strain into cups

name: Adrak Chai (Ginger Tea)
steps: Heat 150 ml water in a pot. Add about 4 g (roughly 1.5 tsp) peeled, grated fresh ginger and 1.5 tsp loose leaf black tea. Bring to a rolling boil, then simmer on medium heat 2 to 3 minutes until the chai turns dark. (Boil the ginger in water before adding milk or the milk can curdle.)
Add 90 ml whole milk and bring to a boil on medium-high heat. Reduce the heat and bring it to a boil again.
Reduce the heat completely. Stir in 1.5 tsp sugar, 1/8 tsp ground cardamom and 1/8 tsp ground black pepper (optional but recommended: a pinch, about 1/8 tsp, of dried ground ginger).
Mix well and aerate the tea with a ladle 4 to 5 times. Turn off the heat, cover the pot and let it rest 3 to 4 minutes.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.
verified_note: Page makes 2: halved. Page range for ginger is 3/4-1 tbsp (7-10 g) per 2 servings, so about 4 g each. Optional dried ground ginger has no separate id and is only in the steps. Loose tea given as 1 tbsp for 2, so 1.5 tsp each; black_tea id is brewed tea but used as dry leaf amount, as in our other chai.

name: Elaichi Chai (Cardamom Tea)
steps: Crush 1 tbsp whole cardamom with a pestle and mortar.
Add the crushed cardamom, 2 tsp loose black tea and 1/4 cup (60 ml) water to a milk pan.
Bring the water to a boil and let it reduce slightly.
Add 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk and 1 to 2 tsp sugar.
Boil the milk and let the tea cook for about 5 minutes.
Strain through a fine strainer into a cup and enjoy hot.
verified_note: Sugar 1-2 tsp mapped to simple_syrup:1.5tsp. Black tea is loose leaf (tsp), not brewed. Cardamom amount is 1 tbsp whole as written.

name: Doodh Patti Chai
steps: Put 360 ml (1.5 cups) whole milk in a pot with 2 lightly crushed cardamom pods and a very small piece of cinnamon (about 1 cm). Bring to a boil. (Tip: lay a heatproof spoon across the pot to stop it boiling over.)
Once the milk has boiled, aerate it with a ladle a few times.
Add about 1 tsp loose tea leaves (or 1 tea bag) and bring to a boil again.
Aerate a few times with a ladle and keep at an aggressive simmer for at least 5 minutes, until reduced by at least a third.
Strain and serve in a mug. (Sugar is listed on the page as 'to taste' with no amount or step.)
verified_note: Page's 1 serving is 2 cups (480 ml) milk with 1/2 tbsp tea and 3 pods; scaled to 3/4 (360 ml milk, about 3/8 tbsp tea, about 2 cardamom pods) to stay under 450 ml. Sugar is 'to taste' with no amount, so omitted from ings.

name: Karak Chai
steps: Boil 1 cup (240 ml) water in a saucepan.
Crush 2 to 3 cardamom pods (2.5 pods), about 1/4 inch of cinnamon bark and 1/2 tbsp grated ginger.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon, ginger and 1.5 tsp loose black tea to the water.
Bring to a boil, then add 1/2 cup (120 ml) evaporated milk (or whole milk).
Add 1 tsp sugar.
Bring to a rolling boil and boil for at least 3 to 4 minutes, until the tea is a dark caramel color and has thickened, then turn off the heat.
Strain through a tea strainer into a cup and serve.
verified_note: Page makes 2 cups (1 cup milk, 2 cups water, 3 tsp tea, 2 tsp sugar, 5 cardamom pods, 1/2 inch cinnamon bark, 1 tbsp ginger), halved. Cinnamon bark 1/4 inch approximated as 0.25tsp. No saffron in source.

name: Kesar Chai (Saffron Tea)
steps: Add 1 cup (240 ml) water and 5 saffron strands to a saucepan and bring to a brisk boil.
Once boiling, add 1/2 tsp tea leaves and simmer for about a minute, then turn off the heat.
Let the tea brew briefly so it stays light and does not turn bitter.
Stir in 2 tbsp (30 ml) milk and let it rest for a few seconds.
Strain into a cup, add a few more saffron strands on top and serve hot.
verified_note: Divided by 2. Page says 1 tsp tea leaves for 2; black_tea here is dry leaf (tsp), not brewed tea. Saffron 10 strands for 2 = 5 per cup, about 1 pinch.

name: Lemon Ginger Tea
steps: Remove 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water from the heat and add a 1/2 inch piece of ginger, thinly sliced, and 1/4 of a lemon, sliced.
Steep for about 20 minutes, then strain.
Serve warm (or pour over crushed ice for iced). Stir in honey if you like.
verified_note: Divided by 4. Ginger 2 inch piece = 0.5 inch, mapped as ginger:0.5pcs. Lemon is sliced into the tea, not juiced. Honey is optional with no amount given, so it is left out of ings. Page does not name a glass; mug is our assumption of a cup for warm tea.

name: Iced Chai Latte
steps: Make the concentrate: put 1 cup water, about 1 tsp chai spice blend (1.5 tbsp for 4 servings), 1 black tea bag and 1 tbsp maple syrup in a small saucepan and bring just to a boil.
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes, then remove the tea bag and strain.
To serve, fill a glass with ice, then combine 3/4 cup (180 ml) concentrate with 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk.
verified_note: Page makes 4 servings of homemade concentrate (4 cups water, 1.5 tbsp chai spices, 4 tea bags, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 cup milk); homemade concentrate mapped to chai_concentrate. Per-serving concentrate ingredient amounts divided by 4.

name: Chai Blossom Soda
steps: Put 1/2 chai tea bag in 60 ml (1/4 cup) boiling water in a small bowl, cover and steep 8 to 10 minutes. (The page makes 4 drinks from 2 tea bags and 1 cup boiling water, so scale up as needed.)
Add 2 tbsp sugar and stir until dissolved. Remove the tea bag and let the mixture cool.
Mix the cooled chai syrup with 30 ml (2 tbsp) fresh lime juice.
Fill a rocks glass with ice, add the chai-lime mixture, and top with 75 ml (2 to 3 oz) club soda.
Garnish with a star anise pod and a lemon twist.
verified_note: Page makes 4: divided by 4. Home-steeped chai tea syrup mapped to chai_concentrate; sugar to simple_syrup. Club soda 2-3 oz per glass (page: 8-12 oz for 4).

name: Classic Southern Sweet Tea
steps: Steep strong black tea and stir the sugar in while it is hot
Dilute with cool water and chill
Serve over ice

name: Chamomile Honey Iced Tea
steps: Bring water to a boil and let it rest about 60 seconds (about 90 C / 195 F). Pour 120 ml over 1 chamomile tea bag (the page uses 4 to 5 bags per quart) and steep 7 to 10 minutes.
While the tea is still warm, stir in 3/4 to 1 tbsp honey until fully dissolved.
Stir in about 1/4 tsp lemon juice.
Add 120 ml cold water, pour into a glass or small carafe and refrigerate until cold.
Pour over ice. For a fizzy version, add a splash of sparkling water.
garnish: fresh lavender or a slice of green apple (optional)
verified_note: Page makes 1 quart (about 950 ml); divided by 4 for a single glass. Brewed chamomile mapped to chamomile_tea (120 ml hot brew) plus 120 ml cold water. Lemon juice 1/4 tsp is about 1 ml.

name: Masala Shikanji
steps: Roll a large lemon on a hard counter, pressing firmly with your palm, then cut and juice it to get about 30 ml (2 tbsp) juice.

Make the shikanji masala for one glass: mix 1/8 tsp black salt, 1/8 tsp rock salt, 1/3 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/8 tsp black pepper, 1/8 tsp chaat masala and about 1/6 tsp dried mint powder (about 1 tsp in total).
In a glass, stir the 30 ml lemon juice with 2.5 tbsp sugar (or honey) and the 1 tsp masala until the sugar dissolves.
Optional: rim the serving glass by dipping it in lemon juice and then in shikanji masala or brown sugar.
Lightly crush a few mint leaves (about 4) with a mortar and pestle.
Fill a tall glass with ice, add 1 or 2 lemon slices and the crushed mint.
Pour in the lemon base, top with chilled water or chilled soda (about 150 ml), stir well and serve immediately.
verified_note: Source makes 4 glasses; divided by 4 (1/2 cup lemon juice, 10 tbsp sugar, 4 tsp masala, amounts for the whole batch). Rock salt and black salt combined into black_salt. Dried mint powder (about 1/6 tsp) folded into fresh mint leaves. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page gives no volume for the top-up water or soda, 150 ml is an estimate to fill a tall glass. The page's note that the base is only 2-3 tbsp per glass conflicts with its ingredient quantities; the ingredient quantities were used.

name: Nimbu Pani
steps: Squeeze the lemon into cold water
Add sugar, black salt, roasted cumin and chaat masala
Stir until the sugar dissolves, then taste and adjust

name: Jaljeera
steps: Make the jaljeera powder once and keep it (batch): dry-roast 2 tbsp cumin on low heat until aromatic and golden brown, then add 2 tsp pepper and roast on low until aromatic.

Cool the roasted spices completely and put them in a grinder jar. Add 2 tbsp black salt, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp ginger powder, 2 tbsp amchur (dry mango powder) and 2 tbsp sugar, and grind to a fine powder.
For one glass, grind 1.5 tbsp mint, 1 tbsp coriander leaves and 3/8 tsp of the jaljeera powder to a fine paste.
Put a few ice cubes in a tall glass and pour the paste over them.
Add ice-cold water (or soda) to fill the glass, about 200 ml, and a lemon slice.
Garnish with mint and serve. Skip the ice if you have a cold or sore throat.
verified_note: Page: 3 tbsp mint, 2 tbsp coriander, 3/4 tsp jaljeera powder for 2 servings, divided by 2. 3/8 tsp powder is mostly cumin, black salt and amchur (about 1/12 tsp each), written as pinches; pepper, ginger and sugar in the powder are trace. Page gives no amount for the water or soda; 200 ml is an assumption for a tall glass. Lemon slices mapped to lemon:1pcs.

name: Jeera Pani Soda
steps: Make the pre-mix once (batch): dry-roast 1/4 cup jeera (cumin) and 1 tsp black peppercorns, cool, and grind to a very fine powder.
Mix in 1 tbsp dry ginger powder, 1 tbsp chaat masala and 1 tbsp black salt. Store in a clean dry bottle in the fridge for up to a month.
For one 6 oz (180 ml) glass, put 3/4 tsp of the pre-mix and 1 tsp lime juice in the glass, with ice if you like.
Top with about 170 ml chilled club soda and stir.
verified_note: Page uses 3/4 tsp pre-mix per 180 ml glass; the pre-mix (about 22 tsp total) is 12 tsp cumin, 1 tsp pepper, 3 tsp dry ginger, 3 tsp black salt, 3 tsp chaat masala, so per glass about 0.41 tsp cumin, 0.03 tsp pepper and 0.1 tsp each of the others. Dry ginger powder mapped to ginger. Soda 170 ml fills the glass to 180 ml. Ice optional on the page.

name: Masala Soda
steps: Blend 2 tbsp packed mint leaves, 1/4 tsp chopped ginger, 1/2 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar, 1/4 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3/4 tsp chaat masala, 1/8 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp black salt and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Pass the mixture through a fine mesh strainer.
Pour 4 to 5 tbsp of the strained mixture into a tall glass.
Add a few ice cubes.
Top with chilled club soda (about 150 ml), stir gently, garnish with a lime slice and mint leaves, and serve immediately.
verified_note: Source makes 4 glasses from one blended concentrate, divided by 4. A blender will need a larger batch in practice (multiply amounts, use 4-5 tbsp of concentrate per glass). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Club soda is 'as required'; 150 ml is an estimate. Lime juice 2 tbsp / 4 = 0.5 tbsp.

name: Aam Panna
steps: Cook the raw mango in a little water until soft
Blend with sugar or jaggery and mint, then strain
Stir in cumin, black salt and pepper
Dilute the concentrate with cold water and serve chilled

name: Kokum Sharbat
steps: Put the kokum concentrate (kokum cooked with sugar, cumin, cardamom and black salt) in a glass
Top with chilled water or soda
Add a few ice cubes and garnish with mint

name: Sol Kadhi
steps: Rinse 2 dried kokum lightly, place in a bowl with about 40 ml (3 tbsp) water and soak for 30 minutes.
Crush and squeeze the kokum in the water with your fingers, then strain, pressing the shreds with a spoon to extract all the flavor.
Add about 80 ml (1/3 cup) water to the kokum extract, then stir in about 50 ml (3 tbsp) thick coconut milk and salt to taste.
For the tempering, heat about 1/4 tsp neutral oil in a small pan on low heat. Add a pinch of mustard seeds and let them crackle, then a pinch of cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add 1 to 2 curry leaves, a small piece of dry Kashmiri chili (seeds removed), half a small crushed garlic clove and a pinch of asafoetida. Fry, stirring often, until the garlic is light golden.
Quickly pour the tempering over the kokum and coconut milk mixture and mix well. Stir in 1 tsp chopped coriander.
Serve right away, or chill for a few hours, in a small glass or bowl. Do not leave it at room temperature as the coconut milk can turn rancid. Garnish with coriander.
verified_note: Page gives no servings; whole batch is 12 kokum, 3 cups water, 1 to 1.5 cups thick coconut milk and I divided by 6 to get a small glass of about 170 ml (my assumption). Salt is 'as required'. Tempering uses mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, chili, garlic, hing mapped approximately; oil and curry leaves are not mapped. Not included: neutral oil (about 1/4 tsp), curry leaves (1 to 2)

name: Rooh Afza Sharbat
steps: Soak the sabja seeds in water for 30 minutes and drain
Stir the Rooh Afza syrup into cold water
Add the soaked seeds and ice, and stir well

name: Mango Cardamom Lassi
steps: Add 1/2 cup (120 g) canned sweetened mango pulp (or 3/4 cup / 140 g chopped ripe sweet mango, chilled, peeled and cubed), 3/8 cup (88 g) cold plain yogurt, 90 ml (3/8 cup) cold milk, 3/4 to 1.5 tbsp sugar and 1/8 tsp cardamom powder to a blender jar.
Blend until super smooth; the texture should be thick but still pourable.
Taste and adjust: add more sugar for sweetness, or more milk or ice to thin it.
Pour into a glass. For a colder drink refrigerate for 1 hour.
Garnish with a few sliced pistachios or a pinch of saffron (optional).
verified_note: Page uses 1.5 cups (280 g) chopped mango or 1 cup (240 g) canned pulp for 2 servings. Sugar (18-36 g for 2) mapped to simple_syrup at 1 tbsp; cardamom powder is marked optional on the page. Page says milk may be replaced with water or ice.

name: Sweet Lassi
steps: Blend chilled yogurt, sugar, cardamom and rose water
Add chilled water and blend until smooth and frothy

name: Rose Cardamom Lassi
steps: Add 1 cup (240 ml) plain yogurt to a blender jar.
Add 1/4 tsp ground cardamom, a small pinch of salt (1/16 tsp), 1 tbsp rose syrup, 1/2 tbsp sugar and 3 ice cubes.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.
Pour into a glass, garnish with 1/2 tsp edible dried rose petals and serve.
verified_note: Sugar mapped to simple_syrup (0.5tbsp); salt mapped to black_salt; ice omitted.

name: Salted Mint Lassi
steps: Blend 1/8 cup mint leaves with 1 tbsp of the yogurt to a paste.
Add the remaining yogurt (about 1 cup total), 1/2 tsp ginger juice, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp black salt and 1/2 cup (120 ml) water.
Blend until just smooth; stop there since over-blending makes it frothy.
Pour over 1/4 cup ice cubes, sprinkle with a little roasted cumin powder (1/16 tsp) and a few mint leaves and serve.
garnish: mint leaves and roasted cumin powder
verified_note: Salt 1/4 tsp plus black salt 1/8 tsp combined into black_salt:0.38tsp. Ginger juice mapped to ginger. Roasted cumin powder 1/16 tsp.

name: Cardamom Banana Lassi
steps: Blend 2 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 1 ripe peeled banana, a splash of cold milk and a handful of ice cubes until smooth. Add sugar to taste only if needed.
Pour into a tumbler and sprinkle with cardamom powder.
verified_note: Source makes 2 (2 bananas, 4 tbsp Greek yoghurt), halved. 'Splash of cold milk', ice and sugar have no amounts on the page so milk and sugar left out of ings. 'Sprinkle of cardamom' mapped to 1 pinch. Greek yoghurt mapped to yogurt.

name: Melon Lassi
steps: Blend 1/8 of a melon (chopped, about 100 g), 1 tbsp Greek yoghurt and 1/2 tsp sugar (or to taste) until smooth.
Crush some ice and put it in a tumbler.
Pour the blended mixture over the ice.
verified_note: Source makes 4 from 1/2 melon, 4 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 2 tsp sugar; divided by 4.
