steps: Make the syrup first (this is a batch that keeps up to 6 months in the fridge): heat 1/2 cup water in a small pan, and when it boils add 1 g saffron strands. Remove from heat and rest for 30 minutes.

In a large pan combine 1 liter water, 5 cups sugar and 3 tbsp fresh lime juice. Heat on medium-high, stirring often, until it boils. Lower the heat and cook 6-8 minutes, then strain through a fine-mesh strainer.
Stir in the saffron water, 2 tbsp edible-grade sandalwood (chandan) powder and 1 tsp citric acid until well mixed. Pour into a clean glass bottle and refrigerate.
For one serving: shake the bottle well, add 1 tbsp of the syrup to a glass and top with about 200 ml chilled water.
Add a few ice cubes and serve chilled.
verified_note: Page is a syrup recipe; per-glass instruction is 1 tbsp syrup topped with chilled water. Homemade kesar-chandan syrup mapped to simple_syrup. Amount of chilled water per glass is not stated; 200 ml assumed to fill a glass. Syrup steps are given as the page's batch amounts because they cannot be reduced to one glass. Not included: edible sandalwood powder (2 tbsp per batch), saffron (1 g per batch), citric acid (1 tsp per batch)

name: Mogra (Jasmine) Nectar Sharbat
steps: Concentrate (made ahead in a batch, keeps up to a month in the fridge): in a saucepan on medium heat combine 1 1/2 cups sugar and 3/4 cup water, bring to a rolling boil, lower the heat and stir in 1 teaspoon milk.
Skim off the impurities that float to the top with a tea strainer and discard them.
Add 1/4 teaspoon cardamom powder, a few saffron strands and 3/4 cup fresh jasmine buds.
Bring to a rolling boil again, switch off the heat and let it cool to room temperature.
Cover the pan and leave it for about 24 hours so the jasmine flavour infuses the syrup.
Strain out and discard the jasmine buds, then pour the syrup into a bottle and refrigerate.
To serve: put 1 tablespoon of the concentrate in a glass, add a few ice cubes and top with 200 ml water.
verified_note: The jasmine concentrate (sugar, cardamom, saffron, jasmine buds) is mapped to simple_syrup:1tbsp; no jasmine or batch ingredients are in the ingredient list. Not included: jasmine bud concentrate (batch)

name: Brahmi Cooling Tonic
steps: Blend 1/3 cup brahmi leaves with 1/3 tsp roasted cumin powder, a small pinch of black salt and a small pinch of freshly ground black pepper into a fine paste.
Add 2/3 tsp honey and 160 ml (2/3 cup) water, then mix well.
Serve chilled.
verified_note: Source makes 3 glasses (1 cup brahmi leaves, 1 tsp roasted cumin, a pinch black salt, a pinch black pepper, 2 tsp honey, 2 cups water), divided by 3; pinches scaled to 0.33. Brahmi leaves mapped to herbal_leaf. Page names no glass and does not mention ice.

name: Shankhpushpi Herbal Elixir
steps: Stir shankhpushpi extract, lemon juice, and rock sugar syrup.
Add ice to glass.
Fill with cold water and stir thoroughly.

name: Parijat (Night Jasmine) Infusion
steps: Steep parijat petals in warm water, strain and chill.
Mix chilled tea with honey and lime juice.
Serve over ice cubes.

name: Curry Leaf & Lemon Tonic
steps: Wash 5 to 7 fresh curry leaves and pat them dry with a kitchen towel, then chop them.
In a shaker bottle, add the chopped curry leaves and 2 to 3 fresh lime wedges.
Add 4 tsp lime juice and 3 tbsp simple sugar syrup (or adjust to taste).
Add plenty of ice cubes and shake vigorously.
Transfer the mixture into a glass and serve.
verified_note: Curry leaves mapped to mustard_seed (the 'mustard / curry leaf tempering' id) at 6 leaves. Page uses lime (not lemon); lime_juice and lime wedges used. Page also lists 'chilled water as required' but gives no amount or step for it, so water is left out of ings. Black salt not in page.

name: Tulsi Ginger Honey Tonic
steps: Muddle tulsi leaves with ginger juice and honey.
Pour cold or warm water and stir until honey dissolves.
Strain and serve with a tulsi leaf float.

name: Hibiscus (Gudhal) Ruby Sharbat
steps: Put about 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp of dried hibiscus petals and 240 ml (1 cup) water in a saucepan.
Boil until the petals turn white and the water turns ruby red.
While it heats, soak 1 tsp basil (sabja) seeds in a little cold water in a small bowl until they bloom.
Turn off the heat and let the hibiscus liquid cool completely.
Strain out the petals, then stir in about 1.3 tbsp (20 ml) rose syrup.
Stir in the bloomed basil seeds.
Pour into a glass, top with ice and fresh mint.
verified_note: Page: 1/4 cup dried hibiscus + 3 cups water + 4 tbsp rose syrup + 1 tbsp basil seeds for 3 servings; divided by 3. hibiscus_tea:240 is the brewed liquid from about 1.3 tbsp dried petals in 240 ml water. Basil seeds mapped to sabja. Mint garnish only. Ice skipped.

name: Vetiver Rose Herbal Cooler
steps: Layer khus syrup and rose syrup in glass with ice.
Add lemon juice and chilled water.
Stir to create a dual-tone botanical beverage.

name: Saunf Mishri Wellness Water
steps: Grind 2 tbsp saunf (fennel seeds), 2 tbsp mishri (rock sugar) and 5 black peppercorns into a fine powder.
In a glass, mix the powder with 1 cup cold water.
Add 1 tsp black salt and stir well.
Add 4 ice cubes and garnish with 4 sprigs of mint leaves. Serve chilled.
verified_note: Mishri (rock sugar) mapped to simple_syrup (sugar); peppercorns and mint sprigs counted as pcs. Page does not name a glass type.

name: Lemongrass Ginger Iced Tonic
steps: Cut about 1/6 of a lemongrass stalk into 2-inch pieces and crush them with the flat side of a knife. Peel and thinly slice about 1/6 of a two-thumb-sized piece of ginger.
In a saucepan over high heat bring 1 1/3 cups (320 ml) water, the lemongrass, ginger and about 1 tbsp sugar to a boil.
Remove from heat and add 1 to 2 green tea bags (or about 1/2 tbsp loose green tea in a removable container). Steep about 1 minute, or until it tastes right to you.
Remove the tea, then let the mixture sit for about 30 minutes.
Pour through a fine-mesh sieve into a pitcher or jar.
Refrigerate until cool, about a couple of hours.
Pour over ice and top with a mint sprig.
verified_note: Page batch: 8 cups water, 1 stalk lemongrass, ginger piece the size of two thumbs, 1/3 cup sugar (or 1/4 cup agave), 10 green tea bags (or 3 heaping tbsp loose); divided by 6. Brewed tea mapped to green_tea:320; sugar to simple_syrup; lemongrass and ginger given as fractions of a stalk/piece (pcs). Page has no 'tonic' recipe; this is the closest lemongrass-ginger iced drink with exact quantities.

name: Badian (Star Anise) Herbal Fizz
steps: Add star anise syrup and fresh lemon juice to glass.
Fill with ice cubes.
Top with club soda; garnish with floating star anise pod.

name: Bael Leaves Digestive Tea
steps: Boil bael leaves in water for 5 minutes; strain.
Stir in jaggery and cumin powder.
Serve warm or chilled over ice.

name: Arjun Bark Cardiac Tonic
steps: Boil about 100 ml (half a glass) water for 1 minute on a low flame.
Add the crushed ginger, 1 crushed cardamom pod, 1 clove and 1/2 tsp Arjuna bark powder. Let it steep for 4-5 minutes so the spices infuse.
Pour in about 100 ml milk and leave it undisturbed for 2-3 minutes, or longer until the color turns brownish.
Strain the tea.
Sweeten with mishri or powdered jaggery to taste (can also be added while brewing) and serve.
verified_note: Page serves 2 using '1 glass of water, 1 glass of milk' (glass size not stated; assumed about 200 ml, so 100 ml each per serving), '1/4 ginger' (no unit given, halved to 0.125 pcs), 1-2 cardamom pods and 1-2 cloves (used 1 each), 1 tsp arjuna powder (halved, mapped to ginseng id as herbal root). Sweetener amount not given ('as per taste'); jaggery:1tsp is a placeholder.

name: Mulethi (Licorice) Root Tonic
steps: Bring 240 ml water to a boil.
Add about 1/2 inch of licorice (mulethi) root and simmer for a few minutes.
Strain into a cup.
Once the tea is warm, add a slice of lime and sip.
verified_note: Original 1 inch root, 2 cups water, few lime slices, halved. Licorice root mapped to ginseng (herbal root). 'lime:1pcs' = one slice/wedge. Not included: licorice (mulethi) root

name: Neem Honey Detox
steps: Muddle tender neem leaves into fine paste with lemon juice.
Whisk with honey and water until blended.
Strain through fine mesh before drinking.

name: Kanji (Fermented Black Carrot Drink)
steps: Page makes 2 litres at once; for one 250 ml glass use 25 g red or orange carrot, 6 g beetroot, 0.6 tsp yellow mustard seeds ground coarsely, 0.5 tsp salt, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.12 tsp red chili powder and 250 ml filtered water.
Peel the carrots and cut into 1/4-inch-thick, 1-inch-long batons. Peel the beetroot and cut into thin wedges.
Boil the water and switch off the heat as soon as it boils. Add the carrots and beetroot, cover and let sit for 10 minutes.
Remove the lid, add the salt, turmeric, chili powder and ground mustard and stir well.
Transfer to a sterilised jar (boiled 10 minutes and air-dried) and cover the mouth with muslin tied with twine.
Ferment in sunlight for 2 to 5 days (about 2 in sunny weather, up to 5 in mild weather), stirring once or twice a day with a clean dry spoon and keeping the jar in shade at night.
It is ready when pleasantly tart and salty with slight fizz. Refrigerate immediately, discard if green mold appears, and serve chilled in a small glass with 2 to 3 pieces of carrot and beetroot.
verified_note: Page makes 8 servings; divided by 8. Page uses red or orange carrots plus beetroot (not black carrots). Beetroot mapped to beetroot id (juice) in g. Salt mapped to black_salt. Mustard seeds mapped to mustard_seed. Fermenting a single glass is impractical; a larger batch is more realistic. Not included: red or orange carrot (25 g)

name: Beetroot Masala Chaas
steps: Optional: wrap washed beets in foil and roast at 425F for 20-25 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then cool, peel and cube. You need about 2.7 tbsp (1/6 cup) cubed beetroot for one glass.
Whisk about 1/3 cup (80 ml) yogurt in a bowl until smooth.
Whisk in 180 ml water, then add 1/6 tsp black salt, 1/12 tsp chaat masala and regular salt to taste.
Grind the cubed beetroot with about 0.5 g (a thin slice) fresh ginger, 1/3 of a green chili and 2 curry leaves, without adding water, into a paste.
Mix the paste into the yogurt-water mixture, cover and refrigerate for 1-2 hours so the flavors blend.
Strain the mixture until smooth.
Optional tempering: heat a tiny amount of oil (about 1/6 tsp) in a pan, add about 1/12 tsp mustard seeds and let them pop, then stir into the buttermilk.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve chilled.
verified_note: Source makes 3 servings, everything divided by 3. 'Beetroot' id is beetroot juice but used for 2 small cubed beets (1/2 cup cubed per 3 servings). Mustard seeds and curry leaves (about 2 leaves) both mapped to mustard_seed. Cilantro garnish has no stated amount so left out of ings. Glass not stated on page. Not included: oil (1/6 tsp, optional tempering), curry leaves (about 2, folded into mustard_seed)

name: Cucumber Mint Chaas
steps: Blend curd, cucumber, mint leaves, water, and seasonings.
Strain through coarse sieve to remove fibers.
Serve over ice with a pinch of cumin on top.

name: Dhungar (Smoked) Masala Chaas Coal
steps: Add 2/3 cup (160 ml) chilled curd to a blender.
Add about 3 mint leaves, a 1/3-inch piece of ginger, 1/4 tsp cumin powder, a scant 1/4 tsp crushed pepper (1/6 tsp) and 1/6 tsp salt.
Add 1/3 cup (80 ml) chilled water and blend until thick and frothy.
Pour into a serving vessel and place a small cup in the centre. Set 1 small piece of red-hot charcoal in the cup (the page uses 2 pieces for 3 servings).
Sprinkle a small pinch of whole cumin (about 1/12 tsp) over the charcoal and pour a few drops of ghee (about 1/12 tsp) on top.
Cover with aluminium foil and let it rest for 2-3 minutes so the smoky aroma infuses into the chaas.
Serve with a few ice cubes and garnish with mint leaves.
verified_note: Divided by 3. Ginger 1 inch / 3 = 0.33 inch piece, mapped as 0.33pcs. cumin id combines 1/4 tsp powder plus 1/12 tsp whole seeds (0.33tsp). Salt mapped to black_salt (sea salt). Plain curd + water used instead of ready buttermilk. Ghee and charcoal are not in the id list. Not included: ghee (about 1/12 tsp), red-hot charcoal (1 small piece)

name: Roasted Garlic Chaas
steps: Mash roasted garlic cloves into a smooth paste.
Whisk garlic paste into curd, cold water, cumin, and salt.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve cold.

name: Peach Elaichi Lassi Blended
steps: Chop 1 large yellow peach roughly and discard the stone.
Blend the peach flesh with the seeds of 5 crushed cardamom pods (or ground cardamom), 1 tsp honey and a pinch (1/8 tsp) of salt until smooth.
Add 1/2 cup (125 ml) Greek yoghurt and 1/2 cup (125 ml) cold milk and blend again until frothy.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.
verified_note: Page serves 2 (2 peaches, 10 cardamom pods, 2 tsp honey, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 cup yoghurt, 1 cup milk); halved. Greek yoghurt mapped to yogurt, salt to black_salt. The ingredient list mentions a handful of ice cubes but the method does not use them, so ice is left out.

name: Pineapple Mint Lassi Blended
steps: Grind 1/4 tsp cumin seeds to a fine powder with a mortar and pestle or in a blender (a pinch of coarse salt helps in a mortar).
Blend 1/2 cup cubed fresh pineapple, 100 ml yogurt, the cumin powder, 3 mint leaves and salt to taste until smooth.
Taste and adjust salt or cumin; if too thick, add a little water and blend again.
Put ice cubes in a glass and pour the lassi over them.
verified_note: Page: 1 cup pineapple, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 200 ml yogurt, 5-6 mint leaves, salt to taste. Servings are not stated, so halved on the assumption of two glasses. Cumin seeds mapped to cumin; salt to black_salt:1pinch.

name: Guava Red Chili Lassi Blended
steps: Blend guava pulp, yogurt, sugar, and cumin until smooth.
Pour into glass.
Dust tiny pinch of red chili powder on top before serving.

name: Kesar Badam Lassi Rich
steps: Warm 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the milk in the microwave for about 45 seconds and divide it between two small bowls.
Soak a pinch of saffron in one bowl and 3 to 4 almonds in the other for about 15 minutes.
Add the soaked saffron milk and almond milk, the rest of the milk (60 ml), 1/2 cup whipped yogurt, 1 tbsp sugar and an optional pinch of cardamom to a blender and blend until smooth.
Sieve the mixture into a glass and serve right away.
verified_note: Page serves 2 (1 cup milk, 1 cup yogurt, generous pinch saffron, 6-8 almonds, 2 tbsp sugar, optional cardamom); divided by 2. The 1/2 cup milk warmed in the page is assumed to come out of the 1 cup total. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup in tbsp.

name: Blueberry Cardamom Lassi Blended
steps: Add 50 g blueberries to the blender jar and blend alone for 10-15 seconds to break them down.
Add 1/2 cup (120 ml) cold full-fat yogurt, 2 tbsp (30 ml) cold full-fat milk, 1 tbsp sugar or honey, 1/8 tsp cardamom powder and optionally 1/8 tsp rose water. Place 1-2 ice cubes on top.
Blend on high for 45-60 seconds until smooth and frothy. The drink should turn a deep purple-violet.
Taste and adjust: add more sweetener if needed, or a splash of milk for a thinner drink, and blend briefly again.
Pour into a tall chilled glass (freeze the glass about 10 minutes beforehand). Top with a few fresh blueberries and a pinch of cardamom. Serve right away.
garnish: fresh blueberries and a pinch of cardamom
verified_note: Source makes 2 servings (100 g blueberries, 1 cup yogurt, 1/4 cup milk, 2 tbsp sugar or honey, 1/4 tsp cardamom, 1/4 tsp rose water), halved. Blueberries mapped to berries. Honey chosen from 'sugar (or honey)'. Ice (2-3 cubes) skipped.

name: Avocado Honey Lassi
steps: Blend 1/2 avocado, 1/2 cup plain yogurt, 1.5 tbsp honey, 1/2 tsp lime juice, 1/2 cup milk (more or less for the thickness you like) and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Add 1.5 tbsp dry fruits or nuts of your choice (almonds, cashews, pistachios, sultanas; soaking overnight is optional) and pulse briefly so they are coarsely mixed in.
Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Pour into a tall glass and garnish with a cherry.
verified_note: Page serves 2, all halved; cup taken as 240 ml (120 ml each for yogurt and milk). Mixed dry fruits/nuts mapped to nuts. Salt mapped to black_salt. Page does not say whether served iced; marked cold.

name: Banana Elaichi Lassi
steps: Add 1/2 cup (125 ml) yogurt, 1 chopped banana, about 1 3/4 tbsp sugar, a small pinch (1/16 tsp) cardamom powder and about 80 ml chilled water to a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy. For a thinner drink add a little more water while blending.
Pour into a glass and add ice cubes.
Garnish with chopped pistachios or almonds if you like, and serve cold (you can chill it in the refrigerator first).
verified_note: Source (1 cup yogurt, 2 large bananas, 3-4 tbsp sugar, 1/8 tsp cardamom, 1/2-3/4 cup chilled water) halved; 1 cup = 250 ml; mid-range sugar and water used. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Rose Sabja Lassi Seed
steps: Churn yogurt, rose syrup, sugar, and milk until smooth.
Stir in soaked sabja seeds.
Pour into tall glass and garnish with edible rose petals.

name: Muskmelon (Kharbuja) Lassi Blended
steps: Put 3/4 cup muskmelon (cantaloupe) chunks, 1/2 cup (120 ml) plain yogurt and about 2/3 tablespoon honey or sugar in a blender.
Blend on high speed until smooth.
Serve over ice cubes, garnished with almonds if you like.
verified_note: Original 3 cups melon, 2 cups yogurt, 2-3 tbsp honey or sugar for 2-4 servings; divided by 4 (midpoint amounts would exceed 450 ml). No melon id exists, so muskmelon mapped to watermelon (closest melon). Sweetener mapped to honey. Not included: muskmelon / cantaloupe (mapped to watermelon)

name: Apple Cinnamon Lassi Blended
steps: Peel and chop 1 apple into small pieces.
In a blender, add the chopped apple, 1/2 cup yogurt, 1 tbsp sugar, 0.13 tsp (a small pinch) cardamom powder and a few ice cubes.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a glass, garnish with a sprinkle of cardamom powder and serve chilled.
verified_note: Page is a plain apple lassi flavored with cardamom, not cinnamon; no published apple cinnamon yogurt lassi with exact amounts was found. 1/2 cup yogurt taken as 120 ml. Sugar 1 tbsp mapped to simple_syrup. Ice skipped.

name: Saffron Honey Lassi
steps: In a skillet over low heat, crumble 1/8 tsp saffron threads into 30 ml (2 tbsp) water and let stand 5 minutes.
Add 3 tbsp honey and stir until dissolved.
Add 3/4 cup (180 ml) Greek yogurt and 60 ml milk, then whisk together.
Refrigerate for 1 hour or until very cold, then pour into a glass and serve.
verified_note: Salt pinch mapped to black_salt. Source makes 1 batch divided between 2 glasses; amounts halved. Greek yogurt mapped to yogurt.

name: Tender Coconut Lassi Blended Curd
steps: Add 1/4 cup (about 60 g) curd, 1/4 cup grated fresh coconut, 2 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp chopped mint (pudina) and 3/4 cup (about 155 ml) coconut water to a blender.
Blend to a smooth consistency.
Optionally add black sesame seeds (the page gives no amount).
Serve chilled.
verified_note: Grated fresh coconut mapped to tender_coconut:0.25cup. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:2tsp. Black sesame seeds optional, no amount, skipped.

name: Spiced Hing Mattha
steps: Add about 1/3 cup (80 ml) plain yogurt to a bowl and pour in 2/3 cup (160 ml) chilled water. Blend or whisk until smooth and frothy.
Add 1/6 tsp roasted cumin powder, a tiny pinch (about 1/12 tsp) of minced ginger, about 1/12 tsp black salt, 2 tsp chopped mint or coriander leaves and a pinch of asafoetida (hing, optional).
Blend again for a few seconds until combined.
Pour into a glass, garnish with a little extra cumin and chopped herbs, and serve immediately while chilled.
verified_note: Whole page recipe is 2 cups yogurt, 4 cups water, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp minced ginger, 1/2 tsp black salt, 1/4 cup mint or coriander, 1 pinch hing (optional); divided by 6 (page says 6 cups). The pinch of hing is not divided. The page does not say when to add the hing.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Pune Mango Mastani Layered Shake &
steps: Slice about 5 mixed pistachios, almonds and cashews in total and set aside with a glazed cherry.

Blend about 1/2 cup thick mango pulp (or chopped ripe mango, about 180 g) with about 90 ml (6 tbsp) cold whole milk and 2 tsp sugar until smooth and thick. Taste and skip or add sugar depending on the mango.
Reserve 2 to 3 tsp chopped mango for topping.
Pour the shake into a tall glass, leaving room at the top for ice cream.
Add 1 to 2 scoops vanilla or mango ice cream.
Top with the chopped nuts and reserved mango and garnish with the cherry. Serve immediately with a spoon and straw.
garnish: sliced pistachios, almonds, cashews, glazed cherry
verified_note: Divided by 4. Nut mix mapped to nuts (6-7 each of 3 types per 4 servings = about 5 per glass). Cherry is garnish only; our cherry_juice has no basis in the page. Mango pulp = 2 to 2.5 cups / 4.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Dry Fruit Mastani Nut Shake
steps: Pour blended nut shake into glass.
Add ice cream scoop on top.
Decorate generously with sliced figs, dates, and almonds.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Strawberry Mastani Layered
steps: Pour fresh strawberry shake into glass.
Crown with strawberry ice cream scoop.
Garnish with chopped strawberries and slivered nuts.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Thandai Rose Milkshake Blended
steps: Pour 3/4 cup (180 ml) chilled milk into a blender jar.
Add 1 tbsp thandai powder, 3/4 tbsp sugar, 3/4 tsp rose water, 1 tbsp cream and 1 to 2 ice cubes.
Blend until frothy.
Pour into a glass and garnish with dry rose petals, sliced nuts and saffron strands. Serve chilled.
garnish: dry rose petals, sliced nuts, saffron strands
verified_note: Page lists 1.5 cups milk, 2 tbsp cream, 1.5 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp thandai powder, 1.5 tsp rose water, 2-3 ice cubes for 2 glasses. Cream 1 tbsp = 15 ml. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Ice skipped. No rose syrup used. Not included: thandai powder 1tbsp

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Rabri Falooda Glass Layered
steps: Layer sabja, rose syrup, and falooda sev in glass.
Add cold milk, then pour thick rabri over top.
Garnish with pistachios and almonds; serve with spoon.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Pistachio Kesar Doodh Simmered
steps: Blend about 1/4 cup of the blanched, peeled pistachios with a little of the milk into a coarse paste. Cut the remaining pistachios (about 2 tbsp) into thin strips.
Bring 300 ml (1 1/4 cups) milk to a boil in a pan. Lower the heat and simmer until it reduces slightly.
Stir in the pistachio paste and cook until the mixture thickens further.
Stir in 1/4 cup sugar until it dissolves, then mix in 1/2 tsp green cardamom powder.
Serve with the pistachio strips on top.
verified_note: Page has no saffron, glass or temperature; hot assumed because the milk is cooked. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup as 0.25cup sugar. Pistachios 1.5 cups/4 = 0.375 cup, split paste and strips.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Badam Halwa Milkshake Blended
steps: Blend almond halwa into chilled milk with cardamom.
Blend until thick and completely combined.
Garnish with saffron and serve chilled.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Khajoor (Date) Nut Milkshake Blended
steps: Add 3/4 cup (180 ml) chilled whole milk, 1/4 cup chopped seedless dates, 1/2 of a large banana (peeled, sliced and frozen), 1/2 tsp honey and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract to a high-speed blender.
Blend until smooth.
Taste and add a little more sweetener if needed.
Pour into a glass and serve chilled. Optionally add a few ice cubes for an extra-cold, iced version.
verified_note: Dates mapped to dried_fruit; vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup (closest); source has no nuts. Source says 'serving glasses' with no type.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Chikoo Chocolate Shake Blended
steps: Peel, deseed and cube 1 chikoo, then freeze it for 2 to 3 hours until completely frozen.
Add the frozen chikoo to a blender with 1/2 tbsp cocoa powder, 1/8 tsp instant coffee powder, sugar to taste and a few ice cubes.
Pour in about 90 ml (3/8 cup) milk and blend until very smooth.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately. Chocolate topping (about 3/4 tbsp) is used in the glass and blender as chocolate sauce.
verified_note: Source makes 4 (4 chikoo, 2 tbsp cocoa, 1/2 tsp instant coffee, 1 1/2 cups milk, 3 tbsp chocolate topping, sugar to taste), divided by 4. Sugar has no amount and was left out; ice skipped. Page does not say where the chocolate topping goes; its photo steps show drizzling sauce in the glass first and adding some to the blender.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Dry Fruit Cream Blend Ultra
steps: Blend nuts with milk into a smooth nut butter.
Add fresh cream, honey, and cardamom powder; pulse briefly.
Serve chilled in dessert glasses.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Tender Coconut Malai Rose Shake Blended
steps: Blend coconut malai, milk, rose syrup, and sugar until thick.
Pour into tall glass over ice cubes.
Garnish with dried rose petals.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Paan Falooda Special Layered
steps: Make the paan milkshake: in a glass mix 1 cup (240 ml) milk, 2 tbsp paan syrup, 1/2 tbsp gulkand (rose petal jam) and a pinch of green food color. Set aside.
Soak 1 tbsp sabja seeds in 1/2 cup water for about 10 minutes.
Put a few ice cubes in the serving glass.
Add the soaked sabja seeds, then 1 to 2 tbsp boiled falooda sev.
Pour in 1/2 tbsp rose syrup and 1 tbsp rabri.
Pour the paan milkshake over the layers.
Top with another 1 tbsp rabri, 5 to 6 pieces of paan kulfi and 1 scoop of gulkand ice cream.
Finish with chopped cashews and pistachios and the remaining 1/2 tbsp rose syrup, then serve.
verified_note: Rabri (2 tbsp) mapped to condensed_milk:30 as the closest thickened sweet milk. Gulkand ice cream mapped to ice_cream:1pcs (1 scoop). Falooda sev 1-2 tbsp taken as 1.5 tbsp. Sabja soaking water is mostly absorbed so it is not counted. Page lists amounts for one glass. Not included: paan syrup (2 tbsp), paan kulfi (5-6 pieces), green food color (pinch)

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Chocolate Paan Shake Blended
steps: Wash the betel (paan) leaves (about 3 leaves per glass) and tear them into small pieces.

Put the leaves in a blender with 0.8 tbsp gulkand, 2/3 tsp fennel seeds, about 1 cardamom pod, 1/3 tbsp kewra water, a scoop (about 2/3) of vanilla ice cream, 250 ml milk, a little desiccated coconut, a candied cherry and a pinch of green food colour.
Blend until smooth.
Pour about 1 1/3 tbsp chocolate sauce into the glass, then pour the shake over it.
verified_note: Page gives no serving count; batch (750 ml milk, 2 scoops ice cream, 8 leaves, 2.5 tbsp gulkand, 2 tsp fennel, 4 cardamom, 1 tbsp kewra water, 2 tbsp desiccated coconut, handful candied cherries, pinch green colour, 4 tbsp chocolate sauce) divided by 3 to fit a ~300 ml glass. Betel leaf mapped to herbal_leaf, kewra water to rose_water, ice cream scoops to ice_cream pcs. Coconut, cherries and colour have no ids or amounts. sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Makhana (Foxnut) Milkshake Roasted
steps: In a pan over low heat dry roast 1/4 cup foxnuts (phool makhana) for about 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until crisp and not over-browned. Let them cool, then grind them.
Peel and slice 1 large banana (about 1 cup chopped).

Add the banana, 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsweetened almond milk, the ground foxnuts, 1 tbsp peanut butter, 3/4 tbsp maple syrup (1/2 to 3/4 tbsp) and a pinch of kosher salt to a high-powered blender and blend. Add more milk for a thinner smoothie.
Pour into a small cup, top with a few whole foxnuts and serve.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Basundi Drink with Cardamom Poured
steps: Whisk basundi with cold milk to sipping consistency.
Stir in nutmeg and cardamom.
Serve chilled garnished with chipped pistachios.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Cold Filter Coffee Milkshake Blended
steps: Blend coffee decoction, cold milk, sugar, ice cream.
Blend high speed till thick and frothy.
Dust cocoa powder on foam.

sub: Rich Milkshakes, Mastanis & Festive Dessert Shakes
name: Rose Thandai Shake Blended Nut &
steps: Add 2 tsp rose syrup and 2 tsp thandai powder (about 5 g) to a blender jar.
Add 1 cup (240 ml) chilled milk.
Blend until smooth, about 2 to 3 minutes, and taste for sweetness.
Swirl a little extra rose syrup inside the glass, pour in the thandai, top with 3 dried rose petals or buds and serve cold (ice cubes are optional).
garnish: dried rose petals or rose buds
verified_note: Thandai masala (nut and spice powder) mapped to nuts at about 5 g per serving (2 tbsp for 3 servings). Source is a thandai drink, not an ice cream shake.

name: Neera (Fresh Palm Nectar) Chilled
steps: Keep unfermented palm sap ice-chilled.
Add fresh lime juice to balance sweetness.
Serve immediately over ice.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Pathimugam (Kerala Herbal Pink Water) Boiled
steps: Bring 250 ml of drinking water to a rolling boil, then lower the heat to about 95 C.
Add 1/8 tsp dried pathimugam (sappanwood) and take the pot off the heat.
Let the water cool further so the aromatics seep in.
Cool to lukewarm, strain and drink.
verified_note: Page gives 1 litre water and 1/2 tsp dry herbs for pathimugam, jeeragam, karingali or a dahasamani mix; scaled to 250 ml. Sappanwood mapped to herbal_leaf. Served lukewarm, so temp 'hot' is the nearest option. Page title is approximate.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Karikku (Tender Coconut) Cooler
steps: Put the meat and water of half a chilled tender coconut into a blender with sugar to taste.
Blend, then add about 2 tbsp vanilla ice cream and blend for about one more minute.
Serve in a decorated cocktail glass.
verified_note: Page serves 4 with 2 tender coconuts, 1/2 cup vanilla ice cream and sugar 'as reqd'; divided by 4. 125 ml is an approximation for half a coconut's water plus meat (page gives no ml). Sugar amount not given so omitted from ings. Page says nothing about honey or mint.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Jackfruit (Kathal) Nectar Blended
steps: Put 1/2 cup jackfruit bulbs (cut into pieces), 1 big glass (about 250 ml) chilled milk, sugar to taste and 1 crushed cardamom pod into a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Strain the juice through a strainer with large holes.
Pour into a glass and serve.
verified_note: Page: 1 cup jackfruit bulbs, sugar as required (no amount), 2 cardamom pods, 2 big glasses chilled milk; divided by 2. 250 ml per 'big glass' is an assumption. Jackfruit has no id so it is unmapped; sugar has no quantity on the page so it is left out. Not included: jackfruit bulbs (1/2 cup)

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Guava Chaat Cooler Pressed
steps: Put 1 cup chopped ripe guava, 1 to 1.5 tsp sugar and a pinch (1/16 tsp) of chaat masala into a blender jar.
Blend into a smooth puree, straining if needed to remove any unground seeds. Add water as needed to reach the thickness you like.
Soak 1 tsp sabja (sweet basil) seeds in 2 tbsp (30 ml) water for about 5 minutes until they swell, then stir them into the puree.
Serve cold.
verified_note: No fresh-guava id exists, so 1 cup chopped ripe guava is entered as guava_nectar:1cup (closest id; it is fruit puree, not nectar). Sugar 2-3 tsp / 2 = 1 to 1.5 tsp, entered as 1.25tsp midpoint. Chaat masala 1/8 tsp / 2 = 1/16 tsp = a pinch. Sabja 2 tsp / 2 = 1 tsp, soaked in 1/4 cup / 2 = 2 tbsp (about 30 ml) water. Page gives 'water as needed' for blending, not listed.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Watermelon Black Salt Punch
steps: Cut watermelon into quarters, scoop out the pulp, deseed it if you can, and put about 250 g in a blender. Discard the rind.
Add 1 oz (30 ml) water and a splash (about 4 ml) of lime juice and blend until completely smooth.
Strain the juice into a glass and stir in a small sprinkle (about 1/16 tsp) of kala namak (black salt).
Garnish with mint and serve chilled.
verified_note: Page: 1/2 small watermelon, 4 oz water, 1/2 oz lime juice, 1/4 tsp kala namak for 4 servings. Watermelon amount per serving (250 g) is an estimate of 1/8 of a small watermelon; water, lime and salt divided by 4.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Papaya Lime Mint Cooler Blended
steps: Blend 1/2 cup diced ripe papaya, about 1/8 cup fresh mint leaves and 2 tbsp cold water until smooth.
Strain the blend through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a glass or jug.
Add 60 ml (1/4 cup) lemon juice, 2 tbsp honey (or agave) and the remaining water (about 210 ml), and stir.
Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Refrigerate for at least 1 to 2 hours.
Add ice, stir and pour into a glass.
verified_note: Source is a lemon version, not lime; kept lemon_juice as written (swap to lime_juice if you want lime). Page makes a pitcher (2 cups papaya, 1/2 cup mint, 1 cup lemon juice, 1/2 cup honey, 4 cups water) with no servings stated; divided by 4. Mint 1/8 cup approximated as 8 leaves. Total water 240 ml = 30 ml blended plus 210 ml added. Not included: ripe papaya (0.5 cup diced)

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Jamun Ginger Digestive Shot
steps: Shake jamun pulp, ginger juice, black salt, lemon juice with ice.
Strain into shot glass.
Serve as quick digestive shot.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Mulberry (Shahtoot) Sharbat
steps: Put 80 g (about 3 oz) mulberries, 1 1/3 tablespoons jaggery powder and about 1/6 teaspoon rock salt in a small pan and add 80 ml water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Let the mixture cool to room temperature, then blend it.
Strain the smooth mixture into a jar and refrigerate for a few hours.
To serve, mix the sharbat with water and ice in a glass, adjusting to taste.
verified_note: Original 6 servings (17 oz mulberries, 2 cups water, 1/2 cup jaggery powder, 1 tsp rock salt) divided by 6. Page gives no amount of water to add at serving ('to taste'). Mulberries mapped to berries.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Custard Apple (Sitaphal) Rose Cooler Pulsed
steps: Pulse sitaphal pulp with rose syrup and cold water briefly.
Keep pulp texture intact.
Serve chilled over ice.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Lychee Rose Sparkler
steps: Add 2 tinned lychees and 1 tsp maple syrup (or other sweetener, optional) to a shaker or mason jar and muddle for about a minute until the juices are released.
Add 3 oz (90 ml) lychee juice from the tin, 3/4 oz (22 ml) rose syrup and 1/2 oz (15 ml) lime juice, with 3 to 4 ice cubes. Put the lid on and shake for 10 to 15 seconds.
Fill a glass with ice (add edible rose buds if you like) and strain the mixture in.
Top with 1/2 cup (120 ml) ginger kombucha or sparkling or still coconut water and stir gently.
Garnish with lychees, edible rose buds and/or a lime slice if desired.
garnish: lychees, edible rose buds, lime slice
verified_note: Coconut water chosen from the page's top-up options (ginger kombucha or coconut water); no sparkling soda is used. Lychee juice and tinned lychees have no id. Not included: lychee juice from tin (3 oz / 90 ml), 2 tinned lychees

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Sweet Lime (Mosambi) Mint Cooler
steps: Muddle mint leaves in glass base.
Add ice cubes and black salt.
Pour fresh sweet lime juice and stir.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Raw Papaya Lemon Juice Pressed
steps: Stir raw papaya juice, lemon juice, honey, and black salt.
Add cold water and ice.
Serve crisp and cold.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Wild Fig (Anjeer) Nectar
steps: Boil figs in water with jaggery and cinnamon; blend and strain.
Chill fig nectar in refrigerator.
Serve over ice cubes.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Plum Mint Punch
steps: Remove the pits from 125 g plums, leaving the skins on.
Add the plums and about 5 ice cubes to a blender. Pulse briefly on highest speed, about 5 times, until the ice is nearly melted.
Add 1 tbsp vanilla sugar, 250 ml fresh water and 1 to 2 mint leaves, and blend with a hand mixer until very liquid.
Add more water if you want a thinner juice, then pour into a tall glass.
verified_note: Nearest published recipe is Plum and Mint Nectar (not named punch). Plum mapped to jamun (black plum pulp) as there is no plum id; amounts halved so the total stays under 450 ml (page is 250 g plum + 500 mL water for 1). Vanilla sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Rasbhari (Cape Gooseberry) Sharbat
steps: Blend cape gooseberries with sugar, black salt, cold water.
Strain seeds out through fine mesh.
Serve yellow juice over ice.

sub: Coastal Coolers, Wild Berry & Tropical Fruit Nectars
name: Pomegranate Mint Elixir Pressed
steps: In a tall glass, combine 1/4 cup pomegranate arils, 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt.
Mash with a masher or spoon until the sugar dissolves and the arils release their juice.
Add 3 ice cubes, top with 1.5 cups sparkling water (or lemon-lime soda) and stir gently before serving.
verified_note: Pomegranate arils (1/4 cup) mapped to pomegranate_juice:0.25cup as no aril id; salt mapped to black_salt. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Sulaimani Tea (Kerala Spiced Black Tea) Boiled
steps: Lightly crush 1 green cardamom, 1 clove, a 1/4 inch piece of cinnamon and a 1/2 inch piece of peeled ginger (optional) in a mortar and pestle.
Put 1 cup water and the crushed spices in a saucepan, bring to a boil on medium heat, then simmer for 4 to 5 minutes.

Add 1/2 tsp black tea. If using loose leaves, turn off the heat, cover and steep 2 to 3 minutes. If using tea powder or half a tea bag, simmer 2 to 3 minutes until the colour deepens, without over-boiling.
Stir in 4 tsp raw or white sugar until dissolved, then turn off the heat.
Stir in 1/2 tsp lemon juice (add a little more for more tang) and 4 to 5 mint leaves if using, cover and rest for about a minute.
Strain into a cup or glass and serve hot.
verified_note: Halved from 2 cups water because the page gives no serving count. black_tea here is dry tea leaves (tsp), not brewed tea. Cinnamon 1/2 inch halved to 1/4 inch (0.25pcs); ginger 1 inch halved to 1/2 inch (0.5pcs, optional). Raw/white sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page also says it can be chilled and poured over ice.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Chukku Kappi (Dry Ginger Coffee)
steps: Bring 1 cup (250 ml) water to a boil in a small saucepan.
Add 0.75 tbsp jaggery and stir until it dissolves.
Add 0.75 tsp dry ginger powder, 0.25 tsp cumin seeds, 0.75 tsp instant coffee powder and 0.25 tsp black pepper. Boil for about 4 minutes.
Add 5 tulsi (holy basil) leaves and boil for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 1 cardamom pod (or a pinch of cardamom powder) and a tiny pinch of salt, then turn off the heat.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.
verified_note: Quantities divided by 4. Dry ginger powder -> ginger; instant coffee powder -> instant_coffee; salt -> black_salt (1 pinch ~ 1/16 tsp); 1 pod cardamom.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Adrak Elaichi Chai Simmered
steps: Heat about 120 ml water in a saucepan over medium heat.
When the water forms little bubbles, add 1/2 tsp loose Indian tea leaves (or about 3/4 of a tea bag) and 3/4 tbsp sugar and stir well.
Let it boil about 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 150 ml milk. Once it starts to boil and the tea rises, lower the heat and simmer about 2 minutes.
Add 1/2 tbsp grated ginger and 1/4 tsp cardamom powder and boil about 5 minutes.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.
verified_note: Page makes 4: divided by 4. Page's ingredient list says 2 cups water but its step 1 says 3/4 cup; used the ingredient list (120 ml each). Cardamom is powder (1 tsp per 4).

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Gur Wali Chai (Jaggery Tea) Simmered
steps: Heat 1/2 cup (120 ml) water to a boil (add a small piece of crushed ginger, about 1/4 inch, if you like).
Add 1 tsp loose black tea leaves (a strong variety like CTC) and boil for 2 minutes, until the water darkens.
Add 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk and bring to a rolling boil, stirring now and then.
Lower the heat and stir in 1 to 1.5 tbsp grated jaggery until it fully dissolves.
Simmer 2 to 3 more minutes, until the chai is a deep caramel brown.
Strain into a small glass and serve hot and strong.
verified_note: Page makes 2 servings (1 cup water, 2 tsp tea, 1 cup milk, 2-3 tbsp jaggery, optional 1/2 inch ginger), halved. Optional ginger left out of ings.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Lemongrass Mint Chai Boiled
steps: Boil lemongrass and mint in water for 4 minutes.
Add tea leaves, sugar, and milk; boil for 3 minutes.
Strain hot into chai glass.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Kashmiri Rose Kahwa Infused
steps: Lightly crush about 2/3 of a green cardamom, about 2/3 of a clove and a piece of cinnamon about 2/3 inch long (the page uses 2 inches of true cinnamon for 3 cups) in a mortar and pestle. Thinly slice or crush 1 to 2 almonds.
Pour 160 ml (2/3 cup) water into a saucepan on medium heat. Add the crushed spices, 2 dried rose petals and 2 tsp sugar.
Bring to a gentle boil on medium heat, then turn off the heat and set the pan aside.
Add 1/3 tsp green tea leaves, cover and steep for 3 minutes.
Strain into a small cup. Add 3 to 4 saffron strands and the sliced almonds and stir. Serve hot.
verified_note: Divided by 3. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup (2 tsp). Saffron 3-4 strands = 1 pinch. Cloves mapped to clove. Almonds 4-5 for 3 cups = about 1.5 per cup. Page uses honey nowhere; sugar only.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Chocolate Masala Chai Simmered
steps: Put 240 ml (1 cup) water, 120 ml (1/2 cup) milk and 2 chai tea bags in a pan and heat over medium heat.
Once hot, stir in 1.5 to 2 tsp cocoa powder and bring to a boil.
Turn off the heat and strain the chai into a cup.
Add sugar if you want it sweeter (optional, no amount given).
Top with whipped cream and chocolate chips.
verified_note: Page uses chai tea bags (Tazo organic black chai), mapped to black_tea in pcs (tea bags). Cocoa powder mapped to cocoa, not chocolate_syrup. Sugar is optional and has no amount, so it is omitted from ings. No separate whole spices on the page.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Indian Spiced Iced Tea Chilled
steps: Pour 200 ml of lemon iced tea into a glass.
Add 10 ml freshly prepared lime juice.
Add a pinch of salt and 1/2 tsp chaat masala.
Top with 2 to 3 ice cubes and stir for a couple of seconds.
Serve chilled; optionally garnish with mint leaves or a lime slice.
verified_note: Page uses a branded ready-made lemon iced tea (Nestea); mapped to black_tea (chilled), so the lemon sweetness comes from the premix. Table salt mapped to black_salt. Weak source: brand page. Not included: Nestea lemon iced tea premix (sweetened, lemon-flavored)

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Cinnamon Mulethi Warm Brew
steps: Simmer cinnamon and mulethi root in water for 8 minutes.
Strain into mug.
Stir in honey and add lemon slice.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Turmeric Pepper Golden Brew
steps: Put 1 1/4 cups (about 300 ml) water, 1/4 to 1/2 tsp turmeric powder and 1/8 tsp ground black pepper in a small pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 4 to 5 minutes (8 to 10 minutes if using 1 inch of fresh turmeric root instead of powder).
Stir in 1/2 to 1 tsp ghee or a cold-pressed oil (avocado, olive or coconut), then strain into a cup.
Serve hot or warm. Add lemon juice or honey only once the tea is warm, not hot. If it tastes too strong, dilute with hot water.
verified_note: Page gives turmeric as a range (1/4 to 1/2 tsp); lower end used. Page has no ginger and no fixed honey amount (only 'lemon juice or honey' when warm). Not included: ghee or cold-pressed oil, 1/2 to 1 tsp

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Jaggery Lemon Black Tea Boiled
steps: Boil water, tea leaves, cardamom, and jaggery for 3 minutes.
Strain into tea cup.
Stir in lemon juice and serve hot.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Kashmiri Pink Salt Ginger Tea Salted
steps: Boil ginger and tea leaves in water for 3 minutes.
Stir in warm milk and pink salt.
Strain and serve hot in clay cup.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Green Cardamom Hot Milk Infusion
steps: Crush 2 plump green cardamom pods well with a mortar and pestle.
Add 1 cup (240 ml) previously boiled milk to a saucepan, then add a few saffron strands.
Add the crushed cardamom and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 1 tsp sugar and mix well.
Serve hot or warm.
verified_note: Page makes 3 servings (6 pods, 3 cups milk, 3 tsp sugar, few saffron strands); divided by 3. Saffron few strands = 1 pinch.

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Pudina Chai (Fresh Mint Tea) Simmered
steps: Put 1 cup (240 ml) water, 1/2 tsp chai masala powder and a 1/2 inch piece of crushed peeled ginger in a saucepan. Bring to a boil on medium-high heat.
Lower the heat and simmer 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 1 tsp loose black tea leaves and 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk and simmer 2 more minutes.
Add 8 to 10 rinsed fresh mint leaves and cook for 30 seconds. Do not overcook or the tea turns bitter.
Strain into a cup and stir in 1 tbsp powdered jaggery. Serve hot.
verified_note: Divided by 2. Mint 15-20 leaves for 2 = 8 per cup. Chai masala powder (1/2 tsp) has no id, kept in steps. Jaggery id used (page: 2 tbsp powdered jaggery for 2). Page says only serving cups. Not included: chai masala powder 0.5 tsp

sub: Spiced Teas, Heritage Coffees & Warm Restorative Brews
name: Saunf Elaichi Hot Milk Infused
steps: Crush fennel seeds and cardamoms; boil in milk for 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed mishri rock sugar until dissolved.
Strain hot into mug; serve warm.

name: Omija-cha (Five-Flavor Tea)
steps: Put 1.7 g (about 1 teaspoon) dried omija (schisandra) berries in 167 ml (about 2/3 cup) cold water and leave to steep overnight, about 12 hours. Do not use hot water: heat brings out too much sourness and bitterness.
Strain out and discard the berries, keeping the red liquid.
Sweeten with honey or sugar to taste if you like, and add a few thin pieces of Korean (Asian) pear if you like.
Serve as it is, or refrigerate and serve cold.
garnish: Korean pear pieces carved into flower shapes (optional)
verified_note: Dried schisandra berries mapped to omija. Honey/sugar is optional 'to taste' on the page with no amount, so it is left out of ings.

name: Sikhye (Sweet Rice Punch)
steps: Put 11 g barley malt powder (yeotgireum) in a cheesecloth or nut milk bag and soak it in 142 ml (0.6 cup) warm water for 20 to 30 minutes, squeezing the bag until the water turns milky.
Let the malt water stand for 15 to 20 minutes so the sediment settles to the bottom.
Soak and squeeze the same malt again in another 142 ml (0.6 cup) warm water and keep this second liquid for the boiling stage.
Cook 2.5 teaspoons (1/20 cup) short-grain or sweet rice with about 10% less water than usual so it is slightly dry; do not soak it first. Fluff it.
Pour the clear first malt water into a rice cooker, leaving the sediment behind, stir in the rice to break it up, and set the cooker to 'keep warm' (about 60 to 65 C / 140 to 150 F).
After about 4 hours check that some rice grains float on top and feel like soft yarn between your fingers; if not, keep warming another 30 minutes to 1 hour or longer.
Move the mixture to a pot with the second malt water. If you want floating rice for serving, strain some out, rinse it several times in cold water and keep it in fresh water in the fridge.
Bring to a boil and skim off the foam. Add about 1.8 teaspoons sugar (to taste), a small slice of ginger (optional) and a pinch of salt, and boil 5 to 6 minutes.
Cool and store in the fridge; serve in a small bowl with a few rice grains floating on top.
garnish: Floating rice grains, 5 or 7 pine nuts, sliced jujube (optional)
verified_note: Barley malt powder (yeotgireum) mapped to herbal_leaf; sugar to simple_syrup; salt to black_salt. Page salt amount 1/2 tsp per 20 cups is a pinch per serving; page does not say when to add it.

name: Sujeonggwa (Cinnamon Dried Persimmon Punch)
steps: Rinse 3.5 g cinnamon sticks. Peel 5 g fresh ginger and slice it thinly.

Put the ginger in a small saucepan with 130 ml water, cover and boil on medium heat for 40 minutes. At the same time put the cinnamon in another small saucepan with 130 ml water, cover and boil on medium heat for 40 minutes.
Strain both liquids through a sieve into one saucepan and discard the ginger and cinnamon.
Add 2 tablespoons sugar (raw or brown sugar) and boil on high heat for 10 to 20 minutes, until the sugar has completely dissolved.
Let it cool for a couple of hours (or stand the pan in a sink of cold water and ice for about half an hour).
Serve cool, garnished with pine nuts and dried jujube; if adding dried persimmon, put it in the drink at least 1 hour before serving so it softens.
garnish: Pine nuts, dried jujube, dried persimmon (optional)
verified_note: Raw/brown sugar mapped to simple_syrup (granulated). Page lists water as '22cup' but the method uses 11 cups per pot; 22 cups / 20 servings used. Garnishes have no amounts so they are not in ings.

name: Yuja-cha (Citron Honey Tea)
steps: Stir 2 to 3 teaspoons yuja-cheong (homemade or store-bought citron preserve) into 1 cup of hot or cold water until it dissolves.
Serve; you can eat the pieces of rind.
verified_note: Page amount '2-3 tsp' given as 2.5 tsp. Page says the water can be hot or cold; hot chosen as the traditional serve.

name: Daechu-cha (Jujube Date Tea)
steps: Cover 20 g (about 2.5 tablespoons) dried jujubes with boiling water, cover with a plate so they stay under, and leave about 1 hour until soft.
Drain and blend the jujubes with 2 g minced ginger and a small pinch (about 1/8 tsp) ground cinnamon into a thick paste like wet sand.
Mix in 20 g sugar, pack into a clean airtight jar, and leave at room temperature 8 hours or overnight, then keep in the fridge (up to 1 month).
To serve, scoop 1 tablespoon of the paste (or more to taste) into a large mug, pour about 1 cup (240 ml) hot water over it, stir and steep 5 minutes.
verified_note: Dried jujubes mapped to dried_fruit; sugar to simple_syrup. Paste amounts are the batch divided by 15 servings; page serves 1 tbsp paste per cup.

name: Saenggang-cha (Korean Ginger Tea)
steps: Put 10 g peeled, thinly sliced fresh ginger, 2.5 g cinnamon stick and 1 cup water in a small pot.
Boil on medium to medium-low heat for about 25 to 30 minutes.
Strain out the ginger and cinnamon (a fine cloth catches the small bits of cinnamon).
Serve warm, sweetened with 1 teaspoon honey and topped with a few pine nuts if you like.
verified_note: Pine nuts 'some' on the page; 3 pcs is an approximate. Cinnamon sticks mapped to cinnamon.

name: Baesuk (Spiced Korean Pear Warm Chiller)
steps: Put 4 g peeled, thinly sliced ginger and 180 ml (3/4 cup) water in a small pot and bring to a rolling boil over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile cut 122 g peeled Korean pear into 2 wedges and push 3 black peppercorns deep into the back of each wedge with a chopstick.
Remove the ginger. Add the pear wedges and 1/2 tablespoon sugar or honey and simmer on low heat for about 10 minutes.
Take off the heat, let it cool and refrigerate for a few hours.
Serve the pear in its broth, cold or warm, garnished with pine nuts.
verified_note: Korean pear mapped to pear (fruit, not juice); peppercorns counted as pcs; sugar or honey given as honey.

name: Dungulle-cha (Solomon's Seal Tea)
steps: Bring 240 ml (1 cup) water to a vigorous boil.
Add 1 teaspoon roasted Solomon's seal root pieces (or 1/3 of a tea bag).
Simmer on medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes.
Strain out the root pieces and serve hot, or refrigerate and serve cold.
verified_note: Roasted Solomon's seal root mapped to herbal_leaf. Source is a general herbal tea blog (no dedicated recipe site found); batch of 2 tbsp root to 6 cups water treated as 6 servings.

name: Oksusu-suyeom-cha (Corn Silk Tea)
steps: Pull the silk from 1 ear of corn and trim off any dead or exposed ends. If you like, dry it in the sun on a tray until dry to the touch.
Put the silk in a mug and pour 1 cup hot water over it; steep 5 minutes. Or boil the silk and water together in a pot for 5 to 8 minutes.
Strain and drink hot or iced, with maple syrup to taste if you like.
verified_note: Corn silk mapped to herbal_leaf (1pcs = silk of one corn cob). Page uses silk from 3-4 cobs for 3 cups water.

name: Bori-cha (Roasted Barley Tea)
steps: If roasting your own, stir whole barley in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown and fragrant.
Put 1/2 tablespoon roasted barley in a pot with 240 ml (1 cup) water, bring to a boil, then take off the heat.
Steep 5 to 10 minutes depending on how strong you like it.
Strain into a cup and serve hot, or cool, chill and serve over ice.

name: Memil-cha (Roasted Buckwheat Tea)
steps: If toasting your own, spread raw buckwheat groats in one layer in a large dry skillet over medium heat and stir constantly about 5 minutes until fragrant and lightly browned.

Lower the heat to medium-low and keep toasting until the groats are a deep chestnut brown (turn the heat down further if they brown too fast). Pour into a bowl and cool completely; store airtight in the fridge for up to about 3 months.
Put 1 tablespoon toasted buckwheat groats in a tea infuser in a mug.
Pour 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water over them and steep 5 minutes, then remove the infuser and serve.
verified_note: Roasted buckwheat groats mapped to barley_tea (roasted grain tea). Page is the Japanese soba-cha, the same roasted buckwheat tea.

name: Maesil-cha (Green Plum Honey Infusion)
steps: Add 3 tablespoons maesil-cheong (green plum syrup) to 1 cup of water (hot, cold, iced or sparkling) and mix well. Use a wooden spoon if dipping into a homemade jar.
Add honey to taste if you want it sweeter.
Sprinkle 1 or 2 lightly toasted pine nuts on top and serve.
garnish: 1-2 lightly toasted pine nuts (or a plum blossom, or a squeeze of lemon or lime)
verified_note: Honey is optional 'to taste' with no amount, so it is left out of ings.

name: Gam-ip-cha (Persimmon Leaf Tea)
steps: Boil 200 ml water, then let it cool to 70 to 80 C (158 to 176 F); hotter water makes the tea bitter and lowers its vitamin content.
Add 2 to 3 g dried persimmon leaves and steep 2 to 3 minutes, then pour into a cup.
The same leaves can be steeped 1 or 2 more times.
verified_note: Dried persimmon leaves mapped to herbal_leaf (dried_fruit would be the fruit, not the leaves). Page amount 2-3 g given as 2.5 g.

name: Mogwa-cha (Preserved Quince Tea)
steps: Combine quince preserve with hot water in a glass mug
Stir until honey dissolves and aromatic quince fragrance releases

name: Gukhwa-cha (Chrysanthemum Flower Tea)
steps: Put 2.5 g dried chrysanthemum flowers in a tea bag, tea strainer or teapot with a built-in strainer so the petals stay out of the cup.
Boil 1 1/2 cups (355 ml) water and pour it over the flowers.
Steep 3 to 5 minutes and pour.
Top up the same flowers with fresh hot water for 2 or 3 more rounds through the day. In summer it can be served over ice.
verified_note: Dried chrysanthemum mapped to edible_flower. Page is a Chinese-style chrysanthemum tea (same method as Korean gukhwa-cha); no sweetener in the page recipe.

name: Sol-ip-cha (Pine Needle Infusion)
steps: Chop 2 tablespoons fresh or dried pine needles into small pieces.
Put them in a teapot or cup and pour over 1 cup freshly boiled water.
Cover and steep 10 minutes or longer.
Strain through a tea strainer or fine sieve. Add honey or sweetener and a slice of lemon to taste if you like.
verified_note: Pine needles mapped to herbal_leaf. Honey/sweetener is optional 'to taste' with no amount. Page warns pregnant people should avoid pine needle tea and to confirm the pine species.

name: Ssanghwa-cha (Traditional Herbal Vitality Brew)
steps: Lightly rinse the ssanghwa herbs: about 1.7 g each of angelica root, astragalus, cnidium, peony root, rehmannia (sukjihwang) and licorice, plus 1.7 g each of ginger, jujube and cinnamon stick.
Put them in a pot with about 333 ml water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Turn down to medium and simmer 20 to 30 minutes.
Strain and drink plain, or sweeten with honey. For a lighter brew the author halves the herbs and uses about 500 ml water.
verified_note: The six medicinal roots (angelica, astragalus, cnidium, peony, rehmannia, licorice; page uses machine-translated names) are combined as ginseng (herbal root) 10 g; jujube mapped to dried_fruit. Page says peony may be doubled. Batch of 10 g each herb in 2 L water divided by 6.

name: Gyeop-baesuk (Ginger Pear Nectar)
steps: Slice 14 g (1/2 oz) peeled ginger about 6 mm (1/4 inch) thick.
Peel 3/4 of an Asian (nashi) pear, cut into 3 quarter sections, cut out the core and round off the sharp edges.
Push 3 or 4 peppercorns into each pear section, just deep enough to stay in.
Bring the ginger, 3/4 tablespoon sugar and 355 ml (1 1/2 cups) water to a full boil over high heat, then simmer on medium-low until reduced by a quarter.
Strain out the ginger, add the pear sections and cook 10 more minutes.
Remove from heat, let cool, then refrigerate the pear in its liquid.
Serve cold in a small bowl, pear sections covered with the liquid.
verified_note: Asian pear mapped to pear (fruit). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. 1 oz pine nuts per 4 is listed but the method never uses them. 'Gyeop-baesuk' is not a recognised name; baesuk (ginger-pear punch) is the closest real drink.

name: Cheongguk-jang Brew (Fermented Soybean Tea)
steps: Whisk soybean powder into hot water until smooth and velvety
Highly prized traditional probiotic health beverage

name: Yulmu-cha (Job's Tears & Walnut Tea)
steps: Dry-roast Job's tears (yulmu) powder in an empty pan, stirring quickly all the time because it burns easily, until it is yellowish all over. Let it cool completely.
Put about 2 tablespoons of the roasted powder in a cup. Add roasted walnut powder and roasted almond powder for a richer flavor if you like.
Add 1 to 2 pinches of salt and 1/2 tablespoon honey or unrefined sugar.
Add about 30 ml milk (or unsweetened soy milk), then about 80 ml water, adjusting the thickness to taste, and stir well.
verified_note: Job's tears powder mapped to herbal_leaf; '2 rice spoons' given as 2 tbsp. Walnut and almond powder are optional with no amount, so not in ings. Page does not state water temperature; description suggests a warm drink.

name: Hongsi-sujeonggwa (Persimmon Ice Punch)
steps: Wash, peel and slice fresh ginger (about 1 1/2 tablespoons sliced) and put it in a pot with 1 rinsed cinnamon stick.
Add about 367 ml (1 1/2 cups) water and boil 20 minutes over high heat.
Turn down to medium and boil 25 minutes more (take the lid off if it boils over).
Stir in 3 tablespoons sugar and let it cool.
Remove the stem from 1 dried persimmon and wash it well.
Strain out the cinnamon and ginger, pour the liquid into a glass jar or bowl, add the persimmon, cover and refrigerate at least 12 hours.
Ladle into a small bowl with ice cubes, with the persimmon and a few pine nuts on top.
garnish: 1 softened dried persimmon and a few pine nuts
verified_note: Sugar mapped to simple_syrup; dried persimmon to dried_fruit. Maangchi lists amounts only in the directions (1/2 cup sliced ginger, 5 cinnamon sticks, 7 1/2-8 cups water, 1 cup sugar) for 4-5; divided by 5.

name: Naju Pear & Mint Water (Refreshing)
steps: Muddle mint leaves in bottom of glass, add chilled pear juice, ice, and top off with crisp sparkling water

name: Jeju Tangerine Blossom Infusion (Floral)
steps: Steep fragrant citrus blossoms in warm spring water for 4 minutes
Clear, golden hue with subtle orange perfume
Recipe scaled down to a single glass from a batch.

name: Misutgaru Water (12-Grain Shake)
steps: Put 1 tablespoon misugaru (Korean roasted multigrain powder), 187 ml (3/4 cup) water, 3/4 tablespoon honey (or sugar) and 1 ice cube in a blender.
Blend until smooth. If your ice cubes are very hard, shake everything in a shaker bottle instead, or stir the powder, water and honey hard with a spoon and then add the ice.
Serve cold.
verified_note: Misugaru (multigrain powder) mapped to kinako (closest roasted grain/soy flour). Page's base recipe uses milk and says water can be swapped in equal amount; the water version is used here.

name: Hwanggi-cha (Astragalus Root Tea)
steps: Put 1/2 tablespoon dried, shredded astragalus root and 240 ml (1 cup) water in a small covered pot.
Simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Strain and serve hot or iced.
verified_note: Astragalus root mapped to ginseng (ginseng / astragalus / herbal root). Page batch of 1 tbsp root in 2 cups water treated as 2 servings. Page advises checking with a doctor if taking lithium or immune-suppressing drugs.

name: Gisung Mulberry Leaf Tea
steps: Bring water to a boil and let it cool slightly to about 85 C (185 F).
Put 1/2 teaspoon mulberry leaf powder in a bowl, add a little of the hot water and whisk briskly in a 'W' motion until frothy.
Add the rest of the 90 ml (3 oz) water, pour into a cup and drink hot, or let it cool and pour over ice.
verified_note: Mulberry leaf powder (kuwacha) mapped to herbal_leaf. Page is a Japanese tea maker's brewing guide; the 3 oz is the page's cup size.

name: Omija Green Apple Sparkler
steps: Layer Omija cold brew over ice, pour green apple juice and sparkling soda water for a tangy 5-flavor spritzer

name: Bokbunja Chill (Wild Raspberry Nectar)
steps: Dilute black raspberry extract into cold water over ice cubes and garnish with a lime wheel
Rich dark ruby color
garnish: lime wheel Rich dark ruby color 3 tbsp B

name: Gotgam Cinnamon Brew
steps: Put 5.8 g cinnamon sticks in one small pot and 4.7 g thinly sliced ginger in another, with 125 ml (1/2 cup) water in each.
Bring both to a boil, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Strain both through a fine strainer into one pot.
Stir in about 25 g (17 to 33 g, to taste) muscovado or light brown sugar until dissolved.
Let it cool, then refrigerate until chilled.
Soak 1 dried persimmon (gotgam) in the punch for 30 to 60 minutes to soften it, and add pine nuts or a jujube flower just before serving.
garnish: Dried persimmon, pine nuts, rolled jujube flower (optional)
verified_note: Muscovado/brown sugar mapped to brown_sugar_syrup (by weight); dried persimmon to dried_fruit. Gotgam-cinnamon drink is sujeonggwa; page sugar 1-2 cups per 12 given as the midpoint.

name: Lotus Flower Leaf Tea (Yeon-ip- cha)
steps: Put 350 ml water and 7 g dried lotus leaf in a pot.
Add 14 g rock sugar, bring to a boil on high heat, then simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Pour out, stir well and drink.
verified_note: Dried lotus leaf mapped to herbal_leaf; rock sugar to simple_syrup (g). The page's single serving uses 500 ml water, so all amounts were scaled by 0.7 to stay under 450 ml.

name: Dandelion Root Tea (Mindle-cha)
steps: To roast your own root, wash and chop dandelion roots into small pieces, spread on a baking sheet and bake at 200 F (95 C) until the kitchen smells like chocolate; cool and store in a jar.
Bring 240 ml (1 cup) water to a boil.
Add 1/2 tablespoon roasted dandelion root, a small piece (about 1/4) of a small cinnamon stick and a small pinch of cardamom.
Simmer 20 minutes.
Strain and pour into a mug to drink hot, or cool and pour over ice.
verified_note: Roasted dandelion root mapped to ginseng (herbal root). Batch of 4 cups water treated as 4 servings.

name: Hallabong Citrus Nectar (Jeju Citrus)
steps: Wash 1/2 hallabong (dekopon) well and cut it into pieces small enough to blend.
Put the hallabong, 1 cup sparkling water and 1 tablespoon honey (the author uses chestnut honey) in a blender; add ice cubes in summer.
Blend until smooth and serve.
verified_note: Hallabong (whole fruit) mapped to orange; ice is optional on the page (summer only).

name: Doraji-cha (Bellflower Root Tea)
steps: Simmer bellflower root and dates for 35 minutes
Strain, blend with honey to soothe throat and lungs
Recipe scaled down to a single glass from a batch.

name: Eosongcho Tea (Houttuynia Cordata)
steps: Steep dried leaves in warm water for 5 minutes
Traditional detox herbal infusion with clean herbal finish
Recipe scaled down to a single glass from a batch.

name: Korean Burdock Root Tea (Ueong- cha)
steps: Bring 1 cup water to a boil in a small saucepan.
Add 1 tablespoon dried burdock root, turn the heat to low and simmer 10 to 15 minutes (5 minutes longer for a stronger brew).
Strain into a mug and discard the root.
Stir in 1 teaspoon raw honey or a splash of lemon if you like, and serve warm.
verified_note: Dried burdock root mapped to ginseng (herbal root). Honey is optional on the page (1 tsp per recipe, kept per serving as a small amount). Page is an herbal company's recipe blog.

name: Pueraria Root Tea (Galgeun-cha)
steps: Put 6.25 g (5 to 7.5 g) dried kudzu root slices in 250 ml water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes.
Strain, sweeten lightly with honey if you like, and drink warm.
verified_note: Dried kudzu (pueraria) root mapped to ginseng (herbal root). Honey optional with no amount. Page notes caution for legume allergies or hormone-sensitive conditions.

name: Gugija-cha (Goji Berry Tea)
steps: Rinse 1 3/4 tablespoons dried goji berries by pouring boiling water over them and discarding that water.
Bring 1 cup (240 ml) water to a boil and pour it over the berries (add any sugar now so it dissolves; ginger slices or seeded jujubes can go in too).
Steep at least 20 minutes.
Pour into a cup with some of the berries; add honey only if serving chilled.
garnish: A few goji berries in the cup; toasted pine nuts optional
verified_note: Goji berries mapped to dried_fruit. Page's '2 mugs' use 4 cups water (480 ml each, over the 450 ml limit), so scaled to 1 cup water with a quarter of the berries (6-8 tbsp / 4). Sweeteners optional, no amount.

name: Bori Sikhye (Barley Malt Punch)
steps: Put 17.5 g malted barley flour (in a tea bag), 312 ml (1 1/4 cups) water and 1.3 tablespoons steamed short-grain rice (cooked a little drier than usual) in a rice cooker pot.
Set the cooker to 'warm' (not cook) for 4 to 8 hours, until some rice grains float to the top. Without a rice cooker, use the oven at its lowest setting for 4 to 8 hours.
Remove the tea bag and pour the liquid into a pot, scooping out some rice to keep; rinse that rice under cold water and keep it in a little fresh water.
Add 1.3 tablespoons sugar and boil on high heat 5 to 10 minutes until dissolved. Cool, then refrigerate until chilled.
Pour into a cup, add some of the reserved rice, and garnish with pine nuts and/or thin slices of dried jujube.
garnish: Pine nuts and/or thinly sliced dried jujube
verified_note: Malted barley flour mapped to herbal_leaf (grains); sugar to simple_syrup; cooked rice to rice. Pine nut count approximate (page: optional, no amount). Sikhye is the barley-malt rice punch; no separate 'bori sikhye' recipe used.

name: Omija Asian Pear Punch (Hwachae)
steps: Put 4 g dried omija berries in a glass jar with 203 ml (about 7/8 cup) cold water, cover and soak 24 hours.
Strain the liquid into a jar, add 2 1/4 tablespoons honey and stir with a wooden spoon until dissolved. Refrigerate.

For the jelly noodles (optional), stir 35 ml water with 1 teaspoon mung bean starch and a tiny pinch of salt in a small heavy pan, and cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until translucent and bubbling. Pour into a glass container and let set 2 to 3 hours, then turn out and cut into tiny cubes.
Peel a piece of Korean (or Anjou/Bosc) pear, slice it about 6 mm (1/4 inch) thick and cut 4 to 5 bite-size pieces or shapes.
Ladle about 1 cup of punch into a bowl, add 3 to 4 ice cubes, about 3 tablespoons jelly cubes and the pear slices, and stir gently to chill.
Sprinkle with pine nuts (about 1 teaspoon) and serve with a spoon.
verified_note: Dried omija berries mapped to omija; pear slices counted as pcs. Batch (28 g omija, 6 cups water, 1 cup honey, 2 tbsp pine nuts) divided by 7. Not included: mung bean starch (jelly noodles)

name: Wild Chrysanthemum Chiller (Summer Flower)
steps: Put 2.5 g dried chrysanthemum flowers in a tea bag, strainer or teapot with a built-in strainer.
Pour 1 1/2 cups (355 ml) boiling water over them and steep 3 to 5 minutes.
Strain, let cool, and serve over ice for summer.
verified_note: Dried chrysanthemum mapped to edible_flower. Page recipe is hot and notes it can be served with ice in summer; no sweetener in the page.

name: Korean Bamboo Leaf Tea (Juk-ip- cha)
steps: Steep bamboo leaves for 3 minutes
Offers a cool, grassy aroma with light mineral undertones
Recipe scaled down to a single glass from a batch.

name: Maesil Lemonade (Fusion)
steps: Combine green plum syrup with fresh lemon juice in ice glass; crown with sparkling soda and mint

name: Jeju Green Tea Infusion (Sejak)
steps: Put 1 tablespoon Sejak green tea leaves in a small teapot, gaiwan or roomy tea bag.
Pour over 350 ml water at 75 to 80 C and steep 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour off all the tea. The leaves can be infused 1 to 2 more times with fresh hot water.
verified_note: Page is a tea shop's brew guide; it gives no cold or iced method.

name: Ssuk-cha (Korean Mugwort Tea)
steps: Rinse 1.25 g (about 1 tablespoon, loosely packed) dried food-grade mugwort in a fine strainer under cold water.
Put 240 ml (1 cup) water, the mugwort and about half a dried jujube (optional) in a small saucepan.
Heat on medium-high until small bubbles appear, then turn to low; do not let it reach a rolling boil.
Simmer gently on low 15 minutes (no more than 20).
Strain into a mug, add a little honey if you like, and serve hot.
verified_note: Dried mugwort mapped to herbal_leaf; jujube to dried_fruit. Page's serving is 480 ml water (over the 450 ml limit), so the 2-serving batch was divided by 4. Source is a general food blog (no dedicated Korean recipe site found).

name: Gyeul-cheong Warm Drink (Citrus)
steps: Stir preserved tangerine slices and honey syrup into hot water until sweet citrus aroma fills the mug. (RECIPES 46–90) Preparation Method

name: Usucha (Ceremonial Thin Matcha)
steps: Pour boiling water into the tea bowl to warm it, soften the whisk tips in it, then discard the water and dry the bowl with a clean cloth.
Sift 1 teaspoon (about 2 g) matcha through a fine strainer into the dry bowl.
Pour boiling water into a separate cup and let it cool about 1 minute to about 85 C (185 F).
Add a very small splash of the cooled water to the matcha and whisk into a smooth paste.

Pour in about 70 ml of the cooled water and whisk briskly in a quick W or M motion from the wrist until a thick froth of fine bubbles forms; finish by drawing one circle and lifting the whisk from the center.
Serve immediately, ideally with a Japanese sweet, and drink before the powder settles.

name: Sencha (Classic Japanese Green Tea)
steps: Weigh 10 g (about 2 tablespoons) loose sencha and put it in a teapot.
Heat 210 ml water to 80 C (176 F).
Pour the water over the leaves, cover and steep 60 seconds.
Strain through a sieve into warmed teacups and serve right away, without sugar or honey. The same leaves can be refilled 2 to 3 more times.
verified_note: The page's one pot (one batch) is treated as one serving. Card says 7.5 oz (222 ml); body says 210 ml.

name: Gyokuro (Shaded Shade-Grown Tea)
steps: Weigh 10 g (about 2 tablespoons) loose gyokuro and put it in a teapot.
Heat 160 ml water to 60 C (140 F).
Pour the water over the leaves, cover and steep 90 seconds.
Strain through a sieve into warmed teacups and serve right away, without sugar or honey. The same leaves can be refilled 2 to 3 more times.
verified_note: The page's one pot (one batch) is treated as one serving.

name: Genmaicha (Roasted Rice & Green Tea)
steps: Weigh 10 g (about 2 tablespoons) loose genmaicha and put it in a teapot.
Heat 240 ml water to 100 C (212 F).
Pour the water over the leaves, cover and steep 30 to 40 seconds.
Strain through a sieve into warmed teacups and serve right away, without sugar or honey. The same leaves can be refilled 2 to 3 more times.
verified_note: The page's one pot (one batch) is treated as one serving. Genmaicha (green tea with roasted rice) mapped to green_tea. Card says 8.5 oz (250 ml); body says 240 ml.

name: Hojicha (Roasted Green Tea)
steps: Weigh 10 g (about 4 tablespoons) loose hojicha and put it in a teapot.
Heat 240 ml water to 100 C (212 F).
Pour the water over the leaves, cover and steep 30 to 40 seconds.
Strain through a sieve into warmed teacups and serve right away, without sugar or honey. The same leaves can be refilled 2 to 3 more times.
verified_note: The page's one pot (one batch) is treated as one serving. Card says 8.5 oz (250 ml); body says 240 ml.

name: Kukicha (Twig & Stem Green Tea)
steps: Bring 240 ml (1 cup) water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat.
Add 3/4 teaspoon kukicha tea twigs, lower the heat to low and cover the pan.
Simmer for 20 minutes, then pour into a cup.
verified_note: Page makes 1 Tbs twigs in 4 cups water; divided by 4 for one cup. Kukicha twigs mapped to green_tea (loose, measured in tsp). Page does not name a vessel or say hot/iced; it is simmered and served as a warm tea.

name: Sobacha (Japanese Buckwheat Tea)
steps: Boil 265 ml (about 1 1/8 cups) water in an electric kettle or saucepan.
Put 2 teaspoons roasted buckwheat tea grains in a teapot and pour the boiling water over them.
Steep for 3 to 4 minutes, then strain through a fine-mesh sieve and serve hot.
For a cold version, let the tea cool to room temperature, refrigerate it and serve cold.
The same grains can be brewed 2 to 3 more times; add a few minutes to the steeping time each time.
verified_note: Used the page's teapot method (2 Tbsp to 3 1/3 cups, about 790 ml) scaled to one third to stay a single cup. Roasted buckwheat tea mapped to barley_tea (roasted grain tea).

name: Mugicha (Chilled Japanese Barley Tea)
steps: The page brews 1 mugicha tea bag for about 1 litre (4 glasses); per glass that is a quarter of a bag, so for convenience brew the whole bag as below.
Put 1 mugicha tea bag in a measuring cup and add 60 ml (1/4 cup) boiling water (15 ml per glass). Steep for 2 minutes.
Pour the concentrated tea and the tea bag into a large pitcher and add 1 quart (about 950 ml) room-temperature or cold filtered water (about 235 ml per glass).
Refrigerate and steep for 2 hours, then remove and discard the tea bag.
Serve the mugicha over ice cubes in individual glass cups.
verified_note: Page makes about 1 litre from one tea bag; one glass = 1/4 bag and 250 ml water (15 ml boiling + 235 ml cold).

name: Kuromamecha (Black Soybean Tea)
steps: Roast the beans first (the page roasts 225 g / 1/2 lb at a time, enough for 20 to 30 cups): rinse the dried black soybeans under running water for 10 to 20 seconds, rubbing them together, then drain in a colander and air dry on a towel-covered tray.

Dry-fry the beans in a single layer in a pan with no oil over medium heat until the surfaces are completely dry, then turn to low heat and keep frying for 20 to 30 minutes more, shaking and stirring now and then, until they crack, the insides are lightly browned and they smell faintly nutty.
Turn off the heat, let the beans cool and store them in an airtight container.
For one cup, put 1 tablespoon roasted beans in a tea cup or teapot, pour over 240 ml (1 cup) boiling water and steep for 2 to 3 minutes.
Drink the tea; you can eat the beans afterwards.
verified_note: Roasted black soybeans mapped to herbal_leaf (grains). One serving = 1 tablespoon roasted beans per cup of boiling water as the page states.

name: Sakuracha (Salted Cherry Blossom Tea)
steps: Put 2 to 3 salt-preserved cherry blossoms in a small bowl and cover them with about 120 ml (1/2 cup) warm water. Soak for 5 minutes to remove salt.
Lift the blossoms out gently with a spoon or tweezers and shake off excess water (the salty soaking water can be saved for cooking).
Put the blossoms in a clear glass teacup and pour over 240 ml (1 cup) hot, not quite boiling water (200 F / 93 C).
Steep for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring gently once or twice.
Serve at once while steaming, ideally with a Japanese sweet; the blossom can be eaten at the end.
verified_note: Salt-preserved cherry blossoms mapped to edible_flower (page gives 2-3; used 3). The 1/2 cup rinse water is discarded so not counted in ings. Optional 1 tsp agave or sugar left out.

name: Konbucha (Savory Sea Kelp Tea)
steps: Put 3/4 teaspoon (about 3 g) kombu tea powder in a cup.
Pour in 150 ml boiling water (or cold water for a cold version).
Stir well until dissolved; it is ready to drink, usually hot.
verified_note: Page gives 1/2 tsp (2 g) per 100 ml; scaled 1.5x to a 150 ml cup. Kombu (kelp) tea powder mapped to herbal_leaf. The page adds no extra salt.

name: Ume-Konbucha (Plum Sea Kelp Tea)
steps: Put about 3 g ume kombucha powder in a cup.
Pour in 150 ml boiling water and mix well until dissolved.
Serve hot (it can also be enjoyed cold in summer).
verified_note: Page gives about 2 g powder per 100 ml boiling water; scaled 1.5x to a 150 ml cup. Ume kelp tea powder mapped to herbal_leaf.

name: Amacha (Sweet Hydrangea Leaf Tea)
steps: Put about 1 g amacha leaves (roughly 4 leaves) in a porcelain gaiwan.
Pour over 200 ml water at 100 C (boiling); the leaves open quickly.
Steep 30 seconds for the first infusion, then pour off.
Re-steep the same leaves for 45 seconds for the second infusion and 1 minute for the third and later infusions. Avoid long 2 to 4 minute steeps, which make it too strong and sweet.
verified_note: Page ratio is 0.5 g (about 2 leaves) per 100 ml; scaled to 200 ml. Hydrangea leaves mapped to herbal_leaf.

name: Gobocha (Japanese Burdock Root Tea)
steps: Bring 240 ml (1 cup) water to a boil in a small saucepan and add 1 tablespoon dried burdock root.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes (5 minutes longer for a stronger brew).
Strain into a mug, discarding the root.
Optionally stir in 1/2 teaspoon raw honey or a splash of lemon, and serve warm.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved. Burdock root mapped to ginseng (herbal root). Page uses dried, not roasted, burdock. Optional honey/lemon left out of ings.

name: Dokudami-cha (Chameleon Plant Tea)
steps: Put 1.25 g dried dokudami (heartleaf) in a non-reactive pot (glass, ceramic, stainless steel or enamel) with 300 ml (1 1/4 cups) fresh cold water; about 60 ml boils off.
Heat to a full rolling boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10 minutes. Do not stir or shake the tea while brewing.
Turn off the heat and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Strain and serve.
verified_note: Page's general herbal-tea method (5 g to 5 cups, yields about 4 cups) divided by 4. Dokudami mapped to herbal_leaf.

name: Biwa no Ha-cha (Loquat Leaf Tea)
