steps: Put 1.25 g dried loquat (biwa) leaves in a non-reactive pot (glass, ceramic, stainless steel or enamel) with 300 ml (1 1/4 cups) fresh cold water; about 60 ml boils off.
Heat to a full rolling boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10 minutes. Do not stir or shake the tea while brewing.
Turn off the heat and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Strain and serve.
verified_note: Page's general herbal-tea method (5 g to 5 cups, yields about 4 cups) divided by 4. Loquat leaves mapped to herbal_leaf.

name: Kakyoku-cha (Persimmon Leaf Chiller)
steps: Put 1.25 g dried persimmon leaves in a non-reactive pot (glass, ceramic, stainless steel or enamel) with 300 ml (1 1/4 cups) fresh cold water; about 60 ml boils off.
Heat to a full rolling boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10 minutes. Do not stir or shake the tea while brewing.
Turn off the heat and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Strain and serve.
verified_note: Page's general herbal-tea method (5 g to 5 cups, yields about 4 cups) divided by 4. Page gives no cold-brew method.

name: Shincha (First Harvest Spring Green Tea)
steps: Put 10 g (2 tablespoons) shincha leaves in a teapot.
Pour in 210 ml hot water at 80 C.
Pour out and serve 40 seconds after you began pouring the water (about 50 seconds for a slightly stronger cup).
verified_note: Shincha leaves mapped to green_tea (loose, in g).

name: Bancha (Late Harvest Japanese Green Tea)
steps: Heat water to 175 F (80 C) or above; if you only have boiling water, cool it with a little cold water and check with a thermometer.
Put 5 g (1 tablespoon) bancha leaves in a teapot.
Pour in 350 ml (12 oz) of the water slowly.
Steep for 1 to 2 minutes, then pour out completely, in short bursts if sharing between cups. Later steeps can be shorter.
verified_note: Bancha leaves mapped to green_tea (loose, in g).

name: Mecha (Bud Green Tea)
steps: Measure 1 teaspoon (2 to 3 g) mecha into a teapot with a fine mesh strainer (the buds are tiny and pass through wide strainers).
Heat 240 ml (1 cup) water to 70 to 80 C (70 to 75 C gives the fullest flavor); boiling water scorches the buds.
Pour the water over the buds and steep for 40 to 60 seconds.
Pour the tea into your cup through the fine strainer.
Re-steep the same buds at the same temperature for 20 to 30 seconds and pour; a third 15 second steep is possible but thinner.
verified_note: Mecha (bud tea) mapped to green_tea. Page gives 1 tsp per 1 cup water.

name: Tamaryokucha (Curly Green Tea)
steps: Boil water for a few minutes, then cool it to 70 to 80 C by pouring it into empty teacups.
Put 8 g tamaryokucha leaves in a teapot with a filter mesh.
Pour the 160 ml cooled water from the cups into the teapot and put the lid on.
Brew for 60 seconds without stirring or shaking.
Pour out in small amounts until the very last drop. The leaves can be re-steeped up to 3 times at the same temperature, a little longer each time.
verified_note: Page's pot (8 g to 120-160 ml, 2 small Japanese cups) kept as one 160 ml cup, since half would be only 80 ml. Tamaryokucha mapped to green_tea.

name: Kyoto Sanbancha (Late Harvest Tea)
steps: Bring 300 ml water to a boil in a kettle or pan (the page boils 40 g leaves in 2 to 3 litres at a time).
Add about 5 g Kyobancha leaves and keep it boiling for about 2 minutes.
Remove the leaves and drink, hot or cold.
verified_note: Kyoto 'sanbancha' matched to Kyobancha (Kyoto late-harvest roasted bancha). Kettle method 40 g to 2-3 litres scaled to a 300 ml cup using 2.5 litres. Kyobancha is roasted, so mapped to hojicha.

name: Yuzu Sencha (Citrus Infused Sencha)
steps: Heat 230 ml (8 oz) water to 170 F (about 77 C).
Put 5.5 g sencha with yuzu (sencha blended with dried yuzu peel) in a teapot and pour over the water.
Steep for 1 minute 30 seconds, then pour out.
For a second steep, use water at 175 F.
verified_note: Sencha-with-dried-yuzu-peel blend mapped to green_tea; the yuzu peel is part of the 5.5 g blend, so no separate yuzu amount.

name: Matcha-iri Genmaicha (Matcha Rice Tea)
steps: Heat water to 175 F (80 C) or above.
Put 5 g (1 tablespoon) matcha genmaicha in a teapot.
Pour in 350 ml (12 oz) of the water slowly.
Steep for 30 to 60 seconds, then pour out completely. Later steeps can be shorter.
verified_note: Matcha genmaicha (green tea, toasted rice and matcha blend) mapped to green_tea.

name: Kuromatsucha (Pine & Green Tea Blend)
steps: Steep green tea and pine needle tips for 90 seconds
Woodsy, refreshing, piney green tea

name: Kuromame Hojicha (Black Soybean Roasted Tea)
steps: Put 6 g (about 1 1/4 tsp) kuromame houjicha (roasted green tea blended with black beans) in a Japanese teapot.
Cool boiled water to 90 C and pour 300 ml into the teapot.
Steep for 45 seconds, then pour an equal amount into each cup.
verified_note: Ready-made blend of roasted green tea and black beans mapped to hojicha (ratio of beans not stated, so no separate bean amount).

name: Kiku-Sencha (Chrysanthemum Sencha)
steps: Steep green tea with chrysanthemum blossoms for 60 seconds
Soothing floral accent on grassy green tea

name: Shiso-cha (Perilla Leaf Tea)
steps: Rinse 4 to 5 red shiso leaves well and set aside.

Put 240 ml (1 cup) water, 0.6 g dried mandarin orange peel, 0.6 g dried licorice root and 1.25 g smashed ginger in a small pot. Cover, bring to a boil over high heat, then simmer for 10 minutes over low heat.
Add the shiso leaves and 2 to 3 teaspoons sugar (or leave it out, or use honey or agave at serving). Bring back to a boil over high heat, then cover and simmer 7 to 8 minutes over medium-low heat.
Take off the heat and strain out all the solids. Let it cool on the counter; it will be dark purple-red.
Just before serving, stir in about 1 1/2 teaspoons (7 ml) fresh lemon juice; it turns pink.
Serve hot with lemon slices like a tea, lukewarm, or chilled over ice.
verified_note: Page makes 8 servings; divided by 8 (30-40 leaves to about 4 per cup, sugar 1/3-1/2 cup to about 2.5 tsp, lemon 3-4 tbsp to about 7 ml). Red shiso leaves mapped to herbal_leaf, mandarin peel to orange, licorice root to ginseng (herbal root), sugar to simple_syrup. Page turns it pink with lemon juice, not plum vinegar.

name: Mikan Peel Infusion (Chenpi-cha)
steps: Bring 240 ml (8 oz) water to a boil in a saucepan and add a 1 1/2 inch piece of dried orange peel.
Boil for 3 minutes, then take off the heat, cover and steep for at least 5 minutes (longer for a stronger flavor).
Remove the peel with a slotted spoon, reheat if needed, and serve warm in a teacup or mug, sweetened with honey or sugar to taste.
verified_note: Page serves 4; divided by 4 (6-inch dried peel to a 1.5-inch piece, logged as orange:0.25pcs; 32 oz water to 8 oz). Sweetener 'to taste' and optional cinnamon, cloves and star anise left out.

name: Sugi Leaf Cedar Tea (Forest Infusion)
steps: Bring 240 ml (1 cup) water to a boil.
Add 1/2 cup fresh cedar sprigs and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the water turns golden.
Strain off the cedar and sweeten with maple syrup to taste. Drink warm or cold.
verified_note: Closest real recipe is a North American cedar tea (species not stated), not Japanese sugi. 2 cups cedar to 4 cups water scaled to one cup. Fresh cedar mapped to herbal_leaf. Maple syrup 'to taste' left out of ings.

name: Biwa-Yuzu Honey Warm-up (Winter Care)
steps: Stir yuzu honey preserve into piping hot loquat leaf tea until fully dissolved
Comforting for cold winter days

name: Matcha Cold Brew (Mizudashi Matcha)
steps: Put 1 teaspoon matcha and 60 ml (1/4 cup) cold water in a cocktail shaker or tight-lidded jar. Close and shake vigorously for 10 to 20 seconds.
Fill a cup with ice (about 1 cup) and 180 ml (3/4 cup) cold water.
Pour the shaken matcha into the cup and stir well before drinking.
verified_note: Ice not counted. 1 tsp matcha is about 2 g.

name: Mizudashi Sencha (Cold Brew Green Tea)
steps: Weigh 3.75 g Japanese green tea leaves (the page uses 15 g for 1 litre) and put them in a cold brew tea maker or jar.
Add 250 ml room-temperature or cold filtered water.
Steep in the refrigerator for 6 to 8 hours.
Discard the leaves and serve with or without ice. Keeps in the fridge 2 to 3 days.
verified_note: Page makes 1 litre (4 cups); divided by 4. Sencha mapped to green_tea (loose, in g).

name: Kyoto Cold Brew Hojicha (Chilled Roasted)
steps: Measure 2.5 g hojicha (the page uses 10 g for 1 litre; 10 g is 3 to 5 1/2 tbsp depending on the brand) and put it in a cold brew tea maker or jar.
Add 250 ml water and steep in the refrigerator for 6 to 8 hours.
Discard the tea leaves and serve with or without ice. Keeps in the fridge 2 to 3 days.
verified_note: Page makes 1 litre (4 cups); divided by 4.

name: Sakura Sencha Cold Brew (Floral Cold Brew)
steps: Brew 1 jasmine green tea bag in 240 ml (1 cup) hot water.
Sweeten with 1/2 tablespoon honey.
Steep 2 preserved cherry blossoms in a little hot water, then add 1/2 tablespoon of that liquid to the tea and refrigerate to chill.
Freeze the remaining blossom water into ice cubes with one blossom in each cube.
Serve the chilled tea over the cherry blossom ice cubes.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved. Brewed jasmine green tea mapped to green_tea (ml). Preserved (salted) cherry blossoms mapped to edible_flower. Page gives no amount for the blossom steeping water.

name: Kuromame Barley Chiller (Dual Grain)
steps: The page cold-brews 1 to 2 tea bags (8 g each) per litre of water; for one 250 ml glass that is about 3 g of the barley and black soybean blend (brewing one bag in 1 litre and pouring a quarter also works).
Put the tea in 250 ml cold water and chill in the refrigerator for 1 to 2 hours.
Remove the tea bag and drink it fresh.
verified_note: Ready-made blend of roasted barley and black soybeans mapped to barley_tea (bean share not stated). 1.5 bags (12 g) per litre used as the midpoint and divided by 4.

name: Ume Shiso Sencha Spritz (Plum Herb)
steps: Muddle umeboshi plum flesh and shiso in glass, fill with ice, add cold green tea, and top with soda water

name: Hokkaido Azuki Red Bean Tea (Red Bean Infusion)
steps: Simmer roasted azuki beans in water for 12 minutes
Subtle natural sweet bean aroma, clear reddish brown liquid

name: Tochu-cha (Eucommia Bark Tea)
steps: Boil tea leaves for 5 minutes
Rich herbal tea widely consumed across Japan for wellness benefits

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Gensai Wellness Tea Blend (Herbal Digest)
steps: Steep 5g of mixed traditional wellness grains and tea for 3 minutes
Balanced, rounded, pleasant after meals

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Aomori Apple Leaf Tea (Orchard Tea)
steps: Steep apple leaves for 4 minutes
Subtle fruit blossom scent with pleasant green finish

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Kagoshima Fukamushicha (Deep Steamed Tea)
steps: Put 3 to 4 g fukamushi sencha in a teapot.
Pour in 200 ml water at 70 C and steep 30 to 45 seconds, then pour out completely.
Second steep: add 200 ml water at 70 to 80 C and pour out almost at once (about 10 seconds).
Third steep: 200 ml water at 70 to 80 C for 30 to 60 seconds.
verified_note: Fukamushicha mapped to green_tea (loose, in g). ings cover the first steep.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Shiitake Mushroom Savory Tea (Mushroom Broth)
steps: Put about 2.5 g shiitake tea powder in a cup.
Pour in 150 ml boiling water and stir well.
verified_note: Page uses one 2 g stick per 100-120 ml; scaled to a 150 ml cup. Shiitake tea powder mapped to herbal_leaf. Page adds no salt and no mitsuba.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Kyoto Genmaicha Cold Brew Sparkler (Fizzy Tea)
steps: Pour cold brew Genmaicha into chilled glass with ice cubes and top with crisp sparkling water
Highly refreshing. 91–145) Preparation Method

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Fresh Strawberry Milk (Cafe Classic)
steps: Dice or mash 70 g hulled fresh strawberries (for frozen berries, blend with 1 tablespoon hot water on the lowest speed).
Put the strawberries in a bowl, add 35 g raw or white sugar and mix well. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for 1 to 2 hours.
Put the strawberry syrup (about 4 tablespoons) in a serving cup, add 2 to 3 ice cubes if you like, pour 240 ml (1 cup) milk over it and serve at once. Mix with a straw.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup (in g). Ice optional, not counted.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
extras: 1/2 cup steamed roasted sweet potato (Korean goguma)
name: Sweet Potato Milk Latte (Goguma Latte)
steps: Peel 113 g (4 oz) Korean sweet potato (purple skin, pale flesh if available) and cut it into 1 inch (2.5 cm) pieces. Steam, covered, over simmering water until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Put the sweet potato in a blender with 235 ml (1 cup) milk and blend until smooth.
Pour into a small saucepan over medium-low heat and whisk in 1/2 to 1 tablespoon honey and a small pinch of salt. Keep whisking until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Pour into a glass, top with frothed milk, a sprinkle of ground cinnamon and, if you like, finely chopped toasted walnuts. Serve at once.
garnish: frothed milk, ground cinnamon, optional chopped toasted walnuts
verified_note: Page serves 2-4; divided by 2 (227 g sweet potato, 470 ml milk, 1-2 tbsp honey). Salt mapped to black_salt. Cinnamon is a topping (amount not given, logged as a pinch). Frothed milk topping amount not given. Not included: Korean sweet potato 113g

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Black Sesame Latte (Heuk-im-ja Latte)
steps: Combine 1 tablespoon black sesame paste, 2 tablespoons brown sugar and 60 ml (1/4 cup) hot water, and mix with a handheld milk frother.
Pour the black sesame mixture into a cup.
Add about 1 cup ice and top with 240 ml (1 cup) milk. Stir before drinking.
verified_note: Brown sugar (dry) mapped to brown_sugar_syrup. Ice not counted.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Mugwort Milk Latte (Ssuk Latte)
steps: Stir 0.8 tablespoon mugwort powder and 1.2 tablespoons condensed milk into 72 ml hot water until even.
Whip 72 ml whipping cream with 0.8 tablespoon condensed milk into a cream.
Pour 216 ml milk (with ice if you like) onto the mugwort base and top with the cream.
verified_note: Page makes 2 servings in Korean 'spoons' (taken as tbsp) and 'paper cups' (taken as 180 ml). Half the page would be about 500 ml, so scaled to 40% of the page (80% of one serving) to stay under 450 ml. Mugwort powder mapped to herbal_leaf. Ice 'as needed', not counted.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Chestnut Cream Latte (Bam Latte)
steps: Steam about 7 to 8 chestnuts, let them cool and peel them.
Put the chestnuts, 1 to 1 1/2 tablespoons honey and 300 ml (1 1/4 cups) milk in a blender and blend until the chestnuts are fine.
Pour into a pot and turn off the heat as soon as it starts to boil.
Pour into a cup and sprinkle with cinnamon powder to taste.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved (15 chestnuts, 2-3 tbsp honey, 2.5 cups milk; cup taken as 240 ml). Chestnuts mapped to nuts. Cinnamon 'a little', logged as a pinch.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Injeolmi Soybean Paste Latte (Dessert Latte)
steps: Mix 2 tablespoons roasted soybean powder (kinako), 72 ml water and 1.2 tablespoons sugar.
Whip 72 ml whipping cream with 1.6 tablespoons condensed milk.
Hot: put the soybean liquid in a cup, add 216 ml heated milk, then the whipped cream, and top with injeolmi cookies.
Iced: put ice in the glass, then the soybean liquid, 216 ml cold milk, the whipped cream and injeolmi cookies.
verified_note: Page makes 2 servings in Korean 'spoons' (taken as tbsp) and 'paper cups' (taken as 180 ml); scaled to 40% of the page (80% of one serving) to stay under 450 ml. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Injeolmi cookie amount not given.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Decaf Dalgona Cream Latte (Viral Classic)
steps: In a bowl, combine 3/4 tablespoon instant coffee granules (regular or decaf), 2 tablespoons sugar and 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Beat with an electric mixer for about 5 to 7 minutes, until stiff peaks form.
Fill a glass three-quarters full with ice cubes and pour in 120 ml (1/2 cup) milk to cover the ice.
Spoon the coffee foam on top, stir and serve with a straw.
verified_note: Page fills 2 glasses; halved. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page says the coffee may be decaf.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Banana Milk Cloud (Chilled)
steps: Peel 1 ripe banana, cut it into 2 inch pieces, put it in a covered container with 240 ml (1 cup) milk and refrigerate overnight (up to 36 hours). Strain out the banana.
For the syrup, put 1/2 ripe banana cut in 1 inch pieces, 2 tablespoons water and 2 2/3 tablespoons sugar in a saute pan over medium-high heat and stir until the sugar melts.
After about 2 minutes mash the banana, then cook 6 to 8 minutes more until the syrup is dark brown and as thick as honey. Let it cool.
In a cup, combine the banana milk and syrup, adjust to taste, and add ice.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Optional espresso or matcha left out.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Jeju Tangerine Ade (Hallabong Ade)
steps: Wash 1/2 Hallabong (Jeju tangerine) thoroughly and cut it into pieces small enough for a blender.
Put the Hallabong, 240 ml (1 cup) sparkling water and 1 tablespoon honey (chestnut honey or any honey) in a blender.
Blend until smooth. Add ice cubes in summer if you like.
verified_note: Hallabong (whole fruit) mapped to orange. Cup taken as 240 ml. Ice optional, not counted.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Blue LemonADE (Korean Cafe Style)
steps: Add 3 teaspoons butterfly pea flower tea to 240 ml (1 cup) boiling water, cover and steep a few minutes until the water turns deep blue.
Leave the flowers in or remove them. Stir in the juice of 1/2 medium lemon (about 22 ml) and sugar or honey to taste.
Serve over ice.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved. Butterfly pea flower tea mapped to herbal_leaf. Juice of 1/2 medium lemon estimated at 22 ml. Sweetener 'to taste' left out.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Green Plum Mint Sparkler (Maesil Ade)
steps: Gently bruise 1 rosemary sprig with a pestle, muddler or mallet to release its oils.
Fill a glass three-quarters full with ice and add 3 lemon slices and the rosemary.
Add 45 ml (1 1/2 oz) Korean green plum syrup, then top with 180 ml (6 oz) sparkling water.
Stir and enjoy.
garnish: edible flowers and a rosemary sprig (optional)
verified_note: Ice not counted.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Omija Sparkling Sunset (Berry Fizz)
steps: Ahead of time, make omija extract (cheong) by combining omija berries and sugar in a 1:1 ratio; the page's extract was fermented for 100 days.
Put 4 to 5 ice cubes in a glass.
Pour in 50 g of omija extract and 150 ml of sparkling water.
Decorate with a piece of lemon and a few rosemary leaves (mint leaves also work).
garnish: a piece of lemon and rosemary leaves (or mint)
verified_note: Omija extract (cheong) mapped to omija_syrup; rosemary ('a little') kept as garnish only.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Peach Cheong Latte (Fruity Cream)
steps: Make the peach preserve (full batch): wash 3 large peaches and 1/2 lemon, halve the peaches, twist them apart, peel them and cut into 1 cm pieces, then squeeze the lemon juice over them.
Bring 200 ml water and 5 tbsp sugar to a boil; when the sugar has melted, add the peaches, lower the heat and stir.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the peaches are soft.
Divide into hot sterilised containers and let it ripen for a day.
For one serving, blend about 133 ml of the peach preserve until smooth.
Pour 200 ml milk into the ground peach and top with a few pieces of raw peach.
verified_note: Homemade cooked peach preserve mapped to peach_cheong; per-serving amounts are one third of the 400 ml preserve + 600 ml milk used for 3 people.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Shine Muscat Grape Ade (Premium Grape)
steps: Put 15 Shine Muscat grapes and 200 ml sparkling water in a blender.
Blend for 40 seconds to 1 minute.
Pour into a transparent cup; you can drop one whole Shine Muscat grape into the cup.
verified_note: Fresh Shine Muscat grapes mapped to berries (no fresh grape id).

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Dalgona Matcha Cloud (Green Foam)
steps: Beat 120 ml (1/2 cup) chilled heavy whipping cream on high speed until it reaches stiff peaks, about 5 minutes.
Stop the mixer, add 1 to 2 tbsp granulated sugar and 2 tbsp matcha powder, mix on low until the matcha is incorporated, then on medium until thick and glossy.
Fill a stemless wine glass with ice and 180 to 240 ml (3/4 to 1 cup) milk, to about 3/4 full.
Top with the whipped matcha.
verified_note: Granulated sweetener (1 to 2 tbsp) mapped to simple_syrup at the lower amount; milk is 3/4 to 1 cup of any milk (the page suggests unsweetened almond milk), 3/4 cup used. The page also allows aquafaba or coconut cream instead of heavy cream.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Yuja Hibiscus Cooler (Floral Citrus)
steps: Pour 175 ml hot water over 2 g dried yuzu peel and 1 g hibiscus tea in a teapot and steep for 5 minutes, then let it cool.
Pour 175 ml cloudy apple juice into a glass and add ice cubes if you like.
Gently pour the cooled tea into the glass and garnish with mint to taste.
verified_note: Dried yuzu peel mapped to yuzu; hibiscus_tea is 1 g hibiscus tea steeped in 175 ml hot water together with the yuzu peel.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Misutgaru Condensed Milk Shake (Nutty Shake)
steps: Put 1 tbsp misugaru powder, 3/4 cup milk (or water), 1 ice cube (or more to taste) and 3/4 tbsp honey (or sugar) in a blender.
Blend until well integrated.
Alternatively, shake everything in a shaker bottle to keep the ice whole, or stir vigorously with a spoon and then add the ice.
verified_note: Misugaru (roasted multigrain powder) mapped to kinako.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Red Bean Paste Milk (Pat Latte)
steps: Cover 1/4 cup dried red beans with water in a small pot, bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then simmer about 1.5 hours until very tender.
Drain the beans, lightly mash them with a fork and stir in 2 tbsp honey or sugar and a pinch (1/16 tsp) of kosher salt until the sugar melts; let them cool completely.
Bring 1 cup milk to a simmer in a pot, add 2 tbsp tea leaves and remove from the heat; steep 10 to 15 minutes, then strain, pressing the leaves.
Let the milk tea cool at room temperature, then refrigerate until serving.
Put the red beans in a tall glass, fill it halfway with ice, top with the milk tea and stir before drinking.
verified_note: red_bean is 1/4 cup dried red beans cooked, mashed and sweetened at home; black_tea is 2 tbsp loose tea leaves steeped in the milk; kosher salt mapped to black_salt.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Jeju Matcha Oat Milk Latte (Vegan Green)
steps: In a 2-cup measuring cup or frothing pitcher, stir 1 tsp matcha, 2 tbsp hot water (just below boiling, 180F/82C) and 1 tbsp maple syrup into a smooth, lump-free paste.
Heat 1 cup oat milk until just below boiling; pour 1/4 cup of it into the matcha paste and the remaining 3/4 cup into your mug.
Froth the matcha mixture with a hand-held frother for about 30 seconds, until it roughly doubles in volume.
Pour the matcha foam over the hot milk in the mug and serve.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Blueberry Cheong Milk (Berry Cream)
steps: Add blueberry preserve to glass, add ice, pour cold milk over
Deep purple syrup ribbons through white milk

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Sweet Corn Milk Latte (Oksusu Latte)
steps: Blend one 15 oz (425 g) can of sweet corn, liquid included, on high for 60 to 90 seconds until as smooth as possible.
Press the puree through a fine-mesh sieve, then strain the liquid a second time; discard the pulp. You should have about 1/2 to 2/3 cup corn liquid. Keep a few whole kernels for garnish.

In a small saucepan over medium-low heat, warm 240 ml (1 cup) whole milk with 1 to 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk (or maple syrup) and a pinch of sea salt, whisking occasionally until steaming; do not boil.
Off the heat, stir in the corn liquid and 1/4 tsp vanilla extract (optional).
Froth with a milk frother, whisk vigorously for 30 seconds, or pour between two mugs to aerate.
Pour into a mug, put the reserved corn kernels on the foam and serve immediately.
garnish: a few reserved sweet corn kernels
verified_note: Sea salt mapped to black_salt; vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup; sweetener is 1 to 2 tbsp condensed milk or maple syrup, lower amount used. Not included: sweet corn, one 15 oz (425 g) can with its liquid, strained to about 1/2 to 2/3 cup corn liquid

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Mango Cheong Coconut Chiller (Tropical)
steps: Fill a shaker with ice and add 120 ml (4 oz) coconut water, 60 ml (2 oz) mango nectar and 3 dashes of Angostura bitters; shake vigorously until the outside of the shaker feels cold.
Fill a highball or Collins glass with ice and pour in the mango mixture.
Hold an upturned teaspoon near the rim and slowly pour 15 ml (1/2 oz) grenadine over the back of the spoon so it runs down the side of the glass; do not stir.
Garnish with a maraschino cherry.
verified_note: Mango nectar mapped to mango_pulp. Not included: Angostura bitters, 3 dashes (contains alcohol; optional to omit)

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Ginger Honey Milk (Saenggang Milk)
steps: In a saucepan, warm 250 ml milk and 1/2 tbsp honey together over medium heat.
Grate 1 tbsp fresh ginger into a paste and whisk it into the milk.
Let it simmer, then serve warm.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Jujube Caramel Milk Latte (Rich Sweet)
steps: Whisk jujube puree into warm milk until frothy, drizzle caramel syrup over top foam layer

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Persimmon Honey Milkshake (Autumn Shake)
steps: Peel 3/4 of a very ripe Hachiya persimmon and remove any seeds.
Blend the pulp with 125 ml milk, about 1 tbsp honey (3/4 to 1 tbsp) and a scant 1/4 tsp garam masala until smooth; refrigerate until serving.
To serve, put a scoop of vanilla ice cream in a tall glass, stir the chilled milkshake and pour it over the ice cream (or blend the ice cream in with everything else).
Garnish with about 1 tbsp chopped pistachios, or grated chocolate, if you like.
garnish: 1 tbsp chopped pistachios or grated chocolate (optional)
verified_note: Fresh Hachiya persimmon mapped to dried_fruit (the id covering persimmon); 2% milk mapped to milk. Not included: garam masala, about 3/16 tsp (3/4 tsp for 4)

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Jeju Green Lemonade (Green Citrus)
steps: Make the green tangerine syrup ahead: wash the green tangerines, rub them with baking soda and soak 10 minutes, add vinegar and soak 5 minutes more, then rinse, drain and dry.
Cut off both ends of each tangerine (they can taste bitter), cut the rest into pieces and squeeze the juice from the ends over them.
Add sugar (the page uses 6.3 kg sugar to 8 kg fruit), shake to mix and leave at room temperature 7 to 8 hours until the sugar dissolves.
Pour into a sterilised glass bottle, keep at room temperature for a day or two, then refrigerate.
To make the ade, mix syrup and sparkling water at 2:8, 3:7 or 4:6; for one 250 ml glass at 3:7 that is 75 ml syrup and 175 ml sparkling water.
verified_note: Green tangerine (cheonggyul) syrup mapped to fruit_cheong; the per-glass amounts are the page's 3:7 ratio applied to a 250 ml glass.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Fig Cheong Milk Latte (Fig Classic)
steps: Spoon rich honeyed fig preserve into glass bottom, add ice, fill with milk, and float smooth cream on top

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Lotus Biscoff Korean Milkshake (Cafe Trend)
steps: Put 1.5 cups (324 g, 3 to 4 scoops) vanilla ice cream and 30 to 60 ml (1/8 to 1/4 cup) whole milk in a high-powered blender.
Blend 20 to 30 seconds, using a tamper or spatula as needed; add about 2.5 tbsp Biscoff cookie butter and blend again until mostly combined, leaving thin ribbons.
Microwave 1 tbsp more cookie butter for 20 seconds and drizzle it around the inside of the glass.
Pour in the milkshake and top with whipped cream and crushed Biscoff cookies if you like.
garnish: whipped cream and crushed Biscoff cookie crumbs (optional)
verified_note: Milk is 1/8 to 1/4 cup per shake; the lower amount used. Not included: Biscoff cookie butter, about 2.5 tbsp (1/3 cup for 2) plus 1 tbsp warmed for the glass, crushed Biscoff cookies (garnish)

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Mogwa Ginger Sparkler (Quince Ginger)
steps: Mix quince preserve and fresh ginger juice together, add ice cubes, pour sparkling water over
Aromatic and zesty

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Black Rice Milk Chiller (Heukmi Latte)
steps: Blend black rice with milk and condensed milk until purple and silky smooth
Serve over ice

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Pine Needle Green Apple Fizz (Forest Fizz)
steps: Combine pine syrup with clear apple juice over ice, top with bubbly soda water
Piney and crisp

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Plum Shiso Mint Ade (Herbal Plum)
steps: Fill a glass about three-quarters full with ice.
Gently bruise 1 rosemary sprig with a pestle, muddler or mallet to release its oils, then add it to the glass with 3 lemon slices.
Add 45 ml (1 1/2 oz) Korean plum (maesil) syrup, then top with 180 ml (6 oz) sparkling water.
Garnish with edible flowers and a rosemary sprig if you like, stir and serve.
garnish: edible flowers and a rosemary sprig (optional)

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Cherry Blossom Latte (Spring Special)
steps: Use only the flowers from a correctly identified cherry tree, removing all stems, leaves and stalks.
Put 1 handful of fresh blossoms in a jar, pour 1 cup (240 ml) cold full-fat milk over them, cover and refrigerate for 24 hours (warm milk does not infuse well).
The next day, strain the infused milk through cheesecloth or a fine strainer into a pot.
Warm the milk gently, take it off the heat and stir in sweetener to taste if using.
Optionally froth part of the milk with a milk frother until foamy.
Pour the sakura milk into a cup, spoon the foam on top and garnish with fresh sakura blossoms.
verified_note: One handful of fresh cherry blossoms mapped to edible_flower:1pcs; sweetener is optional and unmeasured.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
extras: 1/3 cup steamed sweet kabocha pumpkin purée
name: Sweet Pumpkin Cream Milk (Dan- hobak)
steps: Cut about 67 g seeded kabocha into small chunks, peel and steam 20 to 25 minutes until cooked (about 62 g steamed).
Blend the steamed pumpkin with 167 ml milk for about 1 minute until fully smooth.
Pour into a pot, add 1 tsp raw sugar, about 1/6 tsp each of vanilla essence, nutmeg and cinnamon and a pinch (1/12 tsp) of ground ginger, and heat on low for 4 to 5 minutes, whisking constantly.
Pour into a mug or tea cup, add any optional toppings and serve.
garnish: optional whipped cream, maple syrup, a sprinkle of cinnamon or a cinnamon stick
verified_note: Raw sugar mapped to simple_syrup; vanilla essence mapped to vanilla_syrup; ground ginger mapped to ginger. Not included: kabocha squash, about 67 g raw (62 g steamed) per serving

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Kyoho Grape Sparkler (Grape Fizzer)
steps: Dissolve 19 g Kyoho grape powder mix in 30 ml hot water in the serving glass.
Fill the glass with ice.
Slowly pour 170 ml soda water over the ice and stir lightly.
Garnish with mint leaves and edible flowers.
verified_note: Kyoho grape powder mix (NESTEA, sweetened) mapped to grape_syrup by weight.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Red Ginseng Honey Milk (Wellness Milk)
steps: Clean 1 fresh ginseng root, wash off the soil, dry it and cut it into pieces that fit the blender.
Blend the ginseng with a little under half of the 200 ml milk until finely ground.
Steam the remaining milk to a moderate foam (do not overheat it); a milk whisk also works.
Put the ground ginseng in a wide, deep cup, add 1 spoon of honey and mix well while pouring in the steamed milk little by little.
Top with the milk foam and sprinkle with cinnamon powder.
verified_note: Fresh ginseng root mapped to ginseng; the page's '1 spoon' of honey recorded as 1 tbsp.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Jeju Citrus Matcha Foam Chiller (Citrus Green)
steps: Pour 150 ml orange juice into a large (16 oz / 470 ml) glass.
Fill the glass to the brim with ice.
In a small bowl, whisk 2 g (1 tsp) matcha with 60 ml hot water until there are no lumps.
Pour the matcha over the ice and serve (add sugar syrup if you like).
verified_note: Sugar syrup is optional and unmeasured, so it is left out.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Melon Milk Soda Chiller (Melon Fresh)
steps: Combine melon syrup with milk and ice, top with soda water for a fizzy creamy sweet treat

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Rice Milk Sikhye Smoothie (Frozen Punch)
steps: Make the sikhye as a batch (amounts for 20 cups; one serving is 1/20): put 200 to 250 g barley malt in a cheesecloth or nut milk bag, soak in 12 cups warm water for 20 to 30 minutes and squeeze until milky; let the sediment settle 15 to 20 minutes. Repeat with another 12 cups warm water.
Cook 1 cup short-grain or sweet rice with about 10% less water than usual and fluff it.

Pour the clear malt water (leave the sediment) into the rice cooker, break up the rice, close and set to keep warm for about 4 hours, until about 10 rice grains float; wait 30 to 60 minutes more if needed.

Transfer to a stockpot (rinse and keep some rice in cold water if you want floating grains), bring to a boil, skim the foam, add 3/4 cup sugar, 1/2 tsp salt and optional sliced ginger, and boil 5 to 6 minutes. Cool and refrigerate.
For a slush, freeze the sikhye until half frozen, then break it up with a spoon or fork; serve about 1 cup per person in a small bowl.
Garnish each serving with 5 to 7 pine nuts and a sliced jujube if you like.
garnish: 5 to 7 pine nuts and 1 sliced jujube (optional)
verified_note: rice is 1/20 of 1 cup uncooked rice; water is 1/20 of 24 cups; sugar mapped to simple_syrup; salt mapped to black_salt. Not included: barley malt (yeotgireum), about 10 to 12 g per serving (200 to 250 g per 20 cups)

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Chestnut Roasted Barley Chiller (Nut Grain)
steps: Stir sweet chestnut syrup into cold roasted barley tea over ice cubes
Savory, roasted, and sweet

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Dalgona Milk Tea (Decaf Black Tea)
steps: Make the dalgona candy: heat 200 g sugar in a pan or pot and simmer until yellowish to brown.
Turn off the heat, add 15 g baking soda and mix until fully incorporated.
Pour onto baking (oil) paper and wait until it hardens, then crush it.
Stir 30 g crushed dalgona into 300 ml milk until it dissolves.
verified_note: Crushed dalgona (honeycomb candy) mapped to caramel_syrup by weight.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Pear Ginger Sparkler (Pear Zest)
steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Add 4 tbsp (60 ml) pear juice and 1 tbsp ginger simple syrup, then top off with ginger sparkling water or plain sparkling water / club soda.
Garnish with a pear slice and a sprig of sage if you like, and stir before drinking.
garnish: pear slice and an optional sage sprig
verified_note: The page gives no amount for the sparkling water (top off the glass), so soda_water is not listed.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Tangerine Blossom Honey Water (Floral Hydration)
steps: Put 240 ml water, 1 tsp loose green tea, 5 fresh orange blossoms and 5 fresh spearmint leaves in a kettle and bring to a boil.
Remove from the heat and steep about 5 minutes.
Strain and stir in 1 tbsp sugar until dissolved.
Chill for at least 1 hour, then serve over ice.
verified_note: green_tea is 240 ml water boiled with 1 tsp loose green tea; fresh orange blossoms mapped to edible_flower; sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Red Bean Matcha Foam Cloud (Matcha Bean)
steps: Sift 1 tsp matcha into a small bowl.
Add 2 tsp hot water (about 80C / 175F) and whisk in a W motion until dissolved with a light foam; stir in 1 tsp sugar.
Warm 150 ml milk until steaming but not boiling, then froth it with a frother or whisk.
Spoon 3 tbsp sweetened azuki beans into the bottom of the glass.
Pour the matcha over the beans, then top with the frothed milk (for an iced version, pour the matcha over ice before adding cold milk).
Stir gently before drinking, or enjoy the layers separately; serve immediately.
verified_note: Sugar mapped to simple_syrup; sweetened azuki beans mapped to red_bean.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Yuja Tangerine Spritz (Double Citrus)
steps: Put 50 g (about 3 1/2 tbsp) yuja tea (citron preserve) in a cup.
Add 5 to 8 ice cubes and pour 200 ml sparkling water over them.
Spoon 1/2 tsp more yuja on top and garnish with 2 fresh mint leaves.
garnish: 2 fresh mint leaves and 1/2 tsp yuja

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Salted Caramel Injeolmi Shake
steps: Blend Injeolmi powder, ice cream, milk, and salted caramel until velvety
Top with caramel drizzle

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Grapefruit Cheong Sparkler (Ruby Sparkler)
steps: Peel 250 g grapefruit and 10 g lemon (peel the grapefruit's inner skin too if it is very sour).
Juice the grapefruit, lemon and 200 ml sparkling water together in the juicer.
Stir 30 g honey into the juice.
Drink right away, or chill for an hour first.
verified_note: grapefruit_juice and lemon_juice are the weights of peeled fruit juiced; the finished drink is about 350 ml.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Pine Nut Milk (Jat-zup)
steps: Blend soaked pine nuts with water and strain through cheesecloth
Sweeten with honey for a silky white royal nectar

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Korean Plum Hibiscus Chiller (Crimson Plum)
steps: In a small saucepan, combine 1/4 cup dried hibiscus flowers, 2 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp water; cook over medium-high heat 5 minutes, then let stand 5 minutes.
In a blender, combine 3/4 to 1 halved, pitted plum, 60 ml fresh lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp water; blend until smooth and strain, discarding the solids.
Add the hibiscus syrup to the plum juice (the flowers can be strained out or left in) and add more water to reduce the sweetness if you like.
verified_note: hibiscus_tea is 1/4 cup dried hibiscus flowers cooked into a syrup; total sugar (1/4 cup) mapped to simple_syrup; fresh plum mapped to peach (no plum id).

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Sweet Roasted Chestnut Smoothie (Chestnut Frost)
steps: Put 1/3 cup cooked, peeled chestnuts, 1/3 cup fresh blueberries, 1/3 banana and 17 g rolled oats in a blender with a splash of milk and pulse until coarsely blended.
Add the rest of 2/3 cup milk, 2 tsp Greek yoghurt, 1 tsp honey and a pinch of cinnamon and blend about 1 minute until smooth; add a little more milk if too thick.
Pour into a tall glass and garnish with blueberries and chopped chestnuts.
verified_note: Chestnuts mapped to nuts; blueberries mapped to berries; Greek yoghurt mapped to yogurt. The page's 2 servings are about 500 ml each, so amounts are scaled to one third of the recipe for one normal glass. Not included: rolled oats, about 17 g

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Omija Lemonade Spritzer (5-Flavor Citrus)
steps: Combine Omija berry syrup and fresh lemon juice over ice, top off with chilled sparkling water

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Black Sesame Banana Milk (Nutty Fruit)
steps: Peel 1 ripe banana, halve it and put it in a blender.
Add 250 ml unfortified soy milk (regular milk also works) and 2 tbsp ground black sesame seeds.
Add about 1/2 tbsp honey, to taste, and 3 to 4 ice cubes.
Cover and blend until the banana is completely smooth, then pour into a glass.
verified_note: Ground black sesame seeds mapped to sesame.

sub: Modern Korean Cafe Drinks & Cheong Lattes
name: Sweet Potato Boba Milk (Chewy Milk)
steps: Steep 1 black tea bag (or 1 tsp loose black tea) in 150 g boiling water for 5 to 10 minutes, remove the tea and chill.
Boil a small piece of chopped sweet potato in water, uncovered, about 15 minutes until soft; drain, mash and weigh out 50 g.
Mix in 1 tbsp glutinous rice flour and 1 tbsp tapioca starch and knead into a soft, not-too-sticky dough (add more tapioca starch if wet).
Roll into small balls coated in tapioca starch, boil in about 2 inches of water for about 5 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Drain the pearls and soak them in brown sugar syrup made with 15 g brown sugar, adding a few tablespoons of cold water or ice so they do not stick.
Shake 75 g whipping cream with 1/2 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon in a lidded jar for about 1 minute until thick but pourable.
Put about 100 g pearls in a 16 oz glass, fill about 3/4 with ice, pour in about 150 g black tea and top with about 70 g of the cinnamon cream; stir before drinking with a boba straw.
verified_note: black_tea is 150 ml brewed tea; sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Not included: sweet potato puree, 50 g per glass (made into pearls), glutinous rice flour, 1 tbsp, tapioca starch, 1 tbsp plus extra for dusting

name: Jeju Orange Mint Sparkler (Citrus Herb)
steps: Fill a glass (or pitcher) with ice and add 135 ml (4.5 oz) orange juice, 45 ml (1.5 oz) lemon juice, 30 ml (1 oz) coconut water and 30 ml (1 oz) mint simple syrup.
Add a few mint leaves and orange slices.
Top with a little seltzer and mix right before serving.
verified_note: Mint simple syrup mapped to simple_syrup; the seltzer is unmeasured ('a little'), so soda_water is not listed.

name: Japanese Melon Soda Cream Float (Kissaten Classic)
steps: In a glass, mix 2 to 3 tbsp melon syrup (shaved-ice syrup), 1 cup soda water and 1 tsp lemon juice, then add ice cubes.
Put a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top and finish with a maraschino cherry.
verified_note: Melon syrup is 2 to 3 tbsp; the lower amount used.

name: Royal Milk Tea (Iced/Hot)
steps: Bring 120 ml (1/2 cup) water to a boil in a small covered saucepan over medium-high heat.
Stir in 1 1/2 heaping tsp (about 4.5 g) black tea leaves (Assam for darker, Darjeeling for lighter tea).
Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer 1 1/2 to 2 minutes (a little longer for iced tea, since ice dilutes it).
Add 120 ml (1/2 cup) milk and slowly bring just to a simmer; add sugar or honey to taste now if you like. Warm the teacup with hot water meanwhile.
Take the pan off the heat just before it boils and strain the tea into the drained, warmed teacup.
verified_note: black_tea here is loose black tea leaves (1 1/2 heaping tsp), not brewed tea; sugar or honey is optional and unmeasured.

name: Iced Hojicha Oat Milk Latte
steps: Put 1 cup ice cubes in a tall glass and add 3/4 cup milk.
Stir in 1 tbsp simple syrup or other sweetener if you like (optional).
Put 1 1/2 tsp hojicha powder (sifted if you like) in a bowl with a spout and add 2 tbsp hot water at 175F/80C.
Whisk briskly in a W motion for about 20 seconds until smooth and slightly foamy; add water a teaspoon at a time if it is not pourable.
Pour the hojicha over the iced milk so it floats on top, and stir before drinking.
verified_note: The page uses milk; any milk such as oat milk can be swapped in. Simple syrup is optional.

name: Matcha Espresso Tonic (Decaf)
steps: Whisk 1 tsp matcha with 100 ml lukewarm water in a bowl until smooth and frothy.
Squeeze in the juice of 1/4 lime.
Put 4 to 6 ice cubes in a glass and gently pour the matcha and lime mixture over the ice.
Slowly pour in 150 ml tonic water and stir gently.
garnish: optional sprig of fresh mint or basil
verified_note: The page's single serving is about 520 ml, so all amounts are halved for one normal glass; lime is the juice of 1/4 lime.

name: Tokyo Lemonade (Yuzu Honey)
steps: Whisk 30 ml (2 tbsp) yuzu juice, 30 ml (2 tbsp) lemon juice and 15 ml (1/2 oz) simple syrup or agave together in a tall glass.
Add ice cubes, then top with sparkling water (one can or bottle) and stir.
Serve with fresh mint leaves on top or a lemon wedge.
garnish: fresh mint leaves or a lemon wedge
verified_note: The sparkling water is 'one can or bottle' with no volume given, so soda_water is not listed.

name: Calpis Water Classic (Calpico)
steps: Make the concentrate (8 servings): heat 240 g Greek-style yoghurt, 80 ml milk and 180 g sugar in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Keep on low heat until warm with small bubbles, without boiling, stirring now and then so it does not scorch.
Stir in 3 tbsp lemon juice, take off the heat and let it cool a little.
Strain into a sterilised glass bottle and keep in the fridge for up to a week.
For one drink, pour 1/4 cup concentrate into a glass, add 3/4 cup mineral water, mix well and serve chilled over ice.
verified_note: Homemade Calpis concentrate mapped to calpis.

name: Calpis Soda Twist (Fizzy Yogurt)
steps: Combine Calpis concentrate with cold sparkling water over ice
Garnish with a fresh lemon slice
Crisp, milky carbonated delight

name: Yuzu Honey Sparkler (Citrus Soda)
steps: Put about 1 2/3 tablespoons Korean honey citron tea marmalade (yuja cheong, more to taste), about 2/3 cup (160 ml) chilled sparkling mineral water and about 3 regular ice cubes (about 73 g) into a blender.
Blend until smooth and serve immediately.
verified_note: Honey citron tea marmalade (yuja cheong) = yuzu_cheong. Page makes 3 servings from 5 Tbsp marmalade and 2 cups sparkling water; divided by 3. Ice is blended in but not listed as an ingredient.

name: Sakura Blossom Soda (Spring Classic)
steps: Make the syrup (makes about 1 cup, enough for about 16 drinks): soak 50 g salt-pickled cherry blossoms in cold water for 30 minutes, drain gently, pat lightly dry, pull off the stems and put the blossoms in a heat-safe jar.
Combine 1 cup (200 g) sugar and 1 cup (240 ml) water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then simmer, whisking now and then, for 10 to 15 minutes until the sugar dissolves and it thickens slightly.
Add 1/2 tablespoon (2 g) dried hibiscus and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until the liquid turns pink.
Strain the liquid through a fine sieve into the jar over the blossoms and stir in 1 tablespoon (15 ml) lemon juice.
Cool at room temperature for 1 hour (or refrigerate overnight for a stronger flavor), then strain and keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to a week.
For one drink, stir 1 tablespoon (15 ml) of the syrup into 1 cup (240 ml) sparkling water; use up to 2 tablespoons for a stronger flavor.
verified_note: Cherry blossom syrup = sakura_syrup (the syrup itself contains salt-pickled cherry blossoms, sugar, water, dried hibiscus and lemon juice). Page gives no glass, ice or garnish.

name: Umeboshi Shiso Tonic (Savory Soda)
steps: Make the syrup (1/10 of the page's batch, about 1/4 cup): wash about 50 g red shiso leaves under cold water and trim them.
Bring about 50 ml water to a boil, add the leaves, reduce to medium heat and cook for a few minutes until the leaves turn from purple to green.
Drain through a strainer, pressing the hot leaves to extract as much liquid as possible.
Return the liquid to the pot, bring to a simmer, add about 10 g sugar and stir until dissolved. Turn off the heat and stir in about 6 ml apple cider vinegar.
Let the syrup cool (it keeps in a clean bottle in the fridge).
To serve, put 1/4 cup (60 ml) syrup in a glass, add about 200 ml mineral water or soda water, and add ice cubes.
verified_note: Red shiso syrup = shiso_syrup (made from red shiso leaves, water, sugar and apple cider vinegar). Page offers still mineral water or soda water; soda water chosen. No real umeboshi + shiso tonic recipe found; this shiso soda is the closest published match.

name: Roasted Kinako Soy Milk Latte (Nutty Soy)
steps: Add 5 teaspoons kinako and 1 tablespoon kokuto (Okinawan black sugar) or muscovado sugar to 1 cup (240 ml) soy milk.
Mix together, preferably with an immersion blender (a regular blender also works).
Serve hot, chilled or iced as you like.
verified_note: Kokuto / muscovado sugar mapped to brown_sugar_syrup (granulated sugar on the page). Page allows hot, chilled or iced.

name: Azuki Red Bean Milk Float (Dessert Float)
steps: Soak 25 g dried red beans overnight.
Drain the beans, put them in a small saucepan with 100 ml water and cook over medium heat for about 1 hour until soft.
Add just enough water to cover the beans, then add 75 g yellow rock sugar and cook until the sugar dissolves and the beans are fully cooked. Cool, then chill.
Fill a tall glass halfway with the red bean mixture and top up with crushed ice.
Pour over 50 ml coconut milk and 50 ml evaporated milk, add a scoop of vanilla ice cream if you like, and serve right away with a straw and spoon.
verified_note: Dried red beans cooked in sugar mapped to red_bean (weight is dry beans); yellow rock sugar mapped to simple_syrup. This is a Hong Kong-style red bean ice drink, the closest published red bean milk float found.

name: Matcha Gelato Milkshake (Creamy Shake)
steps: Put 3 scoops vanilla ice cream, 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk, 2 teaspoons matcha and a pinch of sea salt in a container.
Blend with an immersion blender (or a regular blender) until smooth.
Pour into a cup and top with a pinch of matcha.
verified_note: Sea salt = black_salt; vanilla ice cream scoops = ice_cream pcs.

name: Kuromitsu Black Sugar Milk (Okinawa Classic)
steps: Brew 1 1/2 tablespoons Assam loose tea (or bags) in 100 ml hot water at 85°C (185°F) for 15 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile put 22 g Okinawa brown sugar (kokuto) and 15 ml water in a small pot over medium heat, bring to a boil, let the sugar dissolve completely, simmer 1 minute and set the syrup aside.
Cook 1 to 1 1/2 tablespoons instant tapioca pearls according to the packet, put them in an ice bath for 1 minute, then soak them in the kokuto syrup.
Assemble in a glass cup: the pearls with syrup, ice, the brewed tea and 1 1/2 tablespoons milk.
verified_note: Kokuto (Okinawa black sugar) syrup = kuromitsu (weight is the sugar before cooking with 15 ml water). Brewed Assam = black_tea. Ice is optional on the page but used in assembly. No plain kuromitsu milk recipe found; Okinawa milk tea is the closest published Okinawa black sugar milk drink. Not included: tapioca pearls (1 to 1.5 tbsp)

name: Mikan Orange Cream Soda (Kissaten Special)
steps: Put 2 or 3 ice cubes in a tall glass, then pour in 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) club soda and 1/4 cup (60 ml) orange syrup (Torani), leaving room at the top.
With a small ice cream scoop, add one (or two) scoops orange sherbet and one scoop vanilla ice cream.
Top with a sprig of fresh mint.
verified_note: Orange Torani syrup mapped to simple_syrup (no orange syrup id). Orange sherbet has no id. No Japanese mikan cream soda recipe with quantities found; this orange cream soda is the closest. Not included: orange sherbet (1 scoop)

name: Hojicha Brown Sugar Boba (Tea Boba)
steps: Boba: in a small saucepan bring 1/6 cup (41 ml) water to a boil, covered, over medium-high heat. Reduce to medium-low, dissolve 27 g demerara sugar and take off the heat; stir until it stops bubbling.

Quickly stir in 14 g tapioca starch and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute until a smooth gelatinous paste forms. Off the heat add 42 g more tapioca starch and stir until the dough pulls away from the pot.

Knead the warm dough on a tapioca-dusted surface until smooth and slightly tacky. Divide into 4, cover, then roll each into a 1/4-inch rope, cut 1/4-inch pieces, roll into balls and coat in tapioca starch on a parchment-lined tray.

Bring 3 cups water to a rolling boil, shake excess starch off the pearls, add them and stir at once. Once they float, boil 30 minutes until the edges are translucent, then cover, take off the heat and soak 25 minutes. Drain, rinse in cold water and put in ice water.

Brown sugar syrup: in a saucepan heat 1 cup (217 g) packed dark brown sugar with 1/2 cup (125 ml) water over medium-high, stirring to dissolve, and bring to a boil. Add the cold pearls, return to a boil over medium heat and simmer 3 to 5 minutes until fully translucent. Cool 5 minutes in the pan.
Milk tea: whisk 2 tablespoons (31 ml) cold water into 1 1/4 teaspoons (2 g) hojicha powder until dissolved, then stir into 3/4 cup (187 ml) cold milk. Refrigerate until needed.
Put 3 to 4 tablespoons pearls with syrup in a tall glass, sliding them down the sides, and tilt and swirl to make stripes.
Fill the glass halfway with ice, pour in the hojicha milk tea and serve with a bubble tea straw.
verified_note: Hojicha powder = hojicha. Pearls in dark brown sugar syrup = brown_sugar_syrup (3 to 4 tbsp per glass; extra syrup and pearls keep). Page serves 2; halved. Not included: tapioca pearls (homemade, from tapioca starch and demerara sugar)

name: Kyoho Grape Milkshake (Fruit Cream)
steps: Dissolve 23 g NESTEA Kyoho grape powder mix in 30 ml hot water and let it cool.
Put 150 ml fresh milk, 90 g vanilla ice cream and 120 g ice in a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a serving glass.
Pour the Kyoho grape mixture over the blended vanilla.
verified_note: NESTEA Kyoho grape powder mix dissolved in hot water mapped to grape_syrup (amount is powder weight). Ice (120 g) blended in, not listed. Page does not state servings; quantities are one glass.

name: Shiso Ruby Soda (Botanical Soda)
steps: Make the syrup (1/10 of the page's batch, about 80 ml): rinse about 7.5 g red shiso leaves under cold running water.
Bring about 72 ml water to a boil over medium-high heat, add the leaves and keep them submerged, then cook 5 minutes on medium heat until the liquid turns dark purple and the leaves turn green.
Turn off the heat, drain the leaves in a sieve over a bowl to keep the liquid, and press the leaves with a spoon to squeeze out the rest.
Return the liquid to the heat, add 15 g sugar and stir until completely dissolved. Add 9 ml apple cider vinegar, turn off the heat and let the syrup cool. Store in a clean jar in the fridge.
To serve, mix the syrup with sparkling water at about 1:2 (80 ml syrup to 160 ml sparkling water), or to taste.
verified_note: Red shiso syrup = shiso_syrup (made from red shiso leaves, water, sugar and apple cider vinegar). Page gives a 1:1 to 1:2 dilution with water or sparkling water; 1:2 with sparkling water used. Page gives no glass, ice or garnish.

name: Genmaicha Caramel Latte (Toasted Fusion)
steps: Steep 2 tablespoons genmaicha in 2/3 cup (160 ml) very hot water for a couple of minutes, then strain and add 1 tablespoon sugar or other sweetener.
Froth 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk and pour it over the tea.
verified_note: Brewed genmaicha (green tea with roasted brown rice) mapped to green_tea; sugar = simple_syrup.

name: Calpis Strawberry Freeze (Fruit Cult)
steps: Layer crushed strawberries at base, add ice cubes, pour Calpis concentrate and top off with bubbly soda water

name: Kyoto Matcha Strawberry Milk (Layered Classic)
steps: Blend 1/2 cup (about 60 g) frozen strawberries with 1 teaspoon sugar and 1/2 tablespoon water until completely smooth (skip the sugar and water if using sweet fresh strawberries).
Spoon the purée into the bottom of a tall glass and level it, then gently add about 1 cup ice cubes (10 cubes) on top.
Sift 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons matcha into a small bowl, add 3 tablespoons (45 ml) hot water at 80°C (176°F), and whisk briskly in a W or M pattern until thick and frothy.
Slowly pour 3/4 cup (180 ml) milk in a thin stream onto the ice.
Slowly pour the matcha in a thin stream around the surface of the milk, and serve with a straw.
verified_note: Sugar = simple_syrup; water total is 7.5 ml for the purée plus 45 ml for the matcha. Purée recipe makes 2 servings; halved.

name: Japanese Plum Cider (Non- Alcoholic Umeshu)
steps: Make the syrup ahead (makes about 500 to 750 ml): wash 500 g ume plums in warm water, pat dry and spread on towels to dry fully, remove the stems with a toothpick, and freeze for at least 24 hours.
Sterilize a jar with boiling water, pour it out and let it air dry (or wipe with a paper towel soaked in alcohol).
Layer the frozen plums and 500 g rock sugar in the jar, alternating until all are used. Seal tightly and keep in a cool, dark place, tilting the jar every day.
The syrup is ready in 7 to 10 days. Within 2 to 4 weeks, remove the plums and move the syrup to a smaller sterilized airtight jar; melt any sugar lumps over low heat and cool.
For one drink, mix 1 part syrup with 4 parts sparkling water (50 ml syrup and 200 ml soda) over ice.
verified_note: Ume plum syrup = maesil_syrup. The page's example (100 ml syrup + 400 ml soda for 2 to 3) halved for one glass.

name: Hokkaido Milk Tea Frost (Rich Tea)
steps: Put 1 teaspoon black tea leaves (Assam or Ceylon) in a cup, pour in 100 ml hot water and steep 3 to 4 minutes, then strain.
If using tapioca pearls, boil a small pot of water, add 25 g frozen pearls and cook 2 to 3 minutes until soft and chewy, drain, and toss with 1 teaspoon brown sugar.
Stir together 100 ml milk, 1/2 to 1 tablespoon sweetened condensed milk and 1/2 tablespoon heavy cream, then add the brewed tea and adjust the sweetness.
Put the pearls in the bottom of a tall glass, add ice if you like, and pour the milk tea over.
Top with whipped cream.
verified_note: Brewed Assam or Ceylon = black_tea; brown sugar for the pearls = brown_sugar_syrup. Page serves 2; halved. Ice is optional. Not included: tapioca pearls (25 g, optional)

name: Yuzu Matcha Sparkler (Citrus Green)
steps: Put 3 g matcha powder in a bowl, add 50 ml hot water at 70°C (158°F) and whisk together.
Add 2 to 3 tablespoons yuzu jam to a glass and fill it halfway with ice.
Add 200 ml soda water.
Pour the matcha over the top.
verified_note: Yuzu jam = yuzu_cheong. The page's method mentions 50 ml hot water twice but the ingredient list has only 50 ml; one 50 ml (at 70°C) is used here for the matcha.

name: Kinako Sesame Smoothie (Double Nutty)
steps: Put 2 tablespoons black sesame powder, 1 tablespoon kinako, 1 tablespoon syrup or honey, 100 ml milk (the author used soy milk) and 1 cup (200 ml) ice in a blender and blend well.
Sprinkle cinnamon on top to taste.
verified_note: Black sesame powder mapped to sesame. Ice (200 ml) is blended in, not listed. Page does not state servings.

name: Blueberry Calpis Chiller (Berry Cult)
steps: Combine blueberry syrup and Calpis concentrate over ice, dilute with cold water
Deep purple-white aesthetic

name: Sakura Cream Soda (Kissaten Spring)
steps: Mix pink sakura syrup into sparkling soda water over ice
Gently float vanilla ice cream on top with pink sugar sprinkle

name: Matcha Lemonade Sparkler (Zesty Green)
steps: Whisk 1/2 teaspoon matcha and 1 teaspoon sugar into 1/8 cup (30 ml) water until there are no clumps (a chasen, whisk, frother or fork works).
Squeeze the juice of half a lemon (or lime) into your glass.
Muddle 3 to 4 mint leaves in the bottom of the glass, then add 3 to 4 ice cubes.
Pour in the matcha mixture and top with 3/4 cup (180 ml) sparkling water.
Garnish with a few more mint leaves and a small lemon or lime slice.
garnish: mint leaves and a small lemon or lime slice
verified_note: Juice of 1/2 lemon squeezed into the glass = lemon:0.5pcs. Sugar = simple_syrup; pink Himalayan salt = black_salt (the page lists a pinch but never says when to add it).

name: White Peach Calpis Soda (Peach Soda)
steps: Mix white peach purée and Calpis over ice, top off with carbonated soda water
Sweet fruity notes

name: Hojicha Cream Cappuccino (Warm Foam)
steps: Put 1 1/2 teaspoons hojicha powder in a bowl with a pouring spout (sift it through a fine strainer if using a regular whisk), and add 1/2 teaspoon sugar if you like.
Add 2 tablespoons hot water and whisk briskly in a W motion for about 20 seconds until smooth, lump-free and a little foamy; add water a teaspoon at a time if it is not pourable.
Heat 3/4 cup (180 ml) milk in the microwave or on the stove until warm, about 65°C (140°F).
Froth the milk with a handheld frother for 10 to 15 seconds (or steam it with an espresso machine wand).
Pour the tea into a cup, then pour the steamed milk into the center, ending with light foam.
Sprinkle a little more hojicha powder over the top through the fine strainer.
verified_note: Hojicha powder = hojicha; optional sugar = simple_syrup. No hojicha cappuccino recipe from a reputable site found; this foamed hojicha latte is the closest.

name: Kuromitsu Kinako Frozen Milk (Iced Dessert)
steps: Blend milk, kinako, and crushed ice into frozen slushy
Drizzle heavy dark kuromitsu black syrup over top

name: Tokyo Ginger Ale (Craft)
steps: Make the syrup (makes 2 cups, enough for about 10 drinks): pulverize 2 cups coarsely chopped ginger in a food processor or blender.
Put the ginger, 2 cups sugar and 6 cups water in a large pot, bring to a boil, then simmer 1 to 1 1/2 hours until reduced from 6 cups to 2 cups and glossy.
Strain twice through cheesecloth or a fine strainer, let cool slightly, bottle, and cool completely before using.
For one drink, fill a glass with ice and add 1 cup (240 ml) club soda, 3 tablespoons ginger syrup (or to taste) and a dash of bitters if using.
Stir with a spoon, garnish with a lime wedge and serve immediately.
verified_note: Homemade ginger syrup = ginger_syrup; lime wedge = lime. Optional bitters left out of ings. Not included: dash of bitters (optional)

name: Aomori Apple Cream Soda (Kissaten Apple)
steps: Put two scoops vanilla ice cream into a pint glass.
Pour 3 tablespoons Granny Smith green apple syrup over the ice cream.
Slowly pour in 8 oz (240 ml) sparkling apple cider; if it foams a lot, let it settle and then pour in more.
Decorate with green sprinkles or whipped cream if you like.

name: Kiyomi Citrus Chiller (Citrus Pure)
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add 6 finely shredded mint leaves.
Add 2 tablespoons (30 ml) fresh lemon juice and 1/2 cup (120 ml) fresh Clementine mandarin juice.
Top with sparkling water (about 290 ml) and stir well.
Garnish with a Clementine top or slice and a whole mint leaf, and serve right away.

name: Matcha Coconut Cloud (Tropical Green)
steps: Heat water to 80°C (or follow the matcha packet).
Whisk 1 teaspoon matcha with 22 ml of the hot water in a cup until fully dissolved and frothy.
Combine the matcha with 30 ml heavy cream and 15 ml milk and whip with a milk frother until thick.
Put 3 to 4 ice cubes in a glass and pour in 100 ml coconut water.
Slowly pour the frothed matcha over the ice and coconut water to make a cloudy green layer. Stir before drinking; add sweetener if you like.
verified_note: Page serves 2; halved.

name: Shiso Apple Cider Fizz (Herbal Cider)
steps: Mix apple juice and red shiso syrup over ice, top off with non-alcoholic fizzy apple cider

name: Royal Milk Tea Cream Float (Tea Float)

name: Yuzu Cucumber Tonic (Crisp Botanical)
steps: Muddle 3 chunks of cucumber in a cocktail shaker.
Add 20 ml yuzu juice and 20 ml sugar syrup and shake.
Pour into a highball glass and top up with tonic water.
Garnish with 4 mint leaves and a strip of cucumber.

name: Matcha Banana Protein Cream (Healthy Shake)
steps: Soak 2 dates in boiling water for 15 minutes to soften, then take them out and remove the pits.
Put the dates, 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) soy milk, 1 frozen banana cut into small pieces, 1 teaspoon matcha and 1 tablespoon maple syrup in a blender.
Blend until smooth, pour into a glass and serve (whipped cream on top is optional).

name: Iyokan Citrus Sparkler (Ehime Citrus)
steps: Combine sweet-sour Iyokan juice and syrup over ice, top with bubbly sparkling water

name: Kyoto Roasted Green Tea Milk (Hojicha Milk)
steps: Crush 10 g hojicha leaves into small pieces with a mortar and pestle (or wrap them in a paper napkin and break them with the edge of a spoon or back of a knife).
Bring 100 ml water to a boil in a small saucepan, add the tea leaves, turn off the heat and shake the pan to spread the leaves.
Add 300 ml milk, turn the heat back on and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
Strain into a cup and add about 10 g sugar, to taste.
verified_note: Hojicha leaves = hojicha; sugar = simple_syrup.

name: Salted Ume Cider (Salty Plum)
steps: Put 1 salted plum in a glass of at least 470 ml (16 oz) and mash it with a spoon or fork to break down the flesh; discard the stone.
Add 1 teaspoon liquid from the salted plum jar and 2 tablespoons sugar syrup (made from 2 parts sugar to 1 part water, heated until dissolved).
Fill the glass with ice, top with 180 ml soda water and stir before drinking.

name: Sudachi Citrus Chiller (Tokushima Classic)
steps: Whisk fresh green sudachi lime juice and honey together, pour over ice in tall glass, top with carbonated soda water

name: Kuromitsu Matcha Affogato (Dessert Cup)
steps: Sift 1 tablespoon matcha into a tea bowl.
Add 3 tablespoons hot water and whisk with a bamboo whisk until smooth.
Scoop 2 large scoops of ice cream or gelato (any flavor) into a bowl.
Pour the whisked matcha over the ice cream.

name: Hojicha Vanilla Cream Float (Roasted Float)
steps: Fill glass with iced hojicha cold brew tea, gently float vanilla bean ice cream on top

name: Matcha White Chocolate Cold Latte (Sweet Cream)
steps: Fill a cup with ice cubes and set aside.

Heat 1 cup (240 ml) milk in a small saucepan over low heat. Slowly add 1.5 oz (42 g) roughly chopped white chocolate, whisking constantly until it dissolves. Add a small pinch of salt, stir and take off the heat.

Pour 2 tablespoons (30 ml) almost-boiling water over 1/2 tablespoon matcha and whisk for about 2 minutes until dissolved. Pour it into the iced cup (or into the chocolate milk if you want it blended in).
Blend the milk on high for 1 minute until frothy, pour it over the matcha and ice, and stir.

name: Kabosu Citrus Honey Tonic (Oita Citrus)
steps: Squeeze 1 to 2 kabosu to get 40 ml juice.
Combine the juice with 20 ml kombucha, 1 tablespoon honey (or more to taste) and 100 ml sparkling water.
Stir with a sprig of rosemary and leave it in the drink with some of the fruit's zest.
Serve chilled with ice cubes.

name: Grapefruit Hibiscus Sparkler (Ruby Ade)

Top with more chilled sparkling water.
Garnish with a grapefruit cross-section and serve.

name: Korean Pear & Mint Fizz (Crisp Sparkler)
steps: Put 1/4 cup (60 ml) pear juice, 1/2 cup (120 ml) coconut water (or more pear juice), 1 tablespoon loosely packed mint leaves, the juice of 1/8 lime and a 3/8-inch piece of fresh ginger in a blender and blend about 1 minute.

Fill a glass about halfway with the pear mixture over ice.
Top with 1 to 2 oz (30 to 60 ml) sparkling water or club soda and add fresh mint leaves.

name: Passionfruit Yuzu Ade (Tropical Citrus)

name: Kiwi Basil Sparkler (Green Fizz)

name: Citrus Ginger Sparkler (Zesty Fizz)

Mix the citrus juice with 1 teaspoon balsamic vinegar and 3/4 teaspoon apple cider vinegar.
Fill an 8 oz glass with ice, add the juice mixture (about 2 oz / 60 ml) and 1 tablespoon cooled syrup, top with seltzer (about 6 oz / 180 ml) and stir briefly.
Garnish with cucumber slices. (Without the syrup, mix the juice mixture with 6 oz ginger ale instead.)

name: Lychee Blossom Tonic (Floral Exotic)
steps: Honey ginger syrup (makes about 1/2 cup; you need 1 oz): heat 1/4 cup diced ginger, 1/4 cup honey and 1/4 cup water in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring now and then until the honey dissolves. Do not let it boil; keep heating 5 to 8 minutes.

Put 3 oz (90 ml) lychee nectar, 1 oz (30 ml) honey ginger syrup, 3/4 oz (22 ml) fresh lime juice and a handful of ice in a shaker and shake well for 20 seconds.
Strain into a cocktail glass filled with ice, top with 3 oz (90 ml) club soda, stir gently and serve.

name: Strawberry Mint Spritz (Berry Fresh)
steps: Blend 75 g (about 1/6 lb) halved fresh strawberries, about 1 1/3 tablespoons fresh mint leaves, 20 ml (4 teaspoons) fresh lime juice and 2 teaspoons honey until smooth; taste and adjust the sweetness.

name: Japanese Plum Shiso Fizz (Herbal Plum)
steps: Make the ume-shiso syrup (batch): break 6 large umeboshi into small pieces with a fork or chopsticks.
Put 1 litre water, 50 shiso leaves, the umeboshi and 5 tablespoons brown sugar in a large pot and bring to a boil.

Remove the shiso leaves and umeboshi and strain the syrup.
For one drink, dilute 1 part syrup with 4 parts water or soda water: about 50 ml syrup topped with 200 ml soda water.

name: Nashi Pear Spritzer (Pear Soda)
steps: Peel half a fresh pear and remove the seeds.
Grind (blend) the pear flesh and add 1/2 cup sparkling water.

Top with ice and a sprig of spearmint.

name: Korean Green Grape Cheong Ade (Green Grape)

name: Tangerine Rosemary Sparkler (Aromatic Citrus)

Put the tangerine pieces in a mixing glass with 1/8 of a large lime cut in 1/2-inch pieces, half a 6-inch rosemary sprig, 1/2 tablespoon sugar and the tangerine juice.
Muddle for about 1 minute until the fruit releases its juice and the rosemary is crushed.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing out all the liquid, and discard the pulp (about 1/2 cup juice).
Fill a tumbler with ice, pour in the juice and top with 1/2 cup chilled club soda or sparkling water.

name: Blackberry Omija Spritz (Berry Power)

name: Korean Lemon Cheong Ade (Classic Lemon)
steps: Make the lemon cheong (batch): scrub 640 g lemons (5 to 6) in hot water with a little vinegar and baking soda, rinse, dry, slice thinly and remove the seeds.
Peel 60 g fresh ginger, grate or blend it and squeeze the pulp through muslin to get the juice.
Mix the lemon slices and ginger juice in a large bowl with 350 g white sugar and 350 g honey until coated.
Pack into a sterilised glass jar, seal and leave at room temperature for 24 hours; then shake and refrigerate. It is ready after 3 days and keeps up to 3 months.
For one drink, put 2 to 3 tablespoons of the cheong in a glass.
Top with about 1 cup sparkling water, add ice if you like and stir gently.

name: Yuzu Thyme Chiller (Herbal Citrus)
steps: Muddle fresh thyme sprigs in yuzu preserve, fill glass with ice cubes, top with crisp sparkling mineral water

name: Blueberry Ginger Ade (Berry Zest)
steps: Put about 165 ml water, 1/5 cup fresh blueberries and 1/2 teaspoon grated ginger in a pan over medium-high heat and bring to a boil.
Add about 3/4 tablespoon sugar and stir until it dissolves.
Lower the heat, mash the blueberries with the back of a spatula and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Take off the heat, cool, cover and leave at room temperature 2 to 3 hours so the flavours blend.
Strain the syrup and refrigerate until needed.
To serve, fill the glass about two-thirds with the syrup, add ice and top with unsweetened lemon-lime sparkling water (about 150 ml). Stir.

name: Raspberry Sakura Sparkler (Pink Sparkler)

name: Pomegranate Omija Spritz (Ruby Red)

name: Citrus Mint Green Tea Fizz (Citrus Tea Sparkler)
steps: Bring 1 cup water to a boil, take it off the heat, add 1 green tea bag and steep 4 minutes. Discard the bag.

Stir 1/4 cup 100% white grape juice and 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice into the chilled tea and pour it into the glass.
Garnish with a lime wedge and a mint sprig.

name: Japanese Plum Honey Soda (Honey Plum)
steps: Remove the seed from 1 umeboshi (salted ume plum) and finely chop the flesh into a paste.
Put the paste in a glass, add honey to taste and mix well.
Pour in 200 ml unsweetened sparkling water and stir lightly with a spoon.

name: Watermelon Cheong Ade (Subak Ade)
steps: Blend 1 cup cubed fresh watermelon with the juice of 1/6 lime (about 1 teaspoon) on high until smooth.

name: Pineapple Yuzu Sparkler (Tropical Citrus)
steps: Optional: rub a lime wedge around the rim of a martini or wine glass and dip it in sea salt.
In a shaker, muddle 1 slice chopped fresh pineapple with the juice of 1/2 lime, 1/2 oz (15 g) yuzu hot sauce, 1/2 oz (15 g) agave nectar and the juice of 1/2 grapefruit.
Add 1/2 cup ice, seal and shake for about 10 seconds.
Strain into the glass and top with sparkling pineapple or grapefruit juice, or sparkling water.
Garnish with a mint leaf and serve right away.

name: Korean Cherry Cheong Ade (Cherry Sparkler)
steps: Make the cherry cheong (batch): wash 300 g cherries, remove the pits and keep only the flesh.
Put the flesh in a wide bowl, add 300 g raw sugar or sugar (1:1) and stir.
Leave at room temperature for about a day, stirring occasionally.
Move to an airtight container and age for 3 to 4 days.
For one drink, add 3 tablespoons of the cherry cheong to 300 ml sparkling water and stir well.

name: White Grape Shiso Chiller (Muscat Shiso)

name: Korean Apricot Cheong Ade (Salgood)

Put the apricot flesh in a cup and add 40 g unrefined sugar.
Mash the flesh thoroughly until the sugar dissolves (a blender is faster).
Add about 2/3 cup ice.
Slowly pour in 150 ml sparkling water so it does not foam over, stir and drink.

name: Kumquat Honey Sparkler (Geumgyul)
steps: Make the syrup (batch): combine 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes, stirring until dissolved.

name: Blueberry Lavender Cheong Ade (Floral Berry)
steps: Steep 1 Blueberry Lavender tea bag in 8 oz (240 ml) boiling water in a mug for 5 minutes, then discard the bag.

name: Korean Plum Lemon Grass Chiller (Plum Grass)

name: Green Apple Mint Green Tea Spritz (Crisp Green)

name: Korean Peach Lemonade Sparkler (Peach Citrus)
steps: Cook 3/4 peach, 3/4 pear and 1 1/4 apricots (chopped) with sugar to taste and 60 ml water over medium heat for about 5 minutes until soft.

name: Korean Plum Ginger Spritzer (Plum Zest)

name: Jeju Tangerine Thyme Chiller (Citrus Herb)

steps: Peel and chop 1 ripe Fuyu persimmon (stem removed) and purée it in a small food processor until very smooth.
Fill a rocks glass with ice and add the persimmon purée, 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice and 1/2 teaspoon grated fresh ginger. Stir gently.
Sweeten with honey to taste.
Add a strip of lime zest and top with carbonated water.

name: Blackberry Yuzu Sparkler (Berry Citrus)
steps: Combine about 24 ml (1/10 cup) blackberry purée and 12 ml (about 2 1/2 tsp) yuzu juice in a bowl or glass.
Pour in about 84 ml (1/3 cup) sparkling water and stir gently to blend.
Serve over ice.

name: Japanese Kyoho Grape Shiso Soda (Grape Herb)
steps: Muddle shiso leaves with grape syrup over ice, fill with effervescent sparkling soda water
Deep purple sip

name: Korean Green Plum Coconut Fizz (Plum Coconut)
steps: Combine green plum syrup and coconut water over ice, top off with carbonated soda water
Hydrating tangy drink

name: Korean Strawberry Ginger Sparkler (Strawberry Zest)
steps: Make the syrup (batch): put 1 pack bashed lemongrass stems, a large thumb-sized piece of thinly sliced root ginger, 150 g caster sugar and 250 ml water in a small pan. Heat gently until the sugar dissolves, then simmer briskly 5 minutes.
Cool to room temperature, stir in the juice of 1 lime and chill, ideally overnight.
Fill a tall glass with ice and add 1 to 2 finely sliced strawberries.
Add 1/2 tablespoon of the syrup.
For the alcohol-free version the page suggests, top with soda water instead of prosecco, stir briefly and garnish with a mint sprig.
verified_note: Page drink uses prosecco; it says the syrup can be diluted with soda water alone for non-drinkers, so prosecco is replaced by soda water (amount not given; 240 ml placeholder). Lemongrass-ginger-lime syrup mapped to ginger_syrup.

name: Korean Pear Cinnamon Spritzer (Pear Cinnamon)
steps: Make the spiced pear syrup (batch): in a small saucepan combine 1 cup pear juice, 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 whole cloves and two 1-inch pieces of sliced fresh ginger.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then cook 10 to 15 minutes.
Cool, then strain out the spices. Keeps up to 2 weeks in an airtight container.
For one drink, combine 1 oz (30 ml) spiced pear syrup, 1/2 oz (15 ml) lime juice and 1 1/2 oz (45 ml) pear nectar in a shaker or right in the glass.
Strain into a champagne flute (over ice) and top with 4 to 6 oz ginger beer. Stir.
garnish: rosemary or mint sprig; pear slice and cinnamon stick

name: Citrus Flower Honey Spritz (Floral Honey)
steps: Make honey syrup: microwave 2 oz water with 1 oz honey about 30 seconds until dissolved (or warm in a small pot), stir and cool.
Optional sugared rosemary: dip a rosemary sprig in honey syrup, shake off the excess, toss in 1 tsp granulated sugar and leave about 45 minutes.
Shake 2 oz (60 ml) alcohol-free gin, 1 oz (30 ml) fresh lemon juice, 1 oz (30 ml) honey syrup and 2 to 3 ice cubes vigorously for about 20 seconds.
Strain into a chilled stem glass and top with club soda.
Garnish with lemon peel and the sugared rosemary sprig.
garnish: lemon peel and sugared rosemary sprig
verified_note: 1 oz honey syrup (2:1 water:honey) given as honey:10 + water:20. Club soda amount not given (90 ml placeholder). No edible flowers on the page. Not included: alcohol-free gin 60ml

name: Matcha Vanilla Gelato Cream Soda (Green Float)
steps: Bring 1/3 cup water and 1/4 cup sugar to a boil, lower the heat and simmer 5 minutes, then take off the heat.
Sift 2 teaspoons matcha into the hot syrup, stir and let it cool.
Pour the cooled matcha syrup into a tall glass and add 1/4 cup seltzer.
Add 2 scoops vanilla ice cream and top with more seltzer (half a can in total).
Stir with a spoon or straw to blend.
verified_note: Sugar mapped to simple_syrup; half a can of seltzer taken as about 180 ml; ice cream scoops as pcs.

name: Korean Mango Cheong Cream Float (Tropical Float)
steps: Mix 1 cup mango nectar with 1/4 cup club soda.
Put 2 scoops vanilla ice cream in a glass.
Pour the mango soda over the ice cream and serve immediately.
garnish: optional whipped cream, toasted coconut or diced mango
